At least 124 land and environmental defenders were killed around the world last year, with Latin America accounting for 85% of the deaths as conflicts over land and natural resources continued to put Indigenous people and small-scale farmers at risk, according to a report released Wednesday.

The annual report by environmental and human rights advocacy group Global Witness documented 105 killings in Latin America in 2025. Colombia was the deadliest country for the fourth consecutive year, with 39 killings, followed by Brazil with 26. Honduras and the Philippines recorded 12 each.

Land and environmental defenders are people who work to protect their land, natural resources and communities from threats such as mining, logging, agribusiness and other development, often by documenting environmental damage, organizing communities or patrolling territory.

Among those killed was Vicente Fernandes Vilhalva, a 36-year-old member of Brazil’s Guarani Kaiowa Indigenous people who was shot during an armed attack on his community in Mato Grosso do Sul in November. His community has been involved in a long-running struggle to reclaim ancestral territory.

Together, Colombia and Brazil accounted for 52% of all killings documented globally.

The worldwide toll fell for a second consecutive year, but the report cautioned that the decline does not necessarily mean environmental defenders are becoming safer. The group says killings remain significantly underreported, while land disputes, organized crime and competition over resources are increasingly converging in regions where communities are trying to protect forests, rivers and ancestral territories.

The group documented 142 killings and four disappearances in 2024 and 196 killings in 2023. At the country level, however, the trends varied sharply.

Killings fell in Colombia from 48 in 2024 to 39 last year and in Mexico from 19 to 10. In Brazil, they more than doubled from 12 to 26, while Honduras also recorded twice as many killings, with 12.

The report documented 2,375 killings and disappearances of land and environmental defenders since the organization began tracking them in 2012, one of the few efforts to systematically compile such cases worldwide. Global Witness works with more than 30 organizations in over 20 countries and checks cases against sources including media reports and judicial records.

Indigenous people and farmers bear the brunt

More than three-quarters of those killed in 2025 were Indigenous people, small-scale farmers or Afro-descendants, according to the report. Forty-seven victims were small-scale farmers and 44 were Indigenous. Seven of the Indigenous victims were members of community guard systems established to protect their territories.

Land disputes were linked to 84 killings, more than half the global total. Mining and extractive industries were associated with 11 deaths, logging with eight and agribusiness with six.

Organized crime and hitmen were suspected of involvement in more than a third of killings, according to Global Witness, reflecting what it described as an increasing overlap between criminal activity and the exploitation of land and natural resources.

Almost half of the 39 defenders killed in Colombia were Indigenous and another 15 were small-scale farmers. Thirty-five deaths were linked to land conflicts. The advocacy group identified suspected links to organized crime in 17 killings and another five to contract killers.

Thirteen of the killings happened in the southwestern department of Cauca, including four members of Indigenous Guard, community-led groups that patrol and protect Indigenous territories. The report documented 171 defender killings in Cauca since 2012, more than in any other Colombian department.

Astrid Torres, coordinator of the Colombian advocacy group Somos Defensores, said Indigenous authorities can come into conflict with armed groups seeking to control territory for drug trafficking and other illicit activities.

“They want to impose their order against the interests of the communities and their own authorities,” Torres said.

The region’s location near the Ecuadorian border and Pacific trafficking routes has made it strategic for armed groups involved in the cocaine trade.

Brazil sees a sharp increase in killings

The 26 killings documented in Brazil were more than double the 12 recorded a year earlier.

Eleven of those killed were small-scale farmers and seven were Indigenous. Most cases involved demands for recognition of ancestral territories or land reform, with half concentrated in the Amazon states of Rondonia and Para, where illegal logging and mining, cattle ranching and agricultural expansion have contributed to longstanding land conflicts.

The increase came despite greater Indigenous participation and commitments on land rights at last year’s COP30 climate summit in the Amazonian city of Belem. Brazil announced the titling of 10 Indigenous territories during the summit, though hundreds of applications remain pending.

Brazil’s Ministry of Indigenous Peoples told The Associated Press in a written response that reducing violence against Indigenous communities requires securing their territories, combating invasions and illegal activities and holding those responsible for crimes accountable. It said the government has resumed demarcating Indigenous lands and has carried out operations to remove outsiders from 12 territories, benefiting more than 67,000 Indigenous people.

Threats extend beyond Latin America

Killings were documented across 15 countries in 2025.

Asia accounted for 12% of the global total. The Philippines recorded 12 killings, the highest number outside Latin America, and the report said five involved suspected participation by the military amid counterinsurgency operations. Killings were also documented in India, Indonesia, Turkey, Guatemala, Ecuador, Nicaragua and France.

In Africa, three killings were verified — two in Tanzania and one in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The report cautioned that armed conflict, restrictions on civil society and insecurity make attacks especially difficult to document there.

In Congo, journalist Fiston Wilondja Mazambi was found dead in Bukavu after investigating alleged illegal gold mining by the Rwanda-backed M23 rebel group. Global Witness has recorded 79 killings of defenders in Congo since 2012, the highest total it has documented in Africa.

The report also focuses on community-led protection strategies being adopted as Indigenous groups respond to threats that governments have often failed to contain. They include territorial patrols, early warning systems and community monitoring networks.

In Peru, where four defenders were killed last year, the report highlights the Kakataibo Indigenous Guard, whose members patrol Amazonian territory threatened by illegal coca cultivation and organized crime.

“Defending our territory is important to us as a community and as a people, and we’re proud to support the climate that we all depend on,” Segundo Ispón, commander of the Kakataibo Indigenous Guard, said in a statement. “But for this next generation coming up, the work is more dangerous than ever.” ___

The Associated Press’ climate and environmental coverage receives financial support from multiple private foundations. AP is solely responsible for all content. Find AP’s standards for working with philanthropies, a list of supporters and funded coverage areas at AP.org.

More than 1,500 workers across the UK are resigning every day to care for a loved one, a charity has estimated, describing the situation as "deeply worrying".

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has previously stated that caring for a relative without adequate support can and does "break people".

According to Carers UK, polling indicates that the proportion of people forced to leave work to care for someone has risen slightly since pre-pandemic levels, with more individuals also juggling employment alongside their care responsibilities.

Its survey found one in five (20%) workers were having to manage their jobs alongside being an unpaid carer, up from 15% in 2019.

While 5% of respondents in 2019 said they had given up their job completely to care for a family member or friend who is older, disabled or seriously ill, this stood at 6% for the latest survey.

Of those who have quit their jobs to care, a third (34%) had done so in the previous two years, up from 18% in 2019.

Around 2% of the 4,000 UK adults surveyed online in July by Opinium for the charity, said they had given up work to care in the past two years – a rise from 0.9% in 2019.

Carers UK said one in five UK adults providing unpaid care equates to an estimated 11 million people and is a rise from an estimated 8.8 million people in 2019.

It said the proportion leaving work to care equates to an estimated 3.33 million people, with around 1.1 million doing so in the past two years.

open image in gallery Carers UK said one in five UK adults providing unpaid care equates to an estimated 11 million people and is a rise from an estimated 8.8 million people in 2019 ( Alamy/PA )

The charity said this equates to more than 1,500 people a day – up from around 600 a day in 2019.

The charity’s latest report said: “The direction of travel is clear: the pressures facing unpaid carers have intensified significantly in recent years, with more people reaching a point where balancing work and care is no longer sustainable.”

Carers UK has long called for a statutory right to paid leave for carers, arguing current workplace support and employment rights “do not reflect the realities of caring”.

In April 2024, a legal entitlement to unpaid leave for carers came into effect for England, Wales and Scotland.

Since then, employees who are carers for a dependant have been entitled to up to a week of unpaid leave every 12 months – equating to five days for most people.

A Government consultation, launched in June, proposed introducing paid carer’s leave, including asking respondents how much it should be, a new “right to return” to work for carers similar to mothers coming back after maternity leave, and new guidance for workers and employers on protections carers have in the workplace.

The Department for Business and Trade said unpaid carers feeling forced to cut their working hours, delay returning to work or quitting altogether costs the economy an estimated £37 billion a year and that new protections could result in thousands with caring responsibilities returning to work with increased flexibility and financial security.

open image in gallery Speaking in July, Mr Burnham said he could ‘certainly attest from family experience that it’s too hard for the family carers’ ( Jack Taylor/PA )

Emily Holzhausen, director of policy and public affairs at Carers UK, said: “It is deeply worrying to see growing numbers of unpaid carers leaving employment.

“These figures represent real people who have had to make difficult decisions about their careers, their financial security and their futures due to the pressures of balancing work and care.

“The sizeable impact of caring responsibilities on peoples’ working lives should concern us all, because when people are forced to leave work to care employers lose valuable skills and there are wider implications. The economic cost of carers leaving paid work is estimated to be £37 billion a year.

“The positive news is that employer-led initiatives can make a real difference and the government’s review of employment rights for unpaid carers is an important opportunity to ensure better support is available for all working carers.

“Introducing paid Carer’s Leave would provide time away from work without a loss of income.”

Addressing the issue of social care previously during a visit to a care home in the summer, Mr Burnham, whose father had Alzheimer’s and whose death was announced on Monday, directly referenced the struggle so many family carers face.

Speaking in July, the PM said he could “certainly attest from family experience that it’s too hard for the family carers”.

He added: “It can break people if they’re left without the support that they need.

“In fact, it does break people, and that needs to be recognised.”

A series of social media ads for AI apps have been banned for promoting the creation of sexually explicit content and objectifying women.

The first ad, for tyan.ai, presented a female character as someone users could “customise” and instruct, alongside sexualised imagery, the Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) said.

The ad also portrayed someone who appeared to be under 18 in a sexual way.

Two ads for the AI portrait generation tool Nexaipic encouraged users to upload photographs of women, including their “crush”, to create “seductive” sexually explicit videos for the user’s sexual gratification.

An ad for AI image-to-video generation app KH31 DD22 showed a photograph of a clothed woman being transformed into an image of her topless, giving the impression that the app could be used to create content that exposed women’s bodies.

The watchdog found an ad for image generator tool Rusto AI encouraged users to create sexualised videos from photographs, and condoned the digital manipulation of women’s images to create sexually explicit content without their consent.

An ad for AI image-to-video generation app PictoPop used sexualised imagery to demonstrate the tool, including a woman being placed in a subordinate position, the ASA said.

In all five cases, the ASA found the ads were irresponsible and likely to cause serious or widespread offence by objectifying and sexualising women, including through harmful gender stereotypes.

It found many of the ads also actively promoted the creation of sexually explicit content using women’s images without their consent, adding: “There is no place for this type of content in advertising and we will take firm action against ads that promote it.”

The ASA found the ads with its own AI-powered, active ad monitoring system.

While the ASA’s investigations were taking place, the law changed to make the supply of AI “nudification” apps a criminal offence.

ASA regulatory projects manager Nicky Baker said: “We take a firm line on ads that are likely to cause serious or widespread offence and these ads are a clear example of why that matters.

“Encouraging and condoning the objectification of women and the creation of explicit content from people’s images has the potential to cause real-world harm.

“That’s why we’ve taken proactive action through these rulings and why we have a zero-tolerance approach where we see ads like these.”

Young people across the UK face major regional disparities in finding work, new research has found, as the worst areas to be not in education, training or employment (Neet) are revealed.

Some places have just one vacancy for every 22 young people, the findings from the IPPR show.

The think tank warned that the crisis over the high number of young Neets cannot be solved without creating opportunities in the places that lack them.

The number of young considered Neet currently hovers around the one million mark, recording a slight fall between April and June from 1.01 million to 981,000.

Rotheram in South Yorkshire was found to be the local authority with the fewest suitable vacancies, at just 46 for every 1,000 young people – 58 per cent below the UK average.

This was followed by East Renfrewshire in Scotland (53 per cent below), Broxtowe in the East Midlands (47 per cent), and Newcastle-Under-Lyme in the West Midlands (47 per cent).

Of the 20 areas with the lowest number of suitable vacancies per young adult, the East and West Midlands had the most with four each. This was followed by the East of England, Scotland, and Yorkshire, with no southern regions appearing this low.

Meanwhile, 14 of the 20 with the highest number of suitable vacancies were found to be in southern regions. The highest was the Cotswolds, at 165 per cent per cent above the national average, followed by Woking (151 per cent above), Gloucester (139 per cent), Tonbridge (137 per cent), and Horsham (129 per cent).

Commenting on the findings, former employment minister Lord Jim Knight said that it “dispels the myth that nearly a million young people are out of work because they lack aspiration”.

“Young people in Rotherham are not six times less talented than those in the Cotswolds; they face six times fewer suitable vacancies.

“Leaving young people in certain regions with the fewest opportunities on the economic scrapheap would be both a moral tragedy and far more costly in the long run.”

Speaking before becoming PM, Andy Burnham said he would deliver “good growth in every postcode” in the role. In the first few months of his premiership, he introduced education reforms which he said were designed for the country to value “the hard hat as much as the graduation cap”.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham (PA) ( PA Wire )

In light of its findings, the IPPR has called on the government to create a targeted job creation scheme, delivering government-funded entry-level jobs to the places with the highest Neet rates.

It also argues that there has been a “major failure” to use apprenticeships consistently as a route into skilled work, calling for more opportunities which are easier to access.

The government has indicated that it will take further action to tackle the UK’s Neet crisis following the publication of a review into youth unemployment by Alan Milburn later this year.

Delivering his interim report earlier this year, the former Labour health minister said that young people were being “abandoned” to a life on welfare. The current system presents a “perverse choice” his report found, with those on health benefits able to find a “higher income, less hassle and lower risk” than if they took up work.

Reacting to his comments, several charities and campaigners have urged the government not to pursue changes to the welfare system which would see health benefits cut only for young claimants.

Looking at welfare, the IPPR report calls for changes to universal credit which would establish a single rate for young people regardless of their work capability, with new protections for certain disabled claimants. They add that young people should also be able to retain their allowance whilst undertaking education or training.

A Government spokesperson said: "Where you're from should never determine where you end up in life.

“The Milburn Review will lay the foundation for further youth employment reform, but thanks to our £2.5 billion investment we are already taking action, including reprioritising apprenticeships for young people and rolling out youth hubs to every community, helping us create one million work and training opportunities.

“We are also supporting businesses to back young talent by offering hiring incentives worth up to £8,000 and continuing the National Insurance exemptions for under 21s and apprentices under 25.”

Modern slavery victims are being "exploited in plain sight" across the UK retail sector, filling supermarket shelves and staffing convenience store checkouts, a new report warns.

Analysis from anti-slavery charity Unseen reveals that reported instances within the retail industry nearly doubled between 2024 and 2025.

Human rights are being compromised to protect profit margins and personal incomes in a sector facing headwinds such as the growing popularity of online shopping, the organisation said.

Modern slavery covers human trafficking, servitude, forced or compulsory labour, and slavery.

Unseen’s helpline identified 201 prospective modern slavery victims in retail during 2025, up from 100 a year prior and marking a steep increase from just one report in 2021.

While skilled worker visas for this sector are reserved for managers and directors, Unseen said “many migrant workers are being brought to the UK to be exploited in entry level roles that are commonplace in the retail sector”.

open image in gallery Human rights have been compromised in order to maintain or boost profit margins, Unseen said ( Getty Images )

The charity said recent changes announced to cut ties between victims and exploitative employers under the visa “helps after exploitation has happened but does not prevent it”.

Sri Lankan was the most common nationality among potential victims between January 2025 and June this year, where someone’s nationality was known, following by Indian then Pakistani, according to the charity’s report.

The sector was the fifth most common industry for modern slavery cases reported to the helpline in 2025, behind the care sector, hospitality, construction and services.

Unseen said most of the modern slavery cases reported in the retail sector where the type of business was known involved supermarkets (69%) and convenience stores (76%).

Many potential victims told of having wages withheld, living in accommodation tied to their employment and threatened with having their visa revoked or being reported to immigration authorities or the police.

The report, published on Wednesday, said “significant challenges” including “changes in consumer behaviour and the boom in online shopping”, impacts of the pandemic, cost of living crisis and inflation “have created an environment where human rights have been compromised to maintain or increase profit margins and personal income”.

It added: “Whilst understanding around exploitation in global manufacturing supply chains exists, there is little awareness that modern slavery is taking place on high streets and corner shops in neighbourhoods across the UK.”

open image in gallery Victims of modern slavery on skilled worker visas will also have the freedom to leave abusive workplaces without losing their immigration status, the Home Office said ( Alamy/PA )

Justine Carter, deputy chief executive at Unseen, said: “Modern slavery is often described as hidden, but in retail it is happening in places many of us visit every day. Behind the counter, people are being exploited in plain sight.

“In addition to the human suffering and human rights violations, failing to tackle the exploitation of foreign nationals also poses a significant risk to the UK retail sector itself.”

She said Government, enforcement bodies and the retail sector “must work together to close the loopholes that allow exploitation to happen and ensure that workers understand their rights before they arrive in the UK”.

Revised rules, which will take effect from October 8, mean that if someone is formally recognised as a victim of modern slavery, the restriction tying them to a specific sponsor will be lifted and they can take another job for the rest of their skilled worker visa without affecting their immigration status.

The restriction will only be lifted at the point the person is given what is known as a conclusive grounds decision through the Government’s national referral mechanism (NRM).

To access support and have recognition of their circumstances in the UK, victims of slavery and human trafficking have to be assessed under the NRM.

While the restriction will automatically be removed for those who have a conclusive grounds decision on or after October 8, it is understood people deemed to be victims of modern slavery before that date but who have time left on their visa will be able to apply to UK Visas and Immigration to have theirs lifted.

Unseen warned that the change “helps after exploitation has happened but does not prevent it” and that any tightening of access to support through the NRM could undermine the effectiveness of the change.

A Home Office spokesperson said: “Since the election, we have stripped more than 6,600 rogue sponsors of their licences to exploit overseas workers.

“Victims of modern slavery on skilled worker visas will also have the freedom to leave abusive workplaces without losing their immigration status, and we have created the Fair Work Agency to enable a consistent response to labour exploitation.

“We continue to work with brave survivors of modern slavery and have taken immediate action to reduce the backlog of cases, ensuring victims get swift decisions and the support they need to rebuild their lives.”

News.title: Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town
News.content:
At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

News.title: Spurs finally score... but still lose after Szoboszlai seals Liverpool’s win
News.content:
“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

News.title: England cruise to victory led by ‘absolute freak’ Brook
News.content:
As Brendon McCullum watched from the England balcony with the newest member of his think tank, Kevin Pietersen, their captain Harry Brook put on a brutal display that married the best of those two great T20 batsmen. To McCullum’s pure aggression and power, Brook added Pietersen’s flair and sheer range of strokes.

Brook made 114 from 49 balls, his second ton in T20 internationals and his first in any format this summer, as his team continues to take shape. They smashed 254 for four from their 20 overs, setting up a win by 119 runs. Under Brook, England have now won 19 of their 22 completed T20s.

Brook said he and Pietersen have had a “couple of conversations”. But in the idle hours before this match, “I was actually watching his highlights earlier on my phone”. He added that Pietersen “was a phenomenal player”; his influence on his batting is clear, and will only grow now they are working together.

It proved the perfect warm-up. This was the second time he and his predecessor Jos Buttler have wrought utter carnage on this ground this summer. Against India in July, they racked up 257 for three, with that pair sharing 233. Then, Buttler made a big hundred, with Brook finishing 95 not out, having been starved of the strike. This time, Buttler made 80 as they put on only 128 from 60 balls, and they fell just short of the team score from July, but it was still their fourth highest ever. Brook, meanwhile, made sure he got to three figures, reflecting ruefully afterwards that he had “let myself down a couple of times” this summer, letting opportunities for big scores go.

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit 19-year high as global bond rout intensifies
News.content:
The cost of UK government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007 in a fresh global debt sell-off.

The yield on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, rose from 5.37pc to a fresh 19-year high of 5.41pc on Tuesday as rising oil prices risk reigniting inflation.

Mortgage experts have warned that residential and buy-to-let mortgage rates are set to climb towards 5pc, as market turmoil threatens to filter through to household finances.

Short-term debt costs have also jumped, with the yield on two-year UK bonds surpassing 4.9pc for the first time in three years.

The bond chaos came as Andy Haldane, a former Bank of England chief economist, warned that Labour risked becoming “just a traditional tax and spend socialist government with better TikTok videos”.

He told LBC that John Healey’s original plan for a “low drama budget” had been “torpedoed” by higher borrowing costs and “events over the last couple of weeks”.

He said: “I think that [the bond market turmoil] will mean some hard choices next month at the Budget.”

“Few hard choices so far, but one is looming on the horizon, how any hole to the budget headroom is made good on. Is that a question of tax rises, or is it a question of taking the knife to public spending.”

Mr Haldane has been advising Labour since Andy Burnham took power.

It comes as the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England face pressure to raise interest rates this week to combat rising prices.

Anthony Brinkman, a portfolio manager at Principal Asset Management, said: “The recent gilt market movements seem to be intent on showing central banks they are out of time – the market is expecting action.”

Borrowing costs around the world are rising after a 20pc surge in oil prices so far this month.

Brent crude tipped above $109 a barrel this week after Houthi rebels in Yemen, considered a proxy for Iran’s forces, seized control of a key port in the Red Sea, threatening shipping.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates on Wednesday in the face of the inflation threat.

As a result, the yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds has surged above 5pc for the first time since 2007.

News.title: AI could transform global inequalities or ‘widen the gap’, warns Bill Gates
News.content:
“AI could be a great equaliser, or [it could] widen the gap”, says Mr Gates. “This is not a long-range prediction. It’s a present-tense choice”.

“We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident. After all, the market is an extraordinary engine of innovation, but a terrible guarantor of equal opportunity.

“With AI, the gap could grow even faster … That is what makes this moment so urgent. Things are changing rapidly, and the window to shape who benefits from AI, and how soon, is short”.

The key issue holding back the deployment of AI in the developing world revolves around the availability of local data and, in turn, the ability for the technology to scale in environments very different from where it is currently being created.

An app that is trained on billions of hours of American English, will struggle at first with British English (see your spell check) but is next to useless if your local language is Swahili or Chichewa.

More profoundly, an AI tool that allows a farmer in Hampshire to control his combine harvester remotely, will offer little to a smallholder in South Sudan who works the land by hand and faces a completely different array of pests, weather conditions and costs.

The same is true for health. “A community health worker in Rwanda examining a baby with a fever faces different questions than a clinician in a well-resourced hospital - and the AI supporting her needs to reflect that”, says Mr Gates.

He adds: “Most of the world is invisible to today’s AI models. These AI systems were trained primarily on what exists on the internet – and the internet reflects a deeply unequal world. More than 90 percent of the data used to train early, large language models came from English-language sources. The communities that stand the most to gain from AI are largely absent from the knowledge base these tools are built on. They are not just underserved. They are not in the picture at all”.

The new investment aims to help correct that. Mark Suzman, CEO of the Gates Foundation, says investments are already being made with companies including Microsoft and Google to build databases of a much wider range of languages, for instance.

Africa alone has more than 2,000 languages, and for AI’s to be effective there they have to understand what and how people actually speak - “their dialects, accents, and slang, too”.

The investments, he says, are being made on the condition that the intelligence and knowledge they accumulate are made freely available for others to use.

Languages for AI “are true public goods, almost definitional public goods. They need to be freely available to everybody. Once they’re created, they are public goods that can be uploaded onto any AI,” said Mr Suzman.

News.title: Reynolds refuses four times to rule out tax raid on state pensioners
News.content:
The Business Secretary refused four times to rule out retirees paying tax on the state pension from next year.

Jonathan Reynolds declined to reassure pensioners that they would not pay income tax on the benefit for the first time, saying it was a question for the Chancellor.

The comments on Tuesday raised concern for millions of retired people expecting to see their state pension surpass £13,000 from April, forcing them to pay income tax.

However, pensions minister Torsten Bell later insisted Labour would not put up taxes on people who rely on the state pension.

It is still unclear how this will be implemented given the complexity of separating the tax arrangements of different groups of pensioners.

The rise under the triple lock guarantee would drag many pensioners into paying income tax for the first time because their state income would surpass the personal allowance of £12,570.

Rachel Reeves, the former chancellor, said last year that people solely reliant on the state pension would not have to pay the tax.

However, Mr Reynolds was repeatedly asked on BBC Breakfast whether Labour would honour this commitment after the next increase in the state pension in April. He declined to answer four times.

He said: “I’m sorry, that is for the Chancellor and for a Budget.

“The majority of pensioners in this country don’t just rely on the state pensions. Some do, I accept that, but the majority don’t.

“Sometimes when this is looked at, we’re focusing just on the state pension side of this. You’ve got to consider the full range of income retired people in the UK have.”

However Mr Bell, the pensions minister, walked back from Mr Reynolds comments.

He said: “In line with the commitment made at Budget 2025, pensioners who only just exceed the personal allowance will not have the administrative burden of paying small amounts of tax in this Parliament.

“The Chancellor will set out further details on how that commitment will be delivered at the Budget.”

Former pensions minister Sir Steve Webb said only one in 16 pensioners would benefit from this policy.

He said: “Those on the new state pension can expect to see an increase of nearly £500 per year next April.

“But the sting in the tail is that this will take the standard rate of the new state pension above the tax threshold.”

The comments came after official figures on Tuesday indicated the triple lock will rise by 3.9pc from April.

Under the triple lock, the state pension rises each April in line with inflation, average wages or 2.5pc, whichever is highest.

Total pay, including bonuses, rose by 3.9pc in the three months to July, down from 4.2pc in the three months to June.

Pensioners may yet receive a bigger increase if September’s inflation figure is higher than 3.9pc. That will be revealed next month but a higher figure is thought to be unlikely.

News.title: Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon
News.content:
The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Sports.title: Liverpool beat Tottenham after stunning Dominik Szoboszlai strike - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Liverpool booked their place in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup as they survived a late onslaught to beat Tottenham 3-1 and pile more misery on the visitors at Anfield.

Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo had Liverpool in complete control, before Conor Gallagher had Spurs back in the game in the latter stages. But with seconds left, Dominik Szoboszlai scored one of the goals of the season to put them out of sight.

Spurs and Liverpool both had early chances, but Lucas Bergvall was denied by Giorgi Mamardashvili, shortly before Martin Dubravka stopped Lewis Koumas’ efforts. But Mac Allister gave Dubravka no chance in the 21st minute when he fired into the top corner to open the scoring in brilliant fashion.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Roberto De Zerbi's side were made to pay the price for missed chances in the second half when Gakpo lashed in a second shortly after the break. It then looked as if it would be a procession for Liverpool, but Gallagher's header shortly before the 70th minute set up a grandstand finish.

Spurs pushed and pushed for equaliser and were only denied by a stunning Mamardashvili save as the clock ticked down. But any hopes of forcing a penalty shootout were extinguished when Szoboszlai unleashed a ferocious volley from 30 yards to settle the point.

Here are the talking points from Anfield...

‌



WALKING THE WALK

After going public with his ‘sadness’ about not being offered a new contract, Mac Allister knew his performances would immediately be under scrutiny.

Just a day after that very open press conference, the Argentine scored against Atletico Madrid. And as one of the experienced members of a much-changed XI, he provided a moment of real quality to break the deadlock.

View 5 Images Alexis Mac Allister celebrates after opening the scoring for Liverpool vs Tottenham

His season won’t be judged on performances in the early round of the Carabao Cup, but after a difficult 25/26, the early signs are that under Iraola, Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover his form.

‌



Gakpo in the groove

Make that two goals and three assists in five games this season for Gakpo. The fact that just two weeks ago, there was a chance the Dutchman was leaving Anfield now seems difficult to imagine.

Virgil van Dijk made it clear how important his compatriot was to the squad and Anfield bosses should be thanking their lucky stars a deal didn't materialise.

But if transfer speculation was needed to take his game up to the next level, then in the long term it's good news for everyone concerned. He has been one of the standout performers of the early weeks of the season.

View 5 Images Cody Gakpo scored his second goal of the season in the win over Spurs

‌



ALL CHANGE

We all know the Carabao Cup is bottom of Liverpool and Tottenham’s list of priorities this season. But that didn’t make the team selections any less disappointing.

Liverpool need to build some momentum under new boss Iraola, after winning just one of their four league games under the Spaniard. But he decided to make 10 changes to his line-up, despite having until Sunday afternoon to prepare for Bournemouth.

It was a similar story for Tottenham, who made eight changes. If Liverpool wanted to build some momentum, Tottenham just needed a result of any type. And Spurs don’t have European football to contend with.

View 5 Images Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi opted to make eight changes

‌



I’m aware this is all a bit ‘old man shouting at clouds’ and it did give a chance for some very talented youngsters to get minutes, but with a three-week international break on the way, could we have not seen slightly stronger XIs?

Had Tottenham gone stronger from the off, there's a fairly good chance they'd be in the hat for the next round.

NO ROOM FOR RICH!

While De Zerbi was happy to make a host of changes, one he wasn’t willing to make was bringing Richarlison in from the cold.

The Italian has made it clear that he will not play for the club again after turning down a new contract offer in the summer.

‌



View 5 Images Richarlison will not play for Tottenham again according to De Zerbi (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Richarlison was close to leaving in the summer, but is now set to be a glorified spectator until January.

De Zerbi stuck to his word, but there must have been a slight temptation. In six games against Liverpool as a Tottenham player, he has four goals. That kind of firepower would have been handy tonight at Anfield.

Encouraging signs

I know. Spurs fans won't want to hear this. And at the end of the day, this is another defeat - their third in six games, but in the first half particularly, there were reasons for optimism.

‌



On another day Tottenham went in at the break leading, but Bergvall and Kudus both failed to take excellent chances. Scoring a goal - their first against Premier League opposition all season is another huge positive that De Zerbi has to build on quickly.

On Saturday, they host struggling Aston Villa, where they will hope another positive performance can get their first win of the top-flight campaign.

Sports.title: Max Dowman dazzles for Arsenal in rampant win over Ipswich - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Max Dowman scored twice as Arsenal cruised through to the fourth round of the Carabao Cup with a comfortable 4-2 victory over Ipswich.

The Gunners wonderkid produced two classy goals to sandwich Noni Madueke's strike before Mikel Merino put the icing on the cake prior to a couple of consolation goals from the hosts. It's now seven wins from seven games in all competitions for Arsenal, who are enjoying best start to a season under Mikel Arteta.

Both managers showed where their priorities are with their team selections, as Gary O'Neil made 10 changes to the side who impressively beat Crystal Palace 3-2 away from home on Saturday. Meanwhile, Arteta made nine changes after their hard-fought 2-0 win at Sunderland over the weekend.

Here are five talking points from Portman Road.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

1. Teenage kicks

On night when one of Arsenal's rivals were faced with losing their teenage sensation, Max Dowman showed why he's got a bright future with the Gunners. His goal to break the deadlock oozed confidence, taking the ball from the toe of Viktor Gyokeres and gliding into the empty space.

Dowman sent Cedric Kipre for a hot dog with a lovely shuffle of his feet before rifling the ball into the back of the Ipswich net. His second goal came just two minutes after the restart and was a more cultured finish.

‌



The 16-year-old stroked the ball home after good work from Martin Zubimendi and put the game to bed. Pre-match, Arteta warned Dowman that he'll need to earn his minutes in the first-team, and he did exactly that with a man-of-the-match performance that boosted his stock.

Should Max Dowman get an England call-up? Have your say in the comments section.

View 5 Images Max Dowman was simply outstanding (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

2. Madueke sends timely reminder

It's been slim pickings for Noni Madueke since he started the Community Shield clash with Manchester City last month. The winger only played 40 minutes of football in Arsenal's next five games, with Bukayo Saka firmly ahead of him in the pecking order.

‌



And while there was a hint of fortune about his goal, Madueke made no mistake to double the Gunners' lead on 16 minutes with an emphatic finish across Christian Walton after a defensive mix-up. Given his lack of game time, the ex-Chelsea star isn't a lock to be named in England squad which will be announced on Friday, but that strike will certainly help his case.

View 5 Images Noni Madueke made it 2-0 (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

3. Zubimendi's new role

First there was Thomas Partey, then Declan Rice and now Martin Zubimendi is Arsenal's next midfielder-turned-right-back. The Spaniard was deployed in a new-look back four after finding minutes hard to come by in his regular position so far this campaign.

With an assist to his name for Dowman's second, the experiment was looking like a success. But Jack Clarke's introduction caused problems for Zubimendi, as he skipped past him to set up Anis Mehmeti for a consolation goal.

‌



View 5 Images Martin Zubimendi started at right-back (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

4. Gyokeres continues goal drought

When Arsenal paid £64million for Viktor Gyokeres little over a year ago, these were the sort of games you'd expect him to sit out. Instead, the striker finds himself playing second fiddle to Kai Havertz and having to feed off scraps.

Gyokeres only managed one shot against a porous Ipswich defence, so no wonder he's still without a goal this season. Unlikely to start against former club Brighton on Saturday, he'll be hoping to find his shooting boots during the international break.

View 5 Images Viktor Gyokeres hasn't scored this season (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

‌



5. Cup wait goes on for Ipswich

Only making it beyond the third round once in the last 15 seasons, the Carabao Cup isn't often a source of joy for Ipswich supporters. And their wait to make another deep run akin to their semi-final exit to Arsenal in 2011 goes on after this comprehensive defeat.

The top priority for O'Neil's side is and always will be survival, of course, but a cup run could've helped inspire a more memorable campaign than when they were last in the top flight. Until they enter the FA Cup in January, it's all on the Premier League.

Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel drops immediate transfer hint after requesting shock Man Utd exit

Manchester United have been rocked by the news that JJ Gabriel wants to leave Old Trafford, with the 15-year-old wonderkid unhappy with his lack of first-team action

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel wants to leave Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United want-away JJ Gabriel has fuelled rumours over his next move by following a host of Real Madrid players on social media. Gabriel, 15, has requested to leave United in a decision which has stunned those at Old Trafford.

‌



The forward - whose full name is Joseph Junior Andreou Gabriel - is understood to have formally notified officials that he wants to cancel his registration with immediate effect and become a free agent. It remains to be seen whether United will accept his request or try and resolve the situation.

‌



Gabriel has been with the Red Devils since the age of 11 and his impressive performances at academy level have earned him comparions to both Lionel Messi and Neymar. But the wonderkid could join Messi's old rivals, Real Madrid, if he gets his wish and leaves United.

‌



The Spanish giants are keen on beating arch rivals Barcelona to the signing of Gabriel and the player's social media activity is a potential hint towards his stance. His Instagram account shows him following that of Real, their academy and La Liga as well as several members of Jose Mourinho's star-studded squad.

Those are Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior, Thibaut Courtois, Bernardo Silva, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Marc Cucurella, Ibrahima Konate, Federico Valverde, Aurelien Tchouameni, Eder Militao, Denzel Dumfries, Yan Diomande, Dean Huijsen, Arda Guler and Endrick. Gabriel also follows Real legends Cristiano Ronaldo and Zinedine Zidane.

Due to owning an Irish passport, Gabriel will be eligible to join a team in Europe when he turns 16 next month. English players, in contrast, aren't allowed to go abroad until they turn 18.

Before his request to leave shocked club staff, Gabriel was in contention to feature against Brighton in the third round of the Carabao Cup on Wednesday.

But he'll no longer be considered for a debut that would've seen him become United's youngest ever player at senior level. Carrick is on record to be a fan of Gabriel, having witnessed him score and provide two assists against Ipswich in a recent Premier League 2 fixture.

"He's obviously got a really big talent." the United manager said. "He's trained with us quite a bit and is getting experience all the time. He's physically adapting to each step that he makes, and we're just continuing his development."

Sports.title: Howard Webb points blame for Manchester derby offside controversy as Pro Ref take action
Sports.content:
Refereeing chief Howard Webb has claimed that VAR officials in Stockley Park had 'tunnel vision' before the decision to allow Erling Haaland's controversial winner in the Manchester derby.

Video assistant referee Matt Donohue and his assistant, Blake Antrobus, have both been stood down for this weekend's Premier League fixtures after wrongly letting Haaland's goal stand.

Initially flagged for offside due to Enzo Fernandez's attempt to play the ball in build-up, the decision was overturned following VAR check. Webb, as head of Pro Ref, wrote to Manchester United officials within hours of full-time to apologise for the error that played a decisive part in their 1-0 defeat to leave Michael Carrick's side on four points after four games.

Haaland's goal wasn't the only moment of drama at Old Trafford either. City star Phil Foden was sent off after kicking out at United captain Bruno Fernandes, a decision which Webb insists was correct.

‌



Appearing on Match Officials Mic'd Up, the former referee admitted: "We felt it was important that we acknowledged an error in this situation. We know that Erling Haaland, who was penalised on field for offside, wasn't in an offside position.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"But we also know that Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, almost certainly interfered with the Manchester United defence and probably the goalkeeper as well.

‌



"I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are. None more so than the officials themselves. They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they're obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation. They'll not be officiating again until after the international break. We've reached out to Manchester United and acknowledged the error, as we do when these things happen.

"They don't happen that often, but we want to ensure that we are transparent and open, and we've played the audio and the footage to the football club to let them know what happened, and we're going to review this situation to understand what elements of process fell down in this situation which meant we didn't get to the right outcome."

Should Phil Foden have been sent off? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez dived for the ball from an offside position (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Webb added that the officials back in Stockley Park got 'tunnel vision' in focusing on Haaland's part in the goal, with colleagues unable to pull him back out to look at the wider picture.

He added: "And when the VAR starts their check, they see through the use of the semi-automated offside technology, that Haaland, when he's played, is actually onside by three centimetres, played on by [Patrick] Dorgu on the far side, and the VAR gets super focused on Haaland. He establishes he's onside, he thinks that's a good goal, Haaland's not offside, as was thought initially.

"But of course, when he then runs it back through the full APP, he doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez's position. He has a look to see if he touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score. He doesn't touch the ball, but he doesn't truly evaluate other elements of offside. In that moment, he gets tunnel vision. He gets focused on Haaland, and it's down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn't happen on this occasion."

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez's role was incorrectly overlooked in the process of allowing the goal, according to Webb

‌



Webb then emphasised: "We'll review it, reflect upon it, and try to take the learning forward to prevent this unusual type of error from happening again."

City took the lead in the derby after they were reduced to 10 men. Tempers flared in the 23rd minute, as Foden reacted to a kick from Fernandes by lashing out himself.

On-field referee Michael Oliver quickly made up his mind and it was the City player who was punished. "I agree with the red card for Phil Foden for violent conduct," Webb concurred. "He kicks out with force into the upper body of Bruno Fernandes.

"We saw a player sent off for Aston Villa earlier in the season. [Joao] Gomes was sent off for a very similar thing, kicking with the studs into the body. And that's seen by the referee on the field, and that's the on-field call, a red card for Foden.

‌



"Now, when you look at the footage, there is that petulant kick by Bruno Fernandes into the backside of Foden. It is more petulant than violent.

"To be violent conduct, it has to have excessive force or brutality, and when you look at that, particularly in full speed, it doesn't have those elements. So therefore, this would be a yellow card offence. And the VAR can't step in to recommend the referee looks at the screen to give a yellow card.

"Of course, if all of this is missed and nothing is given against Foden, then the VAR could step in so the referee could see Foden's actions for a possible red card, and they would capture Fernandes' yellow card action. But because the referee gave the red card on the field, that option is not open to the VAR."

Sports.title: Dominic Calvert-Lewin is thriving at Leeds while England rivals score cheap goals in Saudi Arabia
Sports.content:
Dominic Calvert-Lewin is thriving at Leeds while England rivals score cheap goals in Saudi Arabia

The Leeds United striker has been on top form since his move from Everton and is line for an international recall when Thomas Tuchel names his latest squad

View 3 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin of Leeds United celebrates his goal to make it 3-0 vs Newcastle

Dominic Calvert-Lewin spent nine seasons in the Premier League with Everton and his most productive campaign was 2020/21 when he scored 16 goals in 33 appearances. He also scored twice in the FA Cup and three times in the EFL Cup.

‌



It was the full Covid season, played almost entirely behind closed doors. There was a theory amongst some Evertonians that Calvert-Lewin felt less pressure without the presence of a set of fans who could be highly critical.

‌



That theory seemed ill-founded. He played in nine matches behind closed doors in the restarted 2019/20 season and did not score once.

‌



And he has performed well under pressure many times in his career. But there is no doubt Calvert-Lewin can experience confidence swings.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



And he has spoken honestly and commendably about mental struggles during a career frequently interrupted by injury. Which is why it is fantastic to see Calvert-Lewin full of confidence, loving his football and looking in the form of his life.

He has now scored 16 goals in 34 Premier League appearances for Leeds United. Considering their serious striking issues - Thierno Barry being the only recognised centre-forward - some Everton fans have been lamenting that Calvert-Lewin was allowed to leave on a free transfer at the end of the 2024/25 season.

But realistically, the long-standing relationship - he was at Everton for nine seasons - had run its course and a change of scenery was best for him. And when he went to Elland Road, it was hard not to feel it would go one of two ways.

‌



View 3 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin's last appearance for England was in a friendly against Uruguay in March (Image: Getty Images)

It would be confirmation that physical setbacks had taken a long-term toll on a hugely talented player or it would restart a career that has seemed so promising. It is most definitely the latter.

Calvert-Lewin turns 30 next March but there is every chance we have not seen the best of the Sheffield-born striker. It goes without saying that is fantastic news for Leeds United - it should also be fantastic news for England.

‌



Calvert-Lewin was unlucky not to be taken to the World Cup and Thomas Tuchel, who did give him half an hour in a friendly against Uruguay early in the year, will surely include him in his next squad, which will be announced on Friday. England have four UEFA Nations League matches coming up. They host world champions Spain before travelling to the Czech Republic and Croatia and then returning to Wembley to play the Czechs again.

The Leeds forward - rightly dismayed at having a goal taken away from him after his towering header took a nick off Jayden Bogle - will surely feature in parts of those games. Calvert-Lewin has just run amok against Newcastle in the Premier League, while Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney are content with cheap goals and bumper pay deals in Saudi Arabia.

View 3 Images England are still heavily reliant on captain Harry Kane (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Tuchel’s and England’s reliance on Harry Kane remains. And will do up until and throughout Euro 2028.

But Calvert-Lewin still has time to establish himself as a serious alternative, a high-quality back-up. When he came on as a substitute against Uruguay in March, it was his first England appearance in almost five years.

Calvert-Lewin has 12 caps. In the five games he has started, he has scored four goals.

Article continues below

True, the field is thin, but when it comes to the fight to be considered as the main alternative to Kane, Calvert-Lewin should be winning it. And he has not got the confidence to shine on the grandest stages.

Sports.title: Brook, Buttler go berserk again as England thrash Sri Lanka in first T20
Sports.content:
​​Harry Brook and Jos Buttler went berserk in a T20 at Southampton for the second time this summer as England smoked 254-4 against Sri Lanka during a 119-run victory in the series opener - their first game since Kevin Pietersen's appointment as white-ball mentor.

White-ball captain Brook (114no off 49 balls) - who nailed six boundaries in one over - and predecessor in that role Buttler (80 off 44) plundered 128 from just 60 balls in partnership for England's second wicket once debutant Aneurin Donald (12 off 5) fell after slamming a six and a four amid a bright but fleeting cameo.

Brook and Buttler had combined for a riotous stand of 233 from 103 balls at the same venue in July as England romped to a total of 257-3 against India that secured a 4-0 series sweep, with Buttler tonking a century on that occasion and Brook an unbeaten 95.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The best of Brook's sensational 114 not out from just 49 balls in the first T20I against Sri Lanka in Southampton

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brook slammed 30 runs off one over with six successive boundaries off Sri Lanka spinner Dunith Wellalage

Score summary - England vs Sri Lanka, first T20, Southampton England 254-4 in 20 overs (put in to bat): Harry Brook (114no off 49 balls), Jos Buttler (80 off 44), Will Jacks (21 off 12); Wanindu Hasaranga (1-34) Sri Lanka 135 all out in 19 overs (target 255): Dunith Wellelage (33 off 21 balls), Dasun Shanaka (24 off 14), Eshan Malinga (13no off 5); Sonny Baker (3-12), Jamie Overton (2-20), Liam Dawson (2-23) , Will Jacks (1-21) Full scorecard Watch Thursday's second T20 in Cardiff live on Sky Sports Cricket and Sky Sports Main Event from 6pm (6.30pm first ball).

This time around the roles were reversed with Buttler - playing his first innings since the Hundred final at Lord's on August 16 - missing out on a ton but Brook reaching three figures for the second time in T20 internationals, doing so from just 42 deliveries.

No wonder England legend Pietersen, who scored almost 14,000 runs in all international cricket between 2004 and 2014, was smiling throughout in the dugout.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking ahead of the first T20, Sky Sports' Eoin Morgan and Kumar Sangakkara looked at what white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen will bring to the set-up

That expression continued as Sri Lanka subsided to 135 all out in 19 overs in reply, to suffer a 13th successive defeat to their opponents in this format, stretching back to 2014, and England made it 21 wins from their last 24 T20Is.

The pacey, accurate and economical Sonny Baker bagged 3-12 from four overs, including bowling Kamil Mishara (10) to claim his first white-ball wicket for England, while leg-spin maestro Adil Rashid (1-31) nicked off Dasun Shanaka (24 off 14) with a peach of a delivery having just been belted for back-to-back sixes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Sonny Baker took his first white-ball wicket for England by bowling Sri Lanka's Kamil Mishara.

KP watches on as Brook dazzles at Utilita Bowl

Brook's innings was a joy to watch, with his expert ability to pick up length on full display in the 30-run fifth over of the game when he struck Sri Lankan left-arm spinner Dunith Wellalage for six boundaries in as many deliveries (three sixes, three fours).

Brook's first boundary in that set, a six onto the cushion at long-on, was a little edgy but his next five were sublime - fours over the bowler's head and down to long-on, a scooped six over fine leg, a maximum over long-off and, finally, a four behind point.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Sky Sports pundit Stuart Broad's failed attempt to get an interview with Brook at the halfway stage at the Utilita Bowl

Only Phil Salt - missing this series due to a quad injury, hence why Derbyshire batter Donald has been handed a chance - has hit a faster T20I hundred for England than Brook, taking 39 balls against South Africa in 2025 when the team amassed 304-2 in Manchester.

Former England Test captain Ben Stokes took to social media to say: "I don't even think the genius of KP could come close to what Brook has talent-wise. You are an absolute freak, Harry. You're mint to watch."

Stokes would later add: "Bit harsh on KP actually. Both are freak talents but Brook is better in my opinion."

Brook then rotated his bowlers smartly in the second half of the game as Sri Lanka's monumental task was made practically impossible when they started slowly and then tumbled to 69-5 inside the first 10 overs of a sorry chase, one in which Wellalage (33 off 21) top-scored, crunching four fours and two sixes.

Brook's boys - for whom seamer Jamie Overton (2-20) and spinner Liam Dawson (2-23) shared four wickets - will now hope to wrap up a series win with a game to spare in Cardiff on Thursday night (6.30pm start), ahead of the final match at Emirates Old Trafford on Saturday (2.30pm start). Welshman Donald will be looking to make a more sustained impact in the country of his birth in the second T20 - the 29-year-old came through the Glamorgan academy and is the Cardiff county's first homegrown international since 2005 Ashes hero Simon Jones.

After Donald heaved a maximum leg-side and drilled four through extra-cover next ball, he spooned Wellalage down the ground, before watching on as Brook and Buttler made mincemeat of the tourists' bowling attack - the duo spanking 28 boundaries between them.

Sports.title: Peterborough edge out Barnsley on penalties after six-goal thriller
Sports.content:
Peterborough moved into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 2009 thanks to a 7-6 penalty shootout victory over Barnsley that followed a thrilling 3-3 draw between the two League One sides.

Barnsley were gifted the lead after 61 seconds when Peterborough goalkeeper Alex Bass was charged down by Cameron McGeehan, with the Tykes captain nodding in after the ball had come off the bar.

Peterborough equalised in the 19th minute when Lucca Mendonca's cross was pushed out by Barnsley goalkeeper Kieran Flavell as far as Harry Leonard, who prodded in.

The hosts then completed the turnaround after 27 minutes when Harley Mills' free-kick was headed in by the unmarked Danny Ormerod.

But the Tykes were level five minutes before half-time when Reyes Cleary beat Mendonca with ease down the left before placing his shot into the bottom corner.

The visitors looked to have won it when Cleary bent in his second in the 74th minute, but Ormerod sent the tie to penalties by heading in Mills' cross with just two minutes remaining.

After 12 successful spot-kicks, a tame effort from Barnsley's Luke Alker was saved by Bass, giving Harrison Jones the chance to send the hosts through, which he dispatched.

Sports.title: Brentford hold off Reading to reach round four of Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
Brentford emerged from a tense finish against Reading to book their place in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 2-1 victory at Select Car Leasing Stadium.

Callum Wilson and Fabio Carvalho were on target in the first half as the Premier League club showed a clinical touch against League One opposition, who produced a number of chances but lacked the firepower to finish them off.

Paudie O'Connor eventually pulled one back to revive Reading's challenge and Brentford could not rest easy in the remaining 18 minutes, although substitute Igor Thiago was among those who should have killed the match off.

It took just 136 seconds for Brentford to take the lead with Wilson finding the bottom left corner of the net after a slip in defence by O'Connor turned Dango Ouattara's pass into an opportunity.

A cross by Carvalho caused problems in the visiting box and Reading then had the ball in the net but referee Tom Nield ruled out O'Connor's bicycle kick for a high boot.

O'Connor was doing everything possible to make up for his earlier mistake as he headed a free-kick inches over the crossbar.

Reading had clearly recovered from the shock of going behind so early as they poured forward, with a double clearance by Michael Kayode saving Brentford before Jamie Reid went desperately close.

O'Connor slipped again as he fluffed a clearance, giving Wilson time to pick his spot only for keeper Joel Pereira to get his body in the way.

Brentford scrambled to keep out Reid as he closed in on goal and then Conor Masterson flashed narrowly wide, but the Premier League club then scored on the counter-attack.

In a cruel blow for the Royals, Ouattara took advantage of the space in defence to slide the ball to Carvalho who calmly directed the ball beyond Pereira.

Ellery Balcombe's sharp reflexes prevented Josh Stokes from pulling one back for Reading but Brentford should have extended the lead only for Kayode to send a close-range effort wide.

Liam Fraser reminded the visitors they could not relax as he drilled a shot past the left post but the better chances were now coming at the other end, with Ouattara this time at fault for not making the most of a great opportunity.

Reading deserved a goal and it arrived in the 72nd minute when a corner was met by O'Connor's header, with the Irish defender's finish setting up a nervy finale.

On came Thiago but he was unable to improve the standard of finishing by his team, which had declined noticeably in the second half.

Sports.title: More talented than Pietersen? Brook brilliance leads to bold Stokes statement
Sports.content:
Ben Stokes no longer plays for England - but that has not stopped him from rating players who do or did.

Harry Brook is, in many ways, a modern-day Kevin Pietersen.

A player with jaw-dropping batting ability who can take any bowling attacking apart and make accessing any part of the ground look routine but also prone to driving fans mad with a daft dismissal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brook slammed 30 runs off one over with six successive boundaries off Sri Lanka spinner Dunith Wellalage

In Southampton on Tuesday, though, we only saw the best of Brook as he tonked a 42-ball hundred - England's second-fastest in T20Is - against Sri Lanka, with his 10 fours and half a dozen sixes including six boundaries in one over off Dunith Wellalage.

The swashbuckling innings was played in front of England legend Pietersen, who has joined head coach Brendon McCullum's white-ball set-up as a mentor, up to and including the 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe in late 2027.

And Brook's knock lured Stokes onto social media to say that, in his opinion, the Yorkshireman's ability outstrips that of Pietersen.

Brook still has a long way to go to match Pietersen longevity-wise.

KP amassed almost 14,000 international runs between 2004 and 2014, a number he was prevented from adding to after a fallout with the ECB truncated his England career.

Brook has over 6,500 international runs since debuting in 2022, so, all being well will eclipse Pietersen's haul at some stage.

At 27, he could have over a decade left.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Eoin Morgan and Kumar Sangakkara heap praise on Brook following his century in Southampton

'Genius Brook has everything as a batter'

Brook's sizzling century against Sri Lanka was his first in any international cricket since a T20 ton versus Pakistan in February, during a World Cup match in Pallekele.

It was worth the wait. The batter's picking up of length was extraordinary in an innings highly praised by Sky Sports pundits Eoin Morgan and Kumar Sangakkara.

Sangakkara said of Brook: "He reads length so quickly. He is very light and nimble on his feet. He has oodles of time and devastating power. On the back foot against spin, he is very good at hitting over long-on, long-off, even square.

"Then against the pace there is the scoop and reverse paddle or punch down the ground for six. He has everything."

Image: Kevin Pietersen (right) is now a mentor to England's white-ball teams

Morgan added: "I think Harry is one of our very best. It is difficult to find a player of recent generations that has Brook's ability.

"He is coming into his peak years, yet we are seeing absolute genius time and time again in all formats of the game."

Morgan is right about all formats, too.

Brook's last Test century may have come over a year ago, against India at The Kia Oval, but he has knuckled down in red-ball matches of late, batting far more responsibly while notching five fifties across the summer in the international game's longest form.

I feel like I've been there or thereabouts all summer, in all three formats. I feel like I've let myself down a couple of times - I've had the opportunity to score a big score. Thankfully I didn't give that opportunity up today. It was nice to get to three figures. A special feeling.

In the international game's shortest form on Tuesday night, he did get a century - and how.

He can now chat about it with KP, a bloke he may even have more talent than…
