Sports.title: Battle of boxing's most unlikeable stars: Conor Benn takes on troubled Ryan Garcia after burning Eddie Hearn with $10MILLION payday in his sights - but here's why Briton's fate rests solely in the hands of his narcissistic American rival
Sports.content:
Battle of boxing's most unlikeable stars: Conor Benn takes on troubled Ryan Garcia after burning Eddie Hearn with $10MILLION payday in his sights - but here's why Briton's fate rests solely in the hands of his narcissistic American rival

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

‘Who ya like buddy?’ It’s the most asked question in casino-ville as the hours tick down to this Saturday’s world title fight between two angry young men.

One, America’s extravagantly gifted but troubled world welterweight champion. The other, the ever-persistent English challenger who never stops throwing punches whether they connect or not. As if in manic obsession with defeating not only opponents but also his demons and a sceptical outside world.

So, Ryan Garcia or Conor Benn?

When the denizens of this neon gambling Strip in the Nevada desert ask that question they don’t’ want to know which of these two combatants you like personally more than the other. It is their way of trying to find out who you might be betting on to prevail in the atmospheric T-Mobile Arena.

Their inquiries are even more numerous than usual on such occasions as this. Because neither the Americans nor the Mexicans who are thronging here in support of their blood brother by heredity know very much about Benn. Other than the fact he is the son of a fabled icon of the British ring.

On his two previous US visits Benn Jr made hard work of beating men who looked more like nightclub bouncers than professional boxers. Of his exploits back home only the pair of fights against Chris Eubank Jr evoked any interest whatsoever on either side of this border.

What they are aware of is the two positive tests for performance enhancing drugs and the protracted legal battle to technically clear his name which kept him out of the ring for months. Just as they know about Garcia’s conviction and suspension for a similar finding.

Conor Benn is locked in the battle of boxing's most unlikeable stars in Las Vegas

Benn is lining up a $10m payday after burning his bridges with promoter Eddie Hearn

So, what’s to like?

There can be no doubting Benn’s work ethic. He trains like a dervish to manufacture the maximum possible out of however much natural-born ability he inherited from Nigel the Dark Destroyer. Nor does he ever give up. Eubank Jr had to go beyond the normal limits of even this battle-hardened business to inflict the only defeat of Conor’s career thus far. A loss he avenged, albeit in partly contrived and contentious circumstances.

Eubank the Younger was perilously drained in the rematch by a clause in the contract which prevented him rehydrating fully after struggling to cut poundage to meet the agreed catchweight.

What goes around comes around. If not in a full measure of the irony. Benn has had to sweat and strain down by almost a stone from middleweight to make the welterweight championship limit of 147 lbs. As he puts it: ‘Five weeks in hell.’

To say his body looks shredded is putting it mildly. But he has not been subjected to rehydration limitations following his Friday morning visit to the scales.

Eubank was handsomely rewarded to put his health on the line, and now Benn has been lured into similar jeopardy by the fortune – some reports say ten million dollars – he is receiving from UFC boss Dana White to be one of the first poster boys for his venture into boxing.

Benn tells it otherwise: ‘I’m doing this because I relish challenges. Have always wanted to strap on the same green WBC belt my dad was so proud to wear. To start getting the world titles that will leave a legacy for my kids. And to prove wrong everyone who doesn’t give me a chance of winning. That puts all the pressure on him, not me.’

Hearn backed the British fighter during his controversial doping ban saga

Ryan Garcia stands in his way of the WBC title, who is the more talented of the fighters

WEIGH-IN VERDICT: After all the brouhaha Conor Benn made the weight with a full pound to spare After what he described as 'five weeks of hell' dieting down by two divisions he scaled 146 lbs in readiness to challenge world welterweight champion Ryan Garcia here this Saturday night. He did so with a told-you so smile. Throughout the speculation as to whether he could shed the best part of a stone in his training camp journey from middleweight Benn had assured one and all that he would be comfortable at his long-ago weight. Good as his word he came in only half a pound heavier than Garcia. Although he is leaner of hip the muscle is still there on arms and torso. Complete with a six pack as a reminder of his constant work ethic. The slightly taller part/Mexican great white hope of American boxing does look more natural at the weight. But Benn does not appear stressed from all his exertions. Even so Garcia is still a solid odds on favourite in the Vegas betting

Whether or not Benn can take in sufficient liquids and pasta before entering the ring, the dangers to him are greater than those with which Eubank struggled. Garcia, one year the younger at 28 but the riper in championships experience, has authentic one-hit-knockout power.

Benn goes into his first world championship fight reliant on the cumulative effect of his non-stop output. The problem with this is that King Ry is probably the best counterpuncher in the world right now and Benn’s headlong style will likely suit him nicely, thank you.

To complicate the evaluation, both have blotted their copybooks as people. Garcia, the handsome heartthrob, burnished his bad-boy rock-star image by trashing a five-star hotel room. He also needed his family’s help with overcoming mental problems aggravated by a passing fancy for social drugs and booze.

Benn invited mockery for claiming initially that he failed his drugs tests because of eating enough eggs to fill the shelves of all the Tescos in London. Then, in order to collect his bonanza from Mister UFC, he unceremoniously dumped his long-time promoter Eddie Hearn who had bankrolled his hefty legal costs and loaned him half a million quid to help sustain his flamboyant lifestyle through that crisis.

Not much to like there.

So, when it comes to the fight, who ya like? The answer is not Conor Benn’s to give. Because the real question is which Ryan Garcia turns up.

If it is the narcissist whose arrogant complacency has cost him a couple of big fights, it may not be totally beyond the bounds of possibility that Conor could pull off one of the major upsets by a British boxer abroad.

If it is King Ry fully prepared and ready to unfurl all the majesty then we can only hope the son of Nigel is not seriously hurt.

Sports.title: Ricky Hatton's mother recalls last hug with boxing champion three days before he took his own life a year ago as parents speak out for first time
Sports.content:
Ricky Hatton's mother recalls last hug with boxing champion three days before he took his own life a year ago as parents speak out for first time

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ricky Hatton's mother has recalled her last hug with him three days before he took his own life one year ago as his parents speak out for the first time.

Carol and Ray Hatton have urged people to tell their friends and family they love them before it's too late after the boxing champion hanged himself on September 14 last year.

One year on from Ricky's death, aged 46, his mother has revealed the last time she embraced her son.

Just days before he took his own life, the boxing champion had been in an argument with his parents but the family were 'building bridges'.

Carol decided to make an unplanned visit to his gym in Hyde and gave him a 'real proper hug'.

She told ITV News: 'I pulled up on the car park because I saw his car. He asked if everything was okay.

'I said "yeah, everything's fine". I said I'd like to see a bit more of him.'

Ricky's mother said he told her he wanted to see his father Ray the next week. However Ricky died three days later.

Former world boxing champion Ricky Hatton died by suicide in September last year aged 46

Ray and Carol Hatton (pictured at their son's funeral) have urged people to tell their friends and family they love them before it's too late

Ricky had previously opened up about his struggle with drug and alcohol addiction and had become estranged from his parents before the reconciled

She added: 'I'm so glad (I got to see him) because nobody knows when it's the last time you're going to see somebody.'

Ray, the boxer's father, said: 'You tell your grandkids how much you love them, you tell your wife how much you love them but I think, especially with men, don't ever be afraid of getting hold of your son and telling him you love him.'

Ricky had become estranged from his parents for around a decade before he reached out to patch up their relationship several years before his death.

He had survived previous suicide attempts and struggled with drug and alcohol addiction.

Ricky fell out with his parents over money and despite the dispute he still allowed Carol and Ray to see his newborn daughter Millie.

However the boxer became upset when his girlfriend Jennifer was not invited to a Christmas Day party.

Months later he received letters from his parents' lawyers saying they wanted to see their granddaughter.

But he told Manchester Evening News in 2013 that he responded by saying: 'I replied to my parents, through solicitors, and said we did not want them to have contact with Millie.'

Carol Hatton wipes a tear from her eye while reading a statement at her home after Ricky's death

Ricky had survived previous suicide attempts before he died in September last year

'We have never stopped them seeing her, as far as I was concerned they had just not been ******.

'I know that sounds harsh and I am sure they see it differently, but it is how I feel.'

He added that the situation 'was a mess', describing the family feud as 'bitter and horrible', referring to back-and-forth letters between his and his parents' lawyers.

This culminated in his father attacking him in a car park fist fight.

Angry about 'all that stuff you've written about your mum in that solicitor's letter', Ray then punched his boxing champion son in the face before Ricky hit back and his father then drove off.

But Ricky's parents are still struggling to come to terms with his death and Carol said the couple 'have to move forward' but will continue 'remembering him and loving him'.

Carol and Ray have now called for a statue of Ricky to be erected in Manchester, saying it would be a 'fitting tribute' to their son who 'brought a lot of pride' to the city.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury looks set for CARDIFF - at 2am: Welsh venue set to waive curfew to take boxing's biggest fight away from Wembley and New York
Sports.content:
Cardiff's Principality Stadium now looks set to be the unlikely winner of the venue war for boxing's biggest fight - by hosting Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury in the early hours of the morning.

The local authorities could today approve lifting the stadium's 10.30pm curfew to host the fight - stepping in after rows over holding it at Wembley Stadium or Madison Square Garden in New York.

Cardiff has history of hosting late-night boxing. Joe Calzaghe fought Mikkel Kessler at the Principality in 2007 at 2am. Fury and Joshua could fight at a similar time to satisfy broadcaster Netflix's huge audience in the United States.

Netflix had wanted the fight in New York to suit their prime timezones, while Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn pitched Wembley to host under the guise that Britain's biggest fight of the century should be hosted in the UK - and he has refused to budge unless contracts are rewritten with upgraded financial offerings.

Cardiff now appears to be the compromise. The Principality Stadium has an 80,000 capacity and a retractable roof - unlike Wembley - which could be useful in late November or December. A date of Saturday, November 28 has been mooted.

The Times report a press conference is tentatively scheduled for next week pending the approval.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could now be set to fight in Cardiff, Wales in November

Joshua and his camp wanted the fight in the UK - while broadcasters Netflix wanted a US host

Wembley looked an ideal venue for the fight but the strict 11pm curfew has been a sticking point, despite London mayor Sadiq Khan saying he wanted to ensure allowances were made to host the fight.

Boxing dealmaker Turki Al-Sheikh has been insistent on a start time of 2am.

Netflix have been running s for Fury-Joshua as recently as Thursday night, clearly confident an agreement will be struck.

The streaming giant has yet to sign off on Cardiff but American sportswriter Dan Rafael last night reported he had asked Netflix if they would approve, with a source telling him: 'I think they're OK.'

A spokesperson for the Welsh Rugby Union said: 'We'd be delighted to host this fight.

'We are very keen to attract more boxing to the stadium, which has a rich history in the sport, enhanced by its closable roof, unrivalled sight lines and unique city-centre location.'

Joe Calzaghe trains at the Principality Stadium before his 2am fight there in 2007

Joshua has fought in Cardiff twice previously, beating Carlos Takam and Joseph Parker in the Welsh capital in 2017 and 2018.

While Joshua has left Hearn to do the talking on his side of the deal, Fury has been publicly speaking and threatening that the heavyweight contest will be called off.

This week he suggested he will no longer be fighting Joshua in another social media rant as rows over the location and contract surrounding the fight continued.

'So it looks like AJ has s*** his pants yet again,' Fury said on social media on Sunday. 'After 11 years, he's finally s*** his pants yet again.'

Last week, Fury, who regularly takes to social media to express his views on potential opponents, was keen to make clear he feels Joshua is not motivated by a love of his country. Earlier this year Daily Mail Sport revealed Joshua had in fact quit the UK to move to Dubai – even as thousands tried to flee amid rising panic in the Middle East warzone.

And Fury, a tax exile to the Isle of Man himself, brought up a 2020 speech at a Black Lives Matter march, where Joshua read out a letter from his friend Reece Campbell to urge attendees to stop spending money with white-owned shops and businesses.

'Show them where it hurts', Joshua had said. 'Abstain from spending your money in their shops and economies, and invest in black-owned businesses.'

Fury re-posted the video of the speech, writing: 'This is the man who loves England, absolute s*** bag! Total piece of s*** bully with zero guts! Don't let them deceive you! & Living in Dubai.'

Provided Cardiff hits no further stumbling blocks, the Welsh capital may now offer the solution to get the fight on at last.

Sports.title: Ferrari not yet switching focus to 2027 F1 car
Sports.content:
Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur says the Scuderia will keep developing its SF-26 Formula 1 car, despite its diminishing title chances.

After Lewis Hamilton retired from the Spanish Grand Prix with brake issues, the seven-time world champion is 101 points adrift of championship leader Kimi Antonelli in the drivers’ standings. Meanwhile, Charles Leclerc finished just fourth at Madring, meaning Ferrari is 145 points down on Mercedes in the constructors’.

Car development resources have to be carefully allocated in light of the cost cap and the aerodynamic testing restrictions; engine-wise, Ferrari has already introduced the two ADUO upgrades it has been allowed.

While teams are known to be working on their 2027 challengers, Vasseur has no intention to make that Ferrari’s full focus just yet.

“We are not in the situation of 12 months ago,” the Frenchman said, referring to F1’s regulatory overhaul for 2026. “Today, what we will develop, we will be able to carry it over on next year's project. We will continue to work, but perhaps on different things, different aspects.

“The development that we do now, 80% will be carried over.”

Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari Photo by: Jayce Illman / Getty Images

As far as Ferrari’s title chances are concerned, Vasseur was asked if it was now ‘game over’ against Antonelli and Mercedes – a question he refused to answer directly.

“Two or three weeks ago I told you that I will take race by race. I didn't change,” he insisted.

The key for Ferrari may be qualifying performance, as Hamilton and Leclerc have both failed to qualify on the front row in any of the four sessions (Zandvoort sprint included) since the summer break. Their average position is fifth, and the SF-26’s deficit to pole has been 0.198s – slower than McLaren and Mercedes, quicker than Red Bull.

“This we need to improve, because I think when you have a look on the pace, during the race the pace is there,” Vasseur said. “For sure we need to do a better job in quali.

“If you take Zandvoort and this one, the profile of the event is a little bit the same for us. We had a decent pace in quali, but we didn't put everything together on the last attempt, and race pace is OK.

“If I have to put the focus of the team on something today, it would be the evolution of the pace during the quali – more than the pace in quali, the evolution, the steps that you can do. We were there on run one Q3, the potential is there, we just have to adapt everything further on.”

Sports.title: Russell and Hamilton concede F1 2026 title chances as Antonelli dominates
Sports.content:
Strange things can happen in Formula 1. Just ask Max Verstappen, who couldn't believe his luck when McLaren handed him a way into the 2025 title fight on a silver platter. Although he eventually missed out by two points to Lando Norris, he was essentially battling with one hand behind his back in an inferior car.

But this year's fight has a distinctly different feel to it. Dominant championship leader Kimi Antonelli has shown fewer, if any, signs of weakness. Mercedes has executed race weekends at a high level - as opposed to rival Ferrari, for example - and it appears to have nixed the most pressing reliability gremlins with the power unit.

Over the European summer, Mercedes was starting to field questions over its lack of development compared to its peers, with a string of four consecutive qualifying defeats starting to make things uncomfortable for Toto Wolff as both Ferrari and McLaren made huge strides with their car.

Did Mercedes, which will only bring significant upgrades to Malaysia in two weeks, get a bit too comfortable courtesy of its early-season dominance?

"I don't think I am in the fight" - Russell

Antonelli's return to winning ways, first with an emotional and staggeringly crushing home victory in Monza and then a slightly more fortunate win in Madrid, has put those questions to bed. After 14 grands prix, Antonelli leads team-mate George Russell by 81 points, with Lewis Hamilton now falling behind triple digits (101) and Norris by 106.

It means Antonelli's biggest threat is now supposed to come from within, but while Russell has stepped up his form in recent weeks with driving style tweaks, it is clear the Briton has no real answer for Antonelli. And even if he were to match his younger team-mate, he is no longer even daring to dream of closing the 81-point deficit.

"I'm not going to say it's over, but it's exceptionally unlikely that I'm in this fight," Russell conceded after only managing fifth at the Madring. "I'm not even thinking about being in the fight because I don't think I am in the fight.

"It almost just allows me to focus race by race and just try and win as many as possible. What will be, will be. That's where we are right now."

Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

Earlier this year, it felt Russell was trying to play mind games when he put the onus on 20-year-old Antonelli to bring it home. Now it sounds like he really means it.

If there's no more threat from within for Antonelli, then a late push from Ferrari and McLaren seems like the biggest hurdle.

Speaking to Autosport earlier this month, Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur vowed his team would push until the end with upgrades, because it also stands the team in good stead for 2027. McLaren made similar comments.

Antonelli and Mercedes have been "phenomenal" - Hamilton

But to the frustration of Hamilton, who had been splitting Antonelli and Russell in the championship this summer, the Scuderia has thrown away too many points with poor race weekend execution, whether in qualifying or the grand prix. A brake failure at the start of the Spanish Grand Prix has now further knocked the wind out of the seven-time world champion's sails.

"Mercedes this year, I think they've done a phenomenal job and they deserve it," Hamilton said as he conceded defeat on Sunday, following similar comments after a frustrating Italian Grand Prix.

"We've just lost so much ground to them [Mercedes] on points. It's tough. I'm giving it everything I can, but sometimes it's just not enough. You need all the other stuff to come together."

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

Meanwhile, all reigning world champion Norris could do was doff his cap at his likely successor given the Italian's age and lack of experience.

"He’s leading by 80 points because he’s doing an incredible job," Norris acknowledged. "He’s beating a much more experienced team-mate, and a decent team-mate. Pretty phenomenal.

"I think it’s cool to see someone so young doing such an incredible job and more than likely go on and win the championship.

"He’s been impressive since the first race this year. Very few mistakes. He’s not driving like it’s his second year in F1, that’s for sure."

Sports.title: Slater to graduate from F3 to F2 for 2027
Sports.content:
Formula 3 runner-up and Audi Formula 1 junior Freddie Slater will step up to Formula 2 with Invicta Racing in 2027.

The 2024 Italian F4 and 2025 Formula Regional European champion was signed by Audi to spearhead its new Driver Development Programme in 2026, while he moved to F3 with Trident.

Four consecutive feature-race podiums meant Slater snatched the lead of the championship away from sophomore Ugo Ugochukwu going into the summer break, but he only scored 15 more points across the last five races of the season and was surpassed by the Campos driver in the title battle.

Read Also: Formula 1 Ugochukwu beats Slater to win F3 title

Slater still was the best rookie of the season – though he did take part in two rounds in 2025. Eight podiums including one victory in Hungary meant the 18-year-old Briton comfortably took the runner-up spot ahead of second-year Tuukka Taponen and fellow debutant Taito Kato.

“I’m really excited to be stepping up to Formula 2 with Invicta Racing next year,” Slater said. “I learned a lot in Formula 3 this season, and I feel I have developed as a driver and as a person over the course of the year.

“Invicta has a great record in Formula 2, and I cannot wait to get started with the team and prepare for our campaign together. I am also very grateful for the continued support from the Audi Driver Development Programme. There is still a lot for me to learn, and I’m really looking forward to taking on this new challenge.”

Rafael Camara, Invicta Racing Photo by: Clive Mason / Getty Images

The Trident-to-Invicta pipeline has been extremely successful in recent years with several instances of back-to-back titles.

Gabriel Bortoleto, Leonardo Fornaroli and Rafael Camara earned the previous three F3 crowns with the Italian squad, before switching to the Norfolk-based outfit in F2 – where Bortoleto and Fornaroli became champions as rookies. Currently a close second in the 2026 standings, Camara has a decent chance of emulating them.

Even though he narrowly failed to prevail in F3, these are the examples Slater will aim to follow in 2027.

“The move to Formula 2 is the natural next step for Freddie, and an important new phase of his development as a driver,” said Audi Driver Development Programme director Allan McNish.

“He enjoyed a strong Formula 3 season, fighting for the title until the final round – showing his speed, racecraft and progress throughout the year. We are very proud of what Freddie has achieved this season and how he has developed along the way.

“Invicta Racing has had an excellent record in recent years, and we are delighted to be working with them. We believe it is the ideal environment for him, and we look forward to supporting him as he takes on this new challenge in 2027.”

Sports.title: Norris completes first full test in McLaren’s Le Mans Hypercar
Sports.content:
Reigning Formula 1 champion Lando Norris completed his first full-fledged test at the wheel of the McLaren MCL-HY Le Mans Hypercar at Portimao on Monday.

Following last weekend’s Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit in which he was denied victory by an ill-timed Virtual Safety Car, Norris travelled across the border to Portugal for a one-day test.

The Briton completed 38 laps of the Algarve International Circuit in the V6-powered challenger, logging a total of 177 miles through the day. McLaren said his programme included testing several development items and providing feedback through his immense experience in F1.

Norris was assisted in his first LMDh test by McLaren’s 2027 drivers Mikkel Jensen and Laurens Vanthoor, who carried out further development work ahead of the British brand’s Hypercar debut next year.

"First of all, a big thanks to the McLaren Hypercar Team for letting me drive the MCL-HY,” he said.

“It was great for them to give me a chance to have a bit of fun and try something new, particularly during their busy preparations for next year.

“I think we also collected some valuable data, and I hope I was able to bring a different set of feelings, comments, and perspectives on things, which is useful for the team in this crucial testing period.

“It was cool for me personally to work with this team, and it was exciting to try new machinery too. I've not done a proper test in anything other than an F1 car for years now, so the fact I got to try something different, especially still as part of the McLaren family, was very special.

“It was a fun day in a quick car on a cool track, helping the team prepare for the start of WEC next year. A big thanks to everyone involved, I can't wait to get back in the car in the future.”

Monday’s test follows Norris sampling the MCL-HY for the first time at the car’s public debut at the Goodwood Festival of the Speed in July.

McLaren Racing boss Zak Brown had previously shown interest in fielding both Norris and Oscar Piastri in the World Endurance Championship’s blue-riband event, although any such outing may rely on the team running an additional third car.

A Le Mans outing would only be possible if there are no clashes with Norris’ F1 commitments next year.

While the full 2027 WEC calendar was already revealed three months ago, with Le Mans pencilled in for the weekend of 12-13 June, F1 is yet to publish its schedule for next year amid the war in West Asia.

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: McLaren

Speaking on Monday, McLaren Hypercar team principal James Barclay left the door open for further outings for Norris in the future, without explicitly referring to any race appearances.

“We are all racers at McLaren Racing, and competing in Formula 1, INDYCAR and the World Endurance Championship creates exciting cross-series opportunities,” he said.

“Lando was keen to drive the MCL-HY beyond his Goodwood Hill run, so we invited him to join our private Portimão test. As we fully expected he adapted very quickly, integrated seamlessly and provided valuable feedback to support the car’s development.

"It was a pleasure to have him with the team, we wish him every success for the rest of the Formula 1 season, and we look forward to welcoming him back into the McLaren Hypercar Team soon.”

Sports.title: F2 adds extra Baku feature race and insists Qatar, Abu Dhabi still on – what does this mean for F1?
Sports.content:
The Formula 2 championship has announced a "supersized" meeting for its next round in Baku. The move will see it host an additional feature race in Azerbaijan and comes just 10 days before the race weekend is due to kick off.

It is an unusual and late decision that inevitably raises eyebrows at a time when the end of the Formula 1 season remains uncertain. At present, the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix could potentially be unable to go ahead as planned due to the tense geopolitical situation in the Middle East.

In practical terms, what the F2 organisers announced on Monday, just over a week before the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, is a double-header weekend, with an additional qualifying session and feature race compared to the usual format.

"As Formula 2 is the only support event at the Azerbaijan Formula 1 Grand Prix, together with the promoters, we have opted for a supersized F2 race weekend, with one free practice, two qualifying sessions, one sprint race and two feature races," F2 CEO Bruno Michel confirmed.

"This is the only weekend where the timetable allows the additional sessions, which will increase the level of entertainment even further for the attending crowd and all our fans. The Baku City Circuit always provides us with amazing racing, so we’re very pleased to make the 12th Round of our season pretty unique."

The organisers have not specified exactly why they chose to expand the Baku meeting, but it is difficult not to see it - without being able to say so for certain - as a way of preparing for the cancellation or reshaping of some of the end-of-season events and compensating for the points that would be lost as a result.

The F2 season finale is still scheduled for Abu Dhabi Photo by: Dom Gibbons / LAT Images via Getty Images

"The final two rounds of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will resume with the usual weekend format made of one free practice followed by one qualifying, a sprint race and a feature race," F2 said in a statement.

That is the situation today, but it could quickly change depending on the decisions made by F1 regarding the end of the season.

The FIA and F1 are expected to decide on the remainder of the 2026 calendar before the end of the month, with a relocated Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang, Malaysia, already added for early October.

Among the options recently discussed is the possibility of cancelling the trips to Qatar and Abu Dhabi and heading to Imola in late November for the season final instead.

Sports.title: Spanish GP organisers promise Madring track changes following F1 criticism
Sports.content:
Organisers of Formula 1's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid are ready to make tweaks to the Madring circuit to boost overtaking for 2027, and have already received recommendations from the FIA.

The 5.4km circuit around Madrid's IFEMA fairgrounds, which made its competition debut last weekend, was praised by drivers and teams for its facilities and its driving challenge. But while the tricky combination of medium to high-speed corners delivered a high-stakes qualifying session, the lack of clear overtaking opportunities led to a lack of action throughout the weekend, including across F1, F2 and F3.

The main overtaking option was supposed to be the Turn 5 chicane following the circuit's longest straight, but the corner's awkward design made that difficult. Voicing their feedback in Friday night's drivers' briefing, drivers were particularly frustrated by the number of combined corner entries, where cars are having to brake and steer at the same time, which has made it straight-forward for the car in front to defend. They also felt the circuit's pitlane was far too long to entice teams to try different pitstop strategies.

Speaking exclusively to Autosport after Sunday's race, the event's managing director Luis Garcia Abad said his team was willing to make the necessary modifications to improve the on-track spectacle, and that he had already received recommendations from the FIA for the 2027 event.

"Being honest with you, the FIA defined clearly which is the way to improve the track layout, and we will be open because we will have to reinstall the track for the next year," Abad said. "I really believe that the drivers enjoyed qualifying a lot. But for sure we will try to make an improvement for next year."

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT Images via Getty Images

Last weekend's race was the first of a 10-year contract. And with the northern half of the circuit being designed from a blank sheet of paper on empty land, Abad vowed there is plenty of scope to make significant changes.

"We have the space, we have a venue, we have the facilities, we have the capacity to do it," he promised. "I'm sure that FOM, FIA, and ourselves, we will try. If we can improve something, we will do it."

Speaking after the race, world champion Lando Norris made a few recommendations.

"To me, it’s not a great race track. It’s great in qualifying, but a straight line from Turn 17 straight to Turn 20 [would help], to have a much wider entry like Austin Turn 1 or Turn 10, a big hairpin. You’ll create much better opportunities for everyone and you’ll be able to enjoy the race.

"There are some simple changes and maybe some trickier ones, like Turn 5, 6, 7. It’s hard to know exactly what is the best thing. The fact you have to turn and brake [at the same time] basically defeats the whole object of racing."

Sports.title: Honda replaces F1 power unit boss in organisation shuffle
Sports.content:
Aston Martin's engine partner Honda has replaced the project leader of its Formula 1 power unit programme as it aims to claw its way back into contention.

On Monday the Japanese manufacturer announced engine development leader Tetsushi Kakuda is set to be replaced by his current assistant Yoichiro Fukao, effective on 1 October. Honda Racing Corporation said the move was part of a "planned transition" but also added the aim was to "accelerate" the development of its power unit.

"Honda Racing Corporation will implement a change in the leadership of its F1 Power Unit (PU) development programme, effective October 1st, 2026, with the aim of further accelerating PU development and ensuring a smooth transition to the next generation of engineers," Honda said in a statement.

"Yoichiro Fukao, currently serving as Assistant LPL (Deputy Leader of the F1 Project, Head of the Software Division), will assume the role of LPL (Large Project Leader), succeeding Tetsushi Kakuda, who has led the PU development to date.

"This organisational change is a planned transition designed to ensure the reliable transfer of technical expertise to the next generation of engineers."

Tetsushi Kakuda, HRC, at the 2023 Japanese GP Photo by: Giorgio Piola

Honda has suffered a horrid start to the brand-new 2026 era, struggling for performance and reliability that has qualified it for additional development help. By implementing the leadership change now, Honda hopes to capitalise on the development of an overhauled power unit for 2027.

"Following the introduction of the new regulations in 2026, and with further regulatory changes expected from 2027 onwards, Honda aims to establish a robust development framework and deliver a highly competitive PU by transitioning to the new structure at an early stage," Honda added.

Following a disastrous start to 2026, Honda was afforded additional power unit help in May, beyond the original ADUO system. But over the Spanish Grand Prix weekend, there have been further talks between FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem and Aston Martin's Lawrence Stroll and Fernando Alonso over what else could be done to help the struggling manufacturer.

One suggestion is to further revisit the ADUO upgrade system designed to help a manufacturer falling behind, with both Mercedes and Red Bull Ford Powertrains being open to more tweaks.

Sports.title: F1 drivers push for Madring changes after "very poor" Spanish GP: "I almost fell asleep"
Sports.content:
The Formula 1 Spanish Grand Prix played out exactly as most drivers had feared. Max Verstappen said on Saturday that he could not see a single overtaking opportunity and added when speaking to the Dutch media, "Just give me the track map", to indicate that he would make numerous changes.

On Sunday, overtaking did indeed prove virtually impossible, making the mood in the paddock clear after the race: the Madring is entertaining over one flying lap, certainly from the drivers’ perspective, but the entertainment value of the race was particularly low.

When Autosport points out that many in the media centre almost fell asleep during the first race around the IFEMA complex, Gabriel Bortoleto responds: “I almost fell asleep as well!”

Even race winner Kimi Antonelli shared that view. The championship leader enjoyed qualifying, but not the race.

"It definitely doesn’t create overtaking opportunities and it doesn’t push you to try and make a move, because 80% of the time you might have contact," said the Mercedes driver after the race.

"I think especially in the second chicane, if I would have turned in there, me and Lando would have touched and probably gone into the wall and blocked the road. It definitely wouldn’t have been nice.

"So, I think there are some corners that need to be changed to create more overtaking opportunities, because right now, yes, it’s nice over one lap, but for sure in the race you’re just stuck behind."

Antonelli states that overtaking manoeuvres in Madrid will usually end in a crash Photo by: Clive Mason / Getty Images

The drivers had already seen that coming beforehand, especially as the designers had not asked them for input in advance. Verstappen explained that this only happened in Jeddah after the track proved dangerous in its first year, but not with new circuits such as the Madring.

For the future, drivers would like to see that change. That includes Haas' Oliver Bearman, who crashed heavily in third practice on Saturday and missed qualifying.

"You only have to look at the layout, and it's quite clear that it's going to be a poor track for racing", Bearman said when asked by Autosport about the lack of overtakes.

"I mean, when you arrive and you see that layout, you're like, what do you expect us to do? It's a bit of a shame."

According to him, there are two factors behind this, making attacking very difficult and defending too easy.

"Not only do you have a lot of long combined exits where it's really tough to put power down, but you have a lot of combined entries as well. It's very easy to drive a bit dangerously defending your position and, therefore, very hard to send an overtake.

"We already said that to the FIA on Friday and we need to look into a way to make the track a bit more interesting for us, because it's interesting to drive for sure, but in the race it's very poor."

Verstappen had already said on Saturday that he couldn’t see any opportunities to overtake Photo by: Peter Fox / Getty Images

What Bearman had already seen from the layout was quickly confirmed during the race weekend in the junior categories, Alex Albon concludes.

"I hope there's open-mindedness to make some track changes for next year,' the Williams driver said. "I mean, if the F3 cars can't overtake, then you know there's going to be no overtaking the whole weekend.

"I think there only needs to be a couple of changes to fix the problem. Otherwise, honestly, it's not a bad track. It's quite a fun track to drive, just like you saw in the races, it's pretty boring."

Three areas to improve at the Madring for 2027

While Albon says relatively minor changes are needed for 2027, the drivers have already shared several suggestions during the weekend – starting with the Williams driver himself.

"A lot of it is around Turn 3 to Turn 5. I think that whole area needs to be redone, maybe straighter braking zones. We need to remove that chicane. It's good for spectacle, but it's not good for racing", Albon said.

"And I think the banking, as great as it is, it's not really doing a good enough job in Turn 13. Turn 13 maybe needs to be a slower corner, a bigger braking zone."

Aside from the fact that the chicane formed by Turns 5 and 6 is bad for racing, Bortoleto also felt another problem on Sunday.

"Just the jump in T5, to do that 50 laps, you get quite a lot of headache at the end of the race. So, it's not the easiest one for our body", the Audi driver said.

According to the drivers, turns 5 and 6 in particular need to be changed, although Albon says the banking isn’t helping enough either Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT Images via Getty Images

Apart from the section around Turn 5 – where drivers see most of the problems – Lando Norris also has a suggestion for the final sector of the circuit.

"I think there are some obvious changes they should make. They should get rid of Turn 18, 19, useless. Just have more of a straight into a hairpin. I don’t know how someone looks at this design and goes, ‘Mint.’ Yeah, I think there’s a lot of opportunity."

That change would remind the reigning world champion of what he considers a good example: the Circuit of the Americas.

"To me, it’s not a great racetrack. It’s great in qualifying, but, you know, a straight line from 17 straight to 20 [would help], to have a much wider entry like Austin Turn 1 or Turn 10, a big hairpin. You’ll create much better opportunities for everyone and you’ll be able to enjoy the race.

"There are some simple changes and maybe some trickier ones, like Turn 5, 6, 7. It’s hard to know exactly what is the best thing. The fact you have to turn and brake basically defeats the whole object of racing. So, they can do some simple changes, I think, easy changes and maybe some trickier changes, but I hope they do it because then it should be more exciting for everyone."

In addition to Turns 5-6 and 18-19, the drivers are also pushing for another change: a shorter pitlane, to encourage additional stops and create more strategic variation.

Sports.title: ‘Realistically I’m not in the fight for the drivers’ championship’ admits Russell | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s closest championship rival admits he does not have a realistic chance of beating him to the title this year.

George Russell lies 81 points behind his team mate with 233 available over the remaining rounds. He hasn’t gained on Antonelli since the British Grand Prix two months ago.

Russell finished fifth in Sunday’s race at the Madring, almost half a minute behind his race-winning team mate, after making a second pit stop. But after struggling with his car earlier in the season, Russell says recent rounds have gone better.

“It has been a more positive couple of races even though the result was far from great today,” said Russell on Sunday. “But it’s kind of the story of the season.

“I just need to focus on the performance and keep trying to help the team. We’re obviously in a great place to win the constructors’ [championship]. Realistically I’m not in the fight for the drivers and that just allows me just to focus on race-by-race and trying to focus on just getting some good results.”

Russell led the championship after the first two rounds but Antonelli moved ahead at the Japanese Grand Prix. He scored his eighth win on Sunday while Russell only has two victories so far this season.

Antonelli said he will not relent as he bids to clinch the world championship. “It’s great, but we’ve just got to keep pushing, keep delivering the results and just trying to do the best job I can whenever I go on track,” he said.

“Because of course, yes, I have a big lead, but you never know what can happen. So I just need to be ready for anything and keep maximising every opportunity I get, and then we’ll see where we end up at the end of the year.”

Sports.title: Pictures: Norris tests McLaren’s MCL-HY WEC hypercar at Algarve | Other Motorsport
Sports.content:
Lando Norris had his first run in McLaren’s new World Endurance Championship hypercar following the Spanish Grand Prix.

The reigning Formula 1 world champion drove the car at the Autodromo do Algarve in Portugal.

McLaren will enter the WEC’s top tier next season. “It was great for them to give me a chance to have a bit of fun and try something new, particularly during their busy preparations for next year,” said Norris.

“I think we also collected some valuable data, and I hope I was able to bring a different set of feelings, comments, and perspectives on things, which is useful for the team in this crucial testing period.”

F1 will return to the Algarve circuit next year, for the first time since 2021. Norris previously drove the car in a brief demonstration run at the Goodwood Festival of Speed.

“It was cool for me personally to work with this team, and it was exciting to try new machinery too,” Norris continued. “I’ve not done a proper test in anything other than an F1 car for years now, so the fact I got to try something different, especially still as part of the McLaren family, was very special.”

McLaren hypercar team principal James Barclay said “Lando was keen to drive the MCL-HY beyond his Goodwood Hill run, so we invited him to join our private Portimao test.”

“As we fully expected he adapted very quickly, integrated seamlessly and provided valuable feedback to support the car’s development,” he added.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Is the new Madrid’s circuit one of Formula 1’s worst tracks? | Brief
Sports.content:
Almost no one had anything positive to say about Formula 1’s newest circuit following the first Spanish Grand Prix yesterday.

One point which several readers made about the Madring, echoed by Lando Norris in the press conference after the race, was why the designers of the hybrid track had created a layout so narrow, twisty and difficult for cars to race closely on:

It was absolutely terrible. I saw someone say they enjoyed FP4, which more or less covers it. But I want to give it a zero [out of 10], because the track was so avoidably terrible. It’s not a once-good track that has been outgrown, like Monaco, or a circuit designed using supposedly sound theory that just didn’t work, like Abu Dhabi. They had a more or less blank slate and (I can only assume deliberately, as no one is dense enough to have done that by accident) created a track it’s impossible to actually race on. I’ve been watching F1 for over 30 years and (having spent some time reflecting to avoid recency bias) the Madring is the worst circuit, for its generation of cars, that I have ever seen.

Sports.title: Norris sure McLaren were right to pit him immediately after the VSC | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris defended McLaren’s tactics after he lost his chance to win yesterday’s Spanish Grand Prix during a Virtual Safety Car period.

The McLaren driver was leading from Andrea Kimi Antonelli and Max Verstappen when a VSC period began on lap 15. Norris passed the pit lane entrance before the VSC was triggered, but Antonelli and all the other drivers had the chance to pit before it ended.

The VSC period ended before Norris returned to the pit lane entrance. McLaren summoned him in anyway, despite not having the opportunity to pit while the cars were lapping slowly. Norris’s misfortune was compounded by a problem with his right-front wheel which slowed his pit stop.

Other drivers such as Charles Leclerc opted not to pit at this time, extending their first stint. However they started the race on the hard compound, while Norris was on mediums. He believes pitting immediately after the VSC was the best choice for him.

“I had to come in at the end of the lap because it was the only chance,” Norris explained. “It was still effectively some pit loss, the fact that everyone’s on colder tyres [means] you’re still minimising the pit loss. The medium tyre was destroyed and the hard tyre was amazing.”

Norris said he was “just unfortunate” with the timing of the VSC period but he was able to close on Antonelli and Verstappen after they closed on Leclerc.

“The pace was very, very strong on the hard tyre. I know they were stuck [but] we caught up 13, 14 seconds or more, almost.

“So there’s plenty of positives. A day full of positives, just one thing let it all down.”

Asked whether McLaren should have anticipated a VSC period would be triggered after Lance Stroll stopped in a run-off area, Norris said: “I need to speak to the pit wall. I’m just driving the car, I don’t know these things.

“So, I need to go speak to the team and see what else. But it’s not the team’s fault, it’s not my fault. Simple as that. We were just unlucky.”

Sports.title: Formula 1 drivers slate “useless” Madring circuit design after dull Spanish Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Drivers called for changes to the layout of the Madring following yesterday’s processional race on Formula 1’s newest track.

Drivers in the Formula 2 and Formula 3 support races also found overtaking was difficult around the 22-turn course.

The track features several tight chicanes in the opening sector. The latter part of the lap also proved difficult for cars to follow closely.

Lando Norris said there are “some obvious changes they should make” to the circuit. “They should get rid of [turns] 18 [and] 19. Useless. Just have more of a straight into a hairpin.”

The world champion said he couldn’t understand how the design was considered suitable for F1 racing. “I don’t know how someone looks at this design and goes: ‘Mint.’ I think there’s a lot of opportunity.”

However he believes that with some changes the track’s layout can be improved. “I think they can make it into a track that’s good for racing and I’m excited to come back here next year if they can make these changes because I think it’s a track that is good fun to drive and it can be a great race track.

“To me, it’s not a great race track. It’s great in qualifying, but [they need to have a] straight line from 17 straight to 20, have a much wider entry like Austin turn one or turn 10, a big hairpin. You’ll create much better opportunities for everyone and you’ll be able to enjoy the race.”

The geography of the surroundings may make it difficult to fix some elements of the track design, Norris admitted. “There are some simple changes and maybe some trickier ones.

“Like turn five, six and seven: it’s hard to know exactly what’s the best thing. The fact you have to turn and brake basically defeats the whole object of racing.

“So, they can do some simple changes, I think, easy changes and maybe some are more tricky. But I hope they do it because then it should be more exciting for everyone.”

Race winner Andrea Kimi Antonelli said the layout discourages drivers from trying to pass rivals because the risk of a collision is high.

“It definitely doesn’t create overtaking opportunities and it doesn’t push you to try and make a move because 80% of the time you might have contact.

“I think especially in the second chicane [on the first lap], if I would have turned in, me and Lando would have touched and probably gone in the wall and blocked the road. It definitely wouldn’t have been nice.

Sports.title: William Zepeda Can Break Abdullah Mason Before Twelve
Sports.content:
“With my style of fighting, going in, getting out, maintaining pressure, maintaining distance, and my body punches, it would be a hard-fought battle,” Zepeda told The Ring. “I believe I have enough weapons in my arsenal to tire him out. I don’t think he would be able to last all 12 rounds with me.”

Mason brings elite speed and concussive power. His razor-sharp straight left down the pipe can crack Zepeda clean whenever the Mexican pressurer charges inside.

The mirror southpaw stance cuts both ways. It clears an open lane for Zepeda’s punishing lead right hook to the liver. Once Zepeda buries his head into Mason’s chest, he creates brutal leverage for short, digging uppercuts.

Mason prefers operating at mid-range, using fast counters to control the pace. He dealt with gritty forward marchers before, but nobody has forced him to fight off his back foot while absorbing heavy artillery downstairs for thirty-six minutes.

Zepeda dropped a decision to Shakur Stevenson in July 2025, but the official cards failed to capture the action. I scored that battle a draw. Zepeda dragged Shakur into the most grueling dogfight of his career. Shakur rolled and shelled up upstairs, yet none of that saved his midsection. Zepeda battered his ribs relentlessly, forcing him into a desperate grind until the final bell.

Mason possesses a weapon Shakur lacked: pure one-punch finishing ability. That leaves Zepeda walking a tightrope through the opening frames. A single flush counter left hand could end the night before the body assault takes hold.

If Mason cannot score an early stoppage, the dynamic shifts completely. The young titlist must prove he can survive relentless trench warfare, manage his gas tank under suffocating heat, and keep his pop into the deep waters. With Gervonta dodging Zepeda, a Mason clash stands out as the premier unification at 135 pounds. It pits an explosive young talent against boxing’s most relentless engine.

Top Rank is unlikely to greenlight this anytime soon. Bob Arum and the matchmakers in Las Vegas are master builders who protect their premier young assets, and throwing Mason into Zepeda right now goes completely against their playbook.

The Sam Noakes fight was a massive red flag for that kind of matchup. Noakes is a tough, relentless battler, but he came forward in straight lines and still made Mason take an uncomfortable amount of clean punishment. Mason had to dig deep into his bag, box off the back foot, and survive serious roughhouse moments to secure that decision.

Zepeda is an entirely different monster. He does not just charge forward like Noakes; he cuts the ring in half with footwork, smothers exit lanes, and throws triple-digit volume per round. Against Shakur, Zepeda showed that elite defensive movement cannot fully neutralize his body work. Shakur possesses some of the best lateral movement and distance control in the sport, yet he spent twelve rounds getting his ribs tenderized.

Mason likes to fight. His instinct when hurt or crowded is to plant his feet and fire back. Against punchers he can out-speed, that wins fight-of-the-year candidates. Against Zepeda, trading in the pocket plays right into Mexican pressure. Zepeda will happily eat two flush shots upstairs if it allows him to dig three hooks into the liver and solar plexus.

Top Rank knows what happens to young champions who absorb that kind of physical tax too early. Even if Mason survived twelve rounds and boxed to a narrow points win, the physical wear from a Zepeda fight can permanently shave years off a young fighter’s prime.

Expect Top Rank to keep Mason on a steady diet of title defenses against mid-tier contenders, guys who will stand at range and let him look like a million bucks on DAZN. They will let Zepeda hunt unifications elsewhere or wait until Mason physically fills out and tightens his inside defense before they even consider putting him in the same ring.

Sports.title: Joshua–Fury Friday Plan Makes Cardiff Even Worse
Sports.content:
“I think we’re going to get December the 4th or December the 11th, which is a Friday night, with that landing at Cardiff, at the Principality Stadium,” said Oliver to talkSPORT Boxing.

Oliver suggested the Friday date would suit Netflix and the American market because of sporting competition on Saturday. The apparent trade is clear: British spectators get the fight on home soil, but the timing is designed around viewers thousands of miles away.

Principality Stadium has a roof, making it one of the few realistic UK stadium options in December. That solves the weather issue. It does nothing for supporters trying to reach their hotels or homes after a main event scheduled between 2 and 3 a.m.

Friday also forces many ticket buyers to take time away from work just to travel to Cardiff. They would then spend most of the night inside the stadium before being released into the city when public transportation is at its weakest.

Calling this a victory for UK boxing requires ignoring the people in the seats. They provide the atmosphere, buy the tickets, and pay the inflated hotel prices, yet their comfort is treated as the least important part of the promotion.

Joshua and Fury should have fought years ago when both were near the top of the heavyweight division. Fans are now being asked to endure an absurd timetable for the delayed meeting of two faded former champions.

Cardiff may be the final location, and Friday may satisfy Netflix, but neither makes a 2 or 3 a.m. fight reasonable. Putting the event in Britain means little when British supporters are treated like studio extras for an American broadcast.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Orders Desperate Gervonta Davis To Get A Tune-Up First
Sports.content:
Tank’s response makes it clear that contact between the camps does not mean the rematch is close. Davis initially named 140 pounds, later offered 144, and now ridiculed Ryan’s insistence on the full welterweight limit.

Garcia revealed that Davis and Al Haymon reached out to open talks for a rematch. Instead of jumping at the offer, Garcia immediately laid down the law: the fight happens at the full 147-pound limit, and Davis must take a tune-up first.

“I can confirm Gervonta and Al have contacted my team. 147 or nothing,” Ryan said on X. “And I want him to get a tune up fight and be at his best when we fight. He has some stuff to handle but we for sure going to get it going on. Let’s rumble.”

Telling Davis to go find an interim opponent is the ultimate power move. It treats Davis like an unranked challenger auditioning for a shot at the crown, not a pound-for-pound star. Davis is coming off a flat, controversial draw against Lamont Roach, an outing that destroyed his invincibility and wounded his box-office appeal. He needs Garcia to restore his standing, but Ryan refuses to hand him a lifeline.

Ordering Gervonta into a tune-up also eliminates every built-in excuse about inactivity while Ryan handles business of his own. Garcia plans to defend his belt in December or January, targeting Angel Fierro or Isaac “Pitbull” Cruz.

Taking Cruz would be a direct psychological attack on Tank. Cruz gave Davis twelve grueling rounds in 2021. If Garcia blows Cruz out inside a few rounds, Davis will enter negotiations with zero credibility remaining.

Davis already senses his control slipping away. He tried offering 140 pounds, then floated 144 from burner accounts. Ryan shut down both numbers without hesitation. Fresh off obliterating Conor Benn in two rounds, Ryan has zero reason to drain himself.

Davis spent years calling the shots. Now he is the needy party begging for terms, and Ryan is perfectly content to make him wait outside.

Sports.title: Newcomers Teaira Skinner And Chelsea Washington Will Clash At The Supper
Sports.content:
Representing Baltimore’s renowned Upton Boxing Center, Teaira Skinner has been boxing since she was 16. Although she is only 26 years old, she looks up to boxers such as Laila Ali, Ann Wolfe, Aaron Pryor, and Pernell Whitaker.

As a kid, the Texas native Chelsea Washington used to get into fights almost every day. She became interested in boxing and started training with Coach Sam Clarkson.

Washington has trained on and off for 15 years, but she never got the chance to build her career because she had kids. Now the 31-year-old has been training consistently; she’s focused and ready to start her boxing journey.

Teaira Skinner has amateur experience, and she already has a pro fight under her belt. In February 2026, Skinner made her pro boxing debut, stopping Samantha Maury in the second round.

Skinner is a hard worker, and she focuses on improving every day. She’s a talented fighter who is a historian of the game. Skinner’s goal is to win fights and entertain the fans.

“What you get out of me is exciting fights. You never have a dull moment with me, and I will always figure out a way to win,” Skinner stated.

Her opponent, Chelsea Washington, has gained boxing experience strictly through sparring. Washington was set to make her debut back in July 2026 at the Roy Jones Jr. event, Royal Roundz 5, but unfortunately the event was canceled.

Now Washington is ready to make her debut on Saturday night in Baltimore, Maryland. Washington knows her opponent and how she plans to approach the fight.

“I am a southpaw, and my style may be a little different,” Washington said. “I adjust while in the fight. I know that she has amateur experience and won her first pro fight. I know she’s tough, but on September 19th we will find out who’s tougher.”

The September 19th event is a Skyy Myles Promotions show featuring Chrisean Rock, Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson, and Mia “Killer Bee” Ellis, but the fight of the night could very well be the flyweight clash between Teaira Skinner and Chelsea Washington.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Won’t Repeat Daniel Dubois Mistakes
Sports.content:
“I became a victim of my own success,” Wardley said during a joint interview with Dubois. “I got too comfortable with the fact that I caught him in the first 10 seconds of the fight. He went down, caught him in the third, and he went down again.”

Wardley treats the loss as a collection of missed opportunities. That overlooks the adjustments Dubois made after surviving the early trouble.

Dubois raised his guard, worked behind a stiff jab, and shut down the gaps Wardley capitalized on early. Once the champion timed those looping power shots, the momentum shifted completely. Wardley carried no counter. He discarded his lead hand entirely, loading up on every swing in search of a knockout blow.

That frantic pace burned valuable energy and gave Dubois clear sight of every incoming punch. Wardley also left his chin parked on the center line, giving the champion an open target to snap home continuous straight punches.

His movement after punching was no better. After throwing, Wardley often admired his work or pulled straight back with his chin exposed. Instead of stepping to an angle or tying Dubois up, he remained directly in front of the return fire.

“I’ll make a mistake once, but I’m not going to do it twice,” Wardley said.

Wardley made multiple blunders, but Dubois forced the issue by reading the telegraphed shots and imposing his own terms.

Wardley reached the heavyweight summit relying on natural power, awkward angles, and pure fighting instincts rather than a seasoned amateur pedigree. That raw approach stunned Dubois early, but it left Wardley without the foundational ring craft required to alter his attack once the champion timed him. Deep-rooted technical tendencies are hard to overhaul, and ingraining sound fundamentals over a single training camp remains a massive hurdle.

Wardley needs a jab to hide his right hand and preserve energy. He must also move his head after punching and stop retreating in a straight line. He has already proved he can hurt Dubois. The return bout hinges on his ability to outbox a champion who will not break under pressure.

Sports.title: Isaac Cruz Risks Ryan Garcia Payday Against Bravo
Sports.content:
Ryan listed Cruz alongside Angel Fierro as potential targets for December or January. Fierro represents the softer touch. Cruz brings name value, explosive fan appeal, and an aggressive style tailored for Ryan. He charges forward, unleashes wild hooks, and creates endless counter-punching openings.

Cruz frequently barrels inside behind wide, looping shots without slipping his head. Lamont Roach Jr. repeatedly timed Cruz, holding him to a draw in December 2025. Ryan’s counter left hook delivers explosive power that makes those reckless charges far more hazardous.

Bravo lacks Roach’s refined skill, but his 17 knockouts prove he carries legitimate power. One clean shot could stun Cruz, wrecking his plans for a massive winter payday. Bravo enters with total freedom. Nobody expects his hand to be raised, and nobody is booking his next ring appearance.

Physical dimensions heavily favor Ryan in a potential clash. Cruz built his reputation at lightweight, remaining undersized at 140 pounds. Ryan operates as a full welterweight with little reason to boil down again. Cruz gives up height, reach, and pounds while marching into the path of boxing’s quickest counter left hook.

Cruz needs to dominate, not merely collect a decision. A sloppy, unconvincing performance gives Ryan every reason to skip him entirely and book Fierro next. That would leave Cruz on the outside, watching his massive winter payday vanish into thin air.

Sports.title: Muhammad Ali Outsmarts Leon Spinks To Make History
Sports.content:
Spinks had defeated an underprepared Ali in Las Vegas despite having only seven professional fights. Ali treated the rematch as his final championship stand. Spinks handled his sudden fame much differently.

The 25-year-old champion missed training time, disappeared from camp, and surrounded himself with an oversized entourage. His corner became divided by competing advisers. The disorganization reached an almost comical level when his team forgot basic supplies on fight day.

Spinks had youth, stamina, and confidence. Ali had discipline. That difference decided the “Battle of New Orleans” before either man reached the ring.

Ali Turns Holding Into A Weapon

Ali knew he could no longer dance continuously for 15 rounds. His solution was to fight in short tactical sequences.

He jabbed, landed the occasional right hand, stepped away, and clinched Spinks before the champion could plant his feet. Ali frequently controlled the back of Spinks’s head, forcing the younger fighter to restart after every break.

Referee Lucien Joubert penalized Ali in the fifth round for excessive holding, but the deduction revealed how central clinching was to the plan. Ali was not merely resting. He was breaking Spinks’s rhythm and preventing him from using the relentless combinations that had won their first fight.

Spinks kept advancing without cutting off the ring. His aggression became predictable. Instead of making Ali work at a punishing pace, he followed him and accepted repeated resets.

Ali’s old speed surfaced only in flashes, but he no longer needed to dominate every second. He controlled where the exchanges occurred and how long they lasted.

The judges scored the fight 10-4, 11-4, and 10-4 for Ali.

The championship picture carried an irony that became clearer with time. The WBC had stripped Spinks after he chose the richer Ali rematch instead of facing Ken Norton.

Norton received the WBC title before losing it to Larry Holmes in June 1978. By the time Ali reclaimed the WBA crown, Holmes already held the other major belt and represented the division’s future.

Ali had secured his historic third championship, but he was no longer the best heavyweight in the world. The throne had split between boxing’s greatest star and the younger fighter destined to succeed him.

A Perfect Ending That Did Not Last

The ABC broadcast reached an enormous prime-time audience, with Howard Cosell calling the action. The record indoor crowd, celebrity attendance, and multimillion-dollar gate turned Ali’s victory into a global cultural event.

Ali formally retired in June 1979, giving boxing what looked like a perfect conclusion. He had avenged his loss, regained his championship and left with history secured.

His later returns against Holmes and Trevor Berbick damaged that ending. Still, New Orleans remains the final championship performance of a diminished master who understood exactly what he had left and used every bit of it.

Sports.title: Bakhram Murtazaliev Returns December 12 In Russia
Sports.content:
Fans should be glad to see the heavy handed Russian back. His third-round destruction of Tim Tszyu in October 2024 established him as one of the most dangerous punchers at 154 pounds. Kelly then showed how that power can be neutralized.

Tszyu stayed within punching range and engaged Murtazaliev in midrange exchanges. Kelly remained mobile, refused to plant his feet for long and forced the champion to chase him. Murtazaliev struggled to cut off the ring or trap Kelly against the ropes, giving future opponents a clear tactical plan.

The champion also learned an unforgiving lesson about defending in the challenger’s home region. He left the decision to three judges in Newcastle, England, and a strange 10-10 score in the final round helped Kelly escape with the belt. Murtazaliev’s attempt to obtain an immediate IBF rematch went nowhere.

At 33, Murtazaliev cannot afford an extended series of soft opponents. His inactivity has removed him from the conversation while Kelly, Jaron Ennis and Vergil Ortiz Jr. pursue the division’s largest fights.

Murtazaliev is now trapped in an awkward position. He has no championship, carries serious knockout power and lacks the commercial following that would persuade leading contenders to face him voluntarily. That makes him a high-risk fight with little financial reward.

Returning in Russia gets him active, but it will not restore his position in the American or British markets. Murtazaliev likely must force another title opportunity through the rankings, possibly by winning an IBF eliminator.

He will eventually need another road fight. Before taking it, Murtazaliev must learn how to catch mobile boxers and ensure that his next championship is not carried into hostile territory without a plan to remove the judges.

Ghana News.title: US borrowing costs hit highest level since 2007
Ghana News.content:
US government borrowing costs climbed to their highest level since 2007 after a jump in oil prices further fuelled inflation concerns.

The effective interest rate on US government bonds with a 10-year maturity, known as the 10-year Treasury yield, rose as high as 5.04% but has since eased.

Government bond yields have been rising globally for months, driven by concerns that inflation from the oil price surge since the start of the US-Israel war with Iran will lead to higher interest rates.

The US has been buying back bonds in a bid to drive Treasury yields down, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent calling the intervention "successful".

The global benchmark wholesale oil price rose to over $109 a barrel on Tuesday, up from around $86 at the end of August, after renewed concerns about Saudi Arabia's ability to export oil following rising tensions in the region.

Investors are anticipating the US Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh will raise interest rates to combat the inflation caused by higher oil prices.

However, US President Donald Trump opposes a rate hike, having long argued lower rates are great for boosting the economy.

He fell out with Warsh's predecessor Jerome Powell over his decision not to cut rates.

Higher interest rates and inflation tend to drive up the yields bond investors demand on government borrowing.

Bond yields can also indicate how much faith investors have in a given government, with higher yields reflecting lower confidence.

Competition for debt from artificial intelligence (AI) firms is also driving up yields.

Tech giants are borrowing massive piles of cash to build huge data centres. This raises interest rates on tech firms' debt, which increases government bond yields in response.

Carol Schleif, chief market strategist at BMO Wealth Management, said bond markets had been signalling for weeks that higher interest rates may be needed.

While the rise in borrowing costs has been "orderly" this year, rather than sudden, she said rates could remain elevated if geopolitical tensions and high energy prices remain "front and centre".

Ghana News.title: Kylian Mbappé scores, sets up winner as Real Madrid top Elche
Ghana News.content:
Carlos Espí tapped in a stoppage-time winner -- from a Kylian Mbappé assist -- as Real Madrid won 3-2 at Elche after letting slip a two-goal lead to climb level on points with Barcelona at the top of LaLiga.

Espi, a summer signing from Levante, stepped off the bench to rescue Real for the second time this season having struck a last-minute winner on his debut at Espanyol on the opening day.

Real appeared to be in control at half-time as they led through Elche goalkeeper Matias Dituro's own goal and Mbappé's seventh goal in six league games this season.

Elche struck back through Abiel Osorio midway through the second half and substitute Fer Nino fired an 83rd-minute equaliser, only for Espi to snatch all three points for Jose Mourinho's side.

Madrid bounced back from their recent defeat at Real Betis by beating Inter Milan in last week's Champions League opener and won 4-1 at home against Rayo Vallecano on Saturday.

And they should have taken a second-minute lead when the unmarked Vinícius Júnior side-footed a golden chance wide at the back post in the second minute.

Dean Huijsen's header from Arda Guler's cross was well held by Elche goalkeeper Dituro, while Osorio was wayward with his effort as the home side ensured it was not all one-way traffic.

But Madrid made the breakthrough in the 25th minute, with Elche punished for Sangare's clumsy foul on Federico Valverde and Guler's subsequent free kick hitting a post before rebounding in off a stationary Dituro.

The visitors doubled their lead in the 33rd minute when Yan Diomande's cross from the right picked out Mbappé in the box and the Frenchman squeezed his shot beyond the on-rushing Dituro and into the bottom corner.

Madrid created further first-half chances, but Elche showed plenty of spirit with Osorio's shot on the turn flying narrowly wide and Tete Morente's low shot well saved by Thibaut Courtois.

Mourinho's side were content to sit back and hit Elche on the break in the second period, but Vinícius wasted another chance when he fired wide from Guler's cross.

Elche made them pay by reducing the deficit in the 71st minute, substitute Lucas Cepeda getting to the byline and crossing for Osorio to beat Courtois with a fine downward header.

Diomande's effort was blocked and Trent Alexander-Arnold was wayward with a free kick before Elche raised the roof with an 83rd-minute equaliser.

Allowed to press on by Madrid, Osorio was afforded too much time to find Fer Nino inside the penalty area and he had plenty of space to pick his spot and finish low into the bottom corner.

But in the first minute of added time, with Elche pushing for a winner, Madrid broke through Mbappé down the left and his cross was turned home by Espi to leave Elche bottom of the table and winless in their first six matches.

Ghana News.title: Tuchel regrets not eating Azteca turf after win over Mexico
Ghana News.content:
Thomas Tuchel regrets not eating any of the grass at the Azteca Stadium after England's World Cup win against Mexico.

His Three Lions beat the co-hosts 3-2 in the last-16 tie in July, despite playing much of the second half with 10 men following Jarell Quansah's red card.

England went on to reach the semi-finals, where they lost to Argentina, before beating France in the Bronze medal match for third place.

Tuchel, though, made a bizarre admission during an interview with Daniel Sturridge for the FA's forthcoming feature 'Reflections: England's World Cup Journey'.

He said: "I texted a friend after the match and I just wrote, 'I regret that I didn't eat some grass after the match to keep something from this in my body forever'. That was the feeling. That was the moment.

England's victory was only the third time Mexico had tasted defeat at the stadium in 90 competitive matches.

Tuchel described it as one of the highlights of the campaign and hailed the "huge bond" within the camp, especially the reaction to Jordan Henderson's tournament-ending injury after falling over an advertising hoarding while celebrating the Azteca success.

"This game had so much of what you could wish for," added the German. "If you needed any proof of what it meant to these players and how they were with each other, it was the moment Jordan fell over and broke his arm.

"Within a second, the players were there. Every single player was there stopping the celebrations, building a shield, protecting Jordan, not going anywhere, in full empathy. It was so special."

England are next in action against World Cup winners Spain on 26 September in their 2026-27 Uefa Nations League opener, with the 2028 European Championships also on Tuchel's radar.

Confident of ending England's wait for a first senior men's trophy since 1966, he believed their World Cup run not only cemented his relationship with the squad - "it feels like they are my players now" - but also represented "something to build on".

Tuchel added: "I'm very excited. I think we got another step closer and I think we're there."

Ghana News.title: Kudus ends 257-day wait for Tottenham start against Liverpool
Ghana News.content:
Tottenham and Ghana forward Mohammed Kudus made his long-awaited return to the starting lineup, playing 75 minutes in Spurs’ Carabao Cup third-round clash with Liverpool at Anfield.

The 26-year-old had not started a match for Tottenham in 257 days but showed little sign of rust as Roberto De Zerbi’s side faced the Premier League champions.

Kudus looked lively throughout his time on the pitch and came close to making an immediate impact in the 32nd minute.

With Tottenham trailing 1-0, the Ghana international found himself with a golden opportunity to level the score, but he fired over the bar from close range.

His evening ended after 75 minutes when he was replaced by new signing Savio.

Tottenham were eventually eliminated from the competition, with Liverpool securing a 3-1 victory at Anfield.

Kudus’ return to the starting XI will be encouraging news for Ghana, with the forward expected to feature in Carlos Queiroz’s squad for the upcoming 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia.

Ghana News.title: Coutinho joins Neymar at Santos for rest of season
Ghana News.content:
Philippe Coutinho has joined his close friend and Brazil team-mate Neymar at Santos FC until the end of the season.

The former Liverpool and Barcelona midfielder, 34, has been without a club since leaving Vasco da Gama in February.

Coutinho returned to his childhood club in 2024 but left after 81 appearances, saying he was "tired mentally".

Santos welcomed the player on social media by posting an old photo of Coutinho and Neymar as teenagers, alongside a new version of them re-enacting the pose in the gym.

The club also posted a video of Coutinho walking into the dressing room where he receives a hug from Neymar and says "if it's a dream, I don't want to wake up".

Neymar returned to Santos, his childhood team, in January last year and this will be the first time that the friends have played together at club level.

Coutinho started his career at Vasco before joining Inter Milan and later moving to Liverpool in 2013, where he scored 54 goals in 201 games before joining Barcelona for £142m in 2018.

He later had stints at Bayern Munich, Aston Villa and Al-Duhail before the return to Vasco.
