World.title: Zamfara organises CBT for 6,412 applicants to boost primary education
World.content:
The Zamfara State Government scheduled a Computer-Based Test (CBT) for thousands of candidates who applied for the 3,050 basic education teaching slots across the state.

The management of Zamfara Information Technology Development Agency (ZITDA) announced this in a circular released at the weekend.

The CBT is following Governor Dauda Lawal’s approval for the recruitment of 3,050 basic school teachers through an open, merit–based digital portal – targeted at underserved and rural schools.

This additional recruitment followed an earlier hiring of 4,000 teachers and upgrading of 789 schools by the governor in a bold move to overhaul the education sector in the state.

The governor had earlier recruited another set of 500 science teachers who were deployed across the 14 local government areas in the state to address the critical shortage of science educators in secondary schools.

The ZITDA circular said the screening committee had shortlisted 6,412 applicants out of the 10,876 that applied.

The agency had fixed Wednesday, September 16, 2026, for the CBT.

The agency advised all shortlisted candidates to check their registered email addresses used during the application process, as notification emails have been sent to successful candidates.

It said the SMS notifications have also been sent to the shortlisted candidates’ registered phone numbers.

ZITDA also urged the candidates to visit the official recruitment portal (https://recruitment.zamfara.gov.ng/ube) to check their application status and print their examination/invitation slip.

It said the examination slip contains all the necessary information about the CBT examination, including the CBT centre, examination date, examination time, and venue.

Candidates were therefore advised to carefully check all the information contained on their slips.

They were also advised to come along with the printed examination slip and a valid means of identification to the CBT examination.

“The examination slip is mandatory for admission into the CBT examination hall. Candidates are therefore strongly advised to print their slips ahead of the examination,” the circular said.

It warned that applicants who have not received an SMS or email notification are advised to remain patient and regularly check the recruitment portal for updates and further opportunities.

World.title: Sokoto defends metropolis-only school resumption
World.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

SOKOTO — The Sokoto State Government has defended its decision to reopen only schools within the state capital, saying the continued closure of schools outside the metropolis is a security measure taken in compliance with a directive from the Federal Government.

Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Prof. Muhammad Ladan Ala, stated this on Monday in Sokoto while briefing journalists on the status of schools following the recent resumption arrangement.

Ala explained that schools within the Sokoto metropolis were currently operating, while those outside the designated area remained closed pending further directives from the appropriate authorities.

“What we said is that schools within Sokoto metropolis are the ones that are in operation. Other schools that are not within Sokoto metropolis are still closed. We are awaiting directives from the top so that they will go ahead,” he said.

He said the metropolis, for the purpose of the arrangement, covered Kware, Dange-Shuni, Wamakko, Sokoto North and Sokoto South Local Government Areas.

The commissioner said the government would not compromise the safety of pupils and students in its determination to reopen schools, stressing that security considerations remained paramount.

“Security is more important than anything you are thinking about. It is only when you have security, when you have peace, then you will be able to go to your farms, you will be able to go to your school,” Ala said.

He disclosed that the state’s Safe School Initiative remained operational, with the ministry maintaining regular consultations and engagements with security agencies, including the Nigerian Army, Police and Department of State Services.

According to him, the ministry had also participated in strategic meetings in Abuja aimed at strengthening security around schools and other educational institutions, particularly against threats capable of disrupting academic activities.

Ala said the government was also strengthening community-based surveillance through School-Based Management Committees, Parent-Teacher Associations and vigilante groups across the local government areas.

“We are working with our SBMCs, with our PTA, in fact with the vigilante groups in the various local governments,” he said.

He urged the groups to conduct coordinated surveillance visits to schools, adding that vigilante personnel had been encouraged to maintain a visible presence around schools, particularly in communities where students commute from surrounding villages.

This, he said, would enable security intervention to be activated quickly whenever an alarm was raised.

The commissioner clarified that although the state government had identified some local government areas as relatively safe, security remained principally a federal responsibility, making compliance with the directive on school closures imperative.

On allegations regarding the feeding of students in boarding schools, Ala dismissed claims that principals were being given funds to feed students, describing the reports as inaccurate.

“There is no principal that is giving any money. The money is paid to the contractors,” he said.

He explained that contractors engaged by the state government supplied food to schools on a rotational weekly basis, adding that the arrangement was supervised by a committee established by the governor to ensure accountability, transparency and compliance with approved standards.

“The contractors are being rotated among the schools so that you don’t become so used to the food,” he said.

Ala also disclosed that the ministry had intensified health and disease prevention measures in schools through its Health Coordinator and collaboration with the State Ministry of Health.

He said the government had taken steps to address diphtheria and other communicable diseases, adding that drugs were supplied to principals of girls’ schools last year as part of efforts to strengthen school health services.

According to him, school supervision had also been expanded to cover 30 key performance indicators, including sanitation, hygiene and other conditions required for a safe and conducive learning environment.

On transportation, the commissioner said the state government had deployed free buses to convey students within the metropolis and those travelling from surrounding communities.

“The buses are free of charge, within the town and outside. Every morning we send them to bring students. By 2 o’clock, the buses will convey them back to their respective villages or bus stops,” he said.

Ala maintained that the government’s overriding objective was to ensure that the resumption of academic activities did not expose students to avoidable security risks.

He assured parents and other stakeholders that the government would continue to monitor the security situation and respond to directives from the relevant authorities before extending the resumption arrangement to schools currently under closure.

World.title: Ogun 2027: Adeola, Hunye clash over Ekiti origin claim
World.content:
…prove my Ekiti origin claim or face legal action

…we welcome the lawsuit — Hunye

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Ogun State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Senator Solomon Adeola, has given Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, chieftain, Abayomi Hunye, and Ambassador Folake Marcus-Bello 24 hours to produce evidence to substantiate their claims that he is of Ekiti State origin or face legal action.

Adeola issued the ultimatum through his Media Adviser, Chief Kayode Odunaro, following separate appearances by Hunye and Marcus-Bello on programmes aired by Channels Television.

According to a statement by Odunaro, the two politicians allegedly claimed during their television appearances that Adeola was originally from Ekiti State, among other allegations, without providing evidence to substantiate the claims.

Adeola described the allegations as false and defamatory, challenging his accusers to produce documentary evidence to support their claims.

“I watched in utter disbelief as these characters that I hardly know utter assertive and outrageous lies about my origin without any proof,” Adeola said.

“One falsely claimed on TV that I am from Ekiti and, when asked where exactly in Ekiti, went blank and could not provide an answer.

“The other one was lying about the locations of the graves of my parents as if she was part of the undertakers at the burial, all in a futile effort to justify an unsustainable falsehood.

“Enough is enough. They should produce their evidence in 24 hours or be ready for my lawsuits,” he added.

Adeola’s camp alleged that claims about his purported Ekiti origin had previously been deployed as a political campaign strategy to frustrate his emergence as senator representing Ogun West Senatorial District.

The statement said the allegations did not stop Adeola from winning the 2023 National Assembly election, adding that he secured what it described as massive support from voters across the senatorial district.

It further alleged that the controversy had resurfaced against the backdrop of Adeola’s ambition to contest the 2027 Ogun State governorship election on the APC platform.

Odunaro maintained that the latest allegations were part of an attempt to undermine Adeola’s political aspiration ahead of the election.

However, Hunye welcomed Adeola’s threat of legal action, saying he was prepared to meet the senator in court and had documentary evidence to support his position.

In a statement issued through his Media Adviser, Femi Oyewale, Hunye said the threat of a lawsuit was welcome, while alleging that the issue concerning Adeola’s ancestry was already before a court.

“We are more than ready to meet Senator Adeola in a court of competent jurisdiction,” Hunye said.

“Interestingly, it seems they are not well informed that the matter is already in court. Threatening us with a lawsuit, therefore, is like a political jamboree designed to make noise in the public.”

Hunye accused Adeola’s camp of attempting to intimidate critics and divert attention from questions surrounding the senator’s ancestry and eligibility to govern Ogun State.

“For far too long, the political space in Ogun West has been subjected to intimidation, high-handedness, and the suppression of truth through propaganda and sponsored brickbats,” he alleged.

He argued that questions surrounding a political candidate’s origin and eligibility were matters of public interest rather than private issues.

“The issue of a candidate’s origin and eligibility is a matter of constitutional concern, not a private affair,” Hunye said.

“It touches on the integrity of our democratic institutions and the aspirations of the good people of Ogun State, who deserve a leader whose roots and allegiance are indisputably local.”

Hunye also maintained that truth would constitute a defence against a libel action, urging Adeola to approach the court if he believed the allegations were defamatory.

“We wish to remind the Senator and his media handlers that truth is an absolute defence against libel,” he said.

“Rather than engaging in empty threats and grandstanding on national television, Senator Adeola should save his energy and approach the court immediately.”

Hunye said he would not be intimidated by the threat of litigation, promising to present what he described as “robust, verifiable facts and documentary evidence” to substantiate the claims concerning Adeola’s alleged Ekiti ancestry.

“The courtroom is where evidence is tested, not the pages of newspapers or sponsored broadcast interviews,” he said.

He urged residents of Ogun State, particularly those in Ogun West, to remain calm, saying the matter would ultimately be determined on the basis of evidence.

“We are prepared to strip bare all falsehoods in the open court of law, where facts, not political titles, will speak,” Hunye added.

World.title: Lagos 2027: Rhodes-Vivour questions Hamzat’s eligibility over US allegiance
World.content:
Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Lagos State, has questioned the eligibility of Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat to contest the 2027 governorship election, citing his alleged oath of allegiance to the United States.

Rhodes-Vivour raised the issue on Tuesday while appearing on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily, recalling the controversy surrounding Hamzat’s eligibility during the 2023 governorship election.

He said his legal team had relied on the alleged US oath while challenging Hamzat’s qualification, arguing that a Nigerian public office holder should not simultaneously owe allegiance to another country.

“We focused on the fact that this current person that wants to contest for governor, deputy governor, swore an oath of allegiance to another country,” Rhodes-Vivour said.

“Constitutionally, that is one of the number one reasons to dismiss a candidate or dismiss somebody that emerges as the governor.”

During the 2023 election petition proceedings, Olubusayo Fasidi, an immigration lawyer, had testified before the Lagos State Governorship Election Petition Tribunal that Hamzat applied for US naturalisation and took an oath of allegiance to the country.

Fasidi, however, told the tribunal that she was invited to explain US immigration law and was not familiar with Nigeria’s constitutional provisions on dual citizenship.

Rhodes-Vivour also criticised the conduct of the 2023 election, alleging incidents of violence and intimidation across the state.

He said Nigerians should elect public officials whose loyalty is exclusively to the country.

The ADC candidate further argued that Hamzat could have publicly renounced any alleged US allegiance before seeking elective office, citing former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson as an example.

Meanwhile, President Bola Tinubu has endorsed Hamzat as the APC candidate for the Lagos governorship election.

World.title: ASUU-LASU declares indefinite strike
World.content:
By Elizabeth Osayande

LAGOS — The Lagos State University branch of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU-LASU) has declared a total and indefinite strike over what it described as the failure of the government to implement the 2025 ASUU/FGN Agreement.

The union announced the decision on Tuesday, September 15, following a congress at which members resolved to commence the industrial action.

In a statement signed by the Secretary of the ASUU-LASU Steering Committee, Comrade Thanny Nooem, and the Coordinator, Comrade Oluwaseun Babalola, the union said the decision followed months of what it described as “patient and constructive engagement” with the government without a resolution of the issues in dispute.

“This unfortunate and avoidable action has become necessary due to the continued failure of the Government to address the Union’s longstanding agitation over the implementation of the 2025 ASUU/FGN Agreement,” the statement said.

ASUU-LASU said it was seeking the “full domestication and implementation of the 2025 ASUU/FGN Agreement” as a condition for resolving the dispute.

“The strike shall be total and comprehensive until there is a satisfactory resolution of the issues in dispute,” the union said.

The union expressed regret over the development, saying previous efforts to resolve the matter through engagement had not produced the desired outcome.

The industrial action is expected to affect teaching and other academic activities at Lagos State University, including its Ojo campus and other campuses, pending further developments.

The union ended its statement with the slogan: “Aluta continua, victoria ascerta.”

World.title: Court denies Odogwu Asaba bail
World.content:
By Egufe Yafugborhi

ASABA — The Delta State High Court has declined the bail application filed on behalf of Mr Ifeanyi Ogbonna, popularly known as Odogwu Asaba, who is facing allegations relating to the death of late Favour Agbro.

The ruling was delivered on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, following arguments by counsel on the defendant’s bail application.

The court ordered that Ogbonna remain in custody at the Ogwashi-Uku Maximum Correctional Centre and directed the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) to file the Information within 14 days.

According to a statement by the defendant’s counsel, Triple O and C Chambers, the court declined the application at this stage, noting concerns relating to the applicant’s safety and possible public reaction, while the Information was yet to be filed by the DPP.

The court, however, held that the defendant would be at liberty to apply for bail after the Information had been filed.

Counsel to Ogbonna, Ugochukwu Okoli, N.N. Onuzurike and C.S. Chukwudolue, appeared for the applicant, while Dr R.O. Ishiguzo, a law officer with the Nigeria Police Force, State CID, Asaba, represented the respondent, the State Commissioner of Police/complainant.

The development was also confirmed by Awele Ideal, counsel representing Favour’s family on a pro bono basis.

In an update, Ideal said the bail application was argued and that the court subsequently ruled against granting bail to Ogbonna.

She said she remained committed to representing Favour’s family and providing legal services on a pro bono basis.

Reacting to the ruling, Comrade Deo, a human rights advocate involved in the campaign for justice for Favour, described the development as “a reminder that justice is a process.”

He commended Ideal for representing Favour’s family and opposing the bail application.

Deo also alleged that activists had worked with the police in efforts that led to Ogbonna’s arrest in Asaba after monitoring his movements.

However, he stressed that the refusal of bail did not amount to a conviction.

“The refusal of bail is not a conviction, and the allegations against the accused remain allegations until determined by the court,” he said.

The case will proceed with the filing of the Information by the DPP, after which Ogbonna may renew his bail application.

Ogbonna remains presumed innocent unless and until proved guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction.END

World.title: 2027: Ex-Nasarawa Speaker begs defectors to return to APC
World.content:
The immediate past Speaker, Nasarawa State House of Assembly, Alhaji Ibrahim Balarabe, has appealed to all aggrieved members who defected from the All Progressives Congress (APC) to other parties to return to the party.

He said the appeal became imperative in view of the fact that they laboured to build a house, only to vacate it “at the time you need it most.”

The former speaker made the call in an interview with newsmen in Lafia on Tuesday.

Balarabe’s call followed the recent defection of the immediate past Chairman of Toto Local Government Area, Aliyu Abdullahi, from the APC.

The News Agency of Nigeria recalls that on September 14, the former chairman announced his resignation from the ruling APC.

The former speaker advocated for calm among APC members in Toto local government area.

Balarabe, who disagreed with the move by the former chairman, enjoined him to set aside whatever grievances and opt for dialogue, to resolve their differences amicably.

He also urged him to withdraw the resignation letter earlier issued and return to the APC.

“You cannot leave the house you have built for another person to inherit.

“APC is our home, it is our party, and our victory is assured by the will of Allah. We will get there. We will deliver our LGA In-Sha-Allah, come 2027.

“We cannot fold our hands and watch our party lose its members. We cannot fold our hands and allow our people to leave.

“In politics, everyone matters. The grassroots matter because politics is local, this is a fact,” Balarabe said.

The former speaker observed that success of APC as a party in the area come 2027, solidly depends on the unity and peace among the party members in the area.

“Unity of purpose is paramount for the task ahead of us, and no matter what, we must unite our people to facilitate victory in 2027,” he added.

World.title: NAF takes delivery of five new helicopters
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has taken delivery of five new helicopters as the Federal Government intensifies efforts to modernise and re-equip the Armed Forces to confront evolving security threats.

The newly acquired platforms comprise three AW-109 Trekker B helicopters manufactured by Leonardo Helicopters of Italy and two H-125 helicopters produced by Airbus Helicopters.

A statement by the NAF Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, said the acquisition was part of the Federal Government’s sustained investment in strengthening the operational capabilities of the service.

Ejodame said the three AW-109 Trekker B helicopters arrived in Lagos on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, as part of a batch of 10 recently acquired by the Federal Government.

He said the remaining seven helicopters were expected to be delivered before the end of 2026.

The two H-125 helicopters had earlier been delivered to the NAF, bringing the total number of helicopters covered by the latest acquisition to five.

Reacting to the development, the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, described the acquisition as another milestone in the Federal Government’s ongoing investment in the modernisation and re-equipment of the NAF.

Aneke said the arrival of the helicopters would increase aircraft availability and give commanders greater flexibility in deploying airpower in support of ongoing military operations across the country.

According to him, the new platforms would particularly strengthen the NAF’s ability to provide timely air support to ground troops operating in challenging environments.

“The arrival of these five helicopters provides greater flexibility in the employment of airpower in support of ground troops in ongoing operations,” he said.

The Air Chief expressed appreciation to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for his continued support for the transformation and modernisation of the NAF.

Aneke said the Federal Government’s investment was enabling the service to progressively develop the capabilities required to meet its operational responsibilities and respond to Nigeria’s evolving security challenges.

He said the three AW-109 Trekker B helicopters would significantly boost the NAF’s rotary-wing capabilities.

He added that the platforms would enhance the service’s capacity for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), close air support, armed escort and combat search and rescue, as well as other joint missions in support of ground forces.

“The versatility of the AW-109 platform is expected to provide commanders with additional options for rapidly deploying air assets in support of troops engaged in counter-terrorism, counter-insurgency and other internal security operations,” Aneke said.

He said the helicopters would also improve the NAF’s ability to respond to emerging threats, particularly where speed, mobility and sustained aerial support were critical to ground operations.

According to him, the two H-125 helicopters would complement the AW-109s by providing versatile light-helicopter capabilities for various operational requirements.

The NAF said the platforms would collectively expand its flexibility and capacity to respond to changing operational demands, including moving personnel and equipment, conducting surveillance and supporting joint forces operating in difficult-to-reach areas.

Helicopters Undergoing Assembly

The NAF said the newly delivered platforms were undergoing post-delivery assembly and other technical processes ahead of their formal induction and operational deployment.

The process, it added, would include crew-readiness and technical preparations required to ensure that the helicopters were fully prepared for operational employment.

Aneke stressed that the NAF’s responsibility went beyond acquiring new platforms, noting that the service must ensure that the Federal Government’s investment translated into measurable operational results.

He said the service would continue to prioritise effective employment, maintenance and logistics sustainment to ensure maximum availability of the aircraft.

“We will continue to prioritise effective employment, maintenance and logistics sustainment so that every aircraft delivered adds measurable value to ongoing operations and the protection of the lives and property of Nigerians,” he said.

The acquisition comes as the Armed Forces continue operations against terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other security threats across multiple theatres.

The NAF said the additional rotary-wing capacity would strengthen support for joint forces by improving the speed, reach and effectiveness of air support available to troops on the ground.

The new helicopters are expected to enhance operational mobility, surveillance and responsiveness while supporting ground forces in their efforts to counter terrorists and other criminal elements.

With the remaining seven AW-109 Trekker B helicopters expected before the end of 2026, the NAF is set to further expand its rotary-wing fleet and strengthen its capacity to provide air support for joint military operations.

World.title: Nigeria: Global Recognition Signals Investor Confidence
World.content:
Nume Ekeghe

writes on the growing international recognition of Nigeria’s economic reforms, as the country records a string of positive signals from global financial institutions, investors and rating agencies, raising hopes that the difficult policy adjustments of the past three years are beginning to translate into stronger investor confidence

For an economy that spent years struggling to convince investors that it could provide a predictable environment for capital, Nigeria is beginning to receive an unusual form of validation: the outside world is starting to change its assessment. The evidence is coming from different directions.

For instance, FTSE Russell recently announced that it is restoring Nigeria to its Frontier Market classification after the country was pushed into “Unclassified” status in 2023 over concerns about foreign exchange liquidity and investors’ ability to repatriate capital.

Also, J.P. Morgan has admitted Nigerian government bonds into its new Government Bond Index–Emerging Markets Edge, potentially opening the door to billions of dollars in benchmark-linked investment.

Earlier this year, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) removed Nigeria from its grey list after the country addressed deficiencies in its anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing framework.

The European Union subsequently removed Nigeria from its list of high-risk third countries for money laundering and terrorist financing.

The three major international rating agencies Fitch, Moody’s and S&P have also moved in a more favourable direction, with S&P upgrading Nigeria to B, Fitch affirming its B rating with a stable outlook and Moody’s revising its outlook to positive.

Then there is the more mundane but perhaps more telling evidence: foreign exchange is becoming easier to access, Nigerian naira cards are working abroad again, banks are raising international spending limits, reserves have climbed above $54 billion and diaspora remittances are approaching the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) $1 billion monthly target.

Taken together, these developments suggest something bigger than a collection of isolated policy announcements. They suggest that Nigeria’s economic reforms are beginning to produce the one outcome that policymakers have been seeking since 2023, confidence.

Reform Architecture

One distinguishing feature of the Bola Tinubu administration’s economic programme is that the key policymakers arrived with a clear diagnosis of the country’s problems.

The reforms were painful because they targeted some of the most entrenched distortions in the economy: fuel subsidy, multiple exchange rates, monetary financing of fiscal deficits, weak public finances and undercapitalised banks.

Government sources volunteered that the objective was not simply to make Nigeria look better to international investors. “It was to make the economy function differently. That distinction is important,” said a government official who do not want his name in print.

Recently, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), in its 2026 Article IV assessment, said sustained reforms since 2023 including ending fuel subsidies and deficit monetisation, tightening monetary policy and liberalising the exchange rate had strengthened macro-economic stability, rebuilt external buffers and improved foreign exchange market functioning. It also noted that portfolio inflows had resumed and Nigeria had regained access to international markets.

Former Finance Minister Wale Edun was similarly emphatic when he represented Nigeria at the IMF and World Bank Spring Meetings.

“The overall message from the Spring Meetings is encouraging. Nigeria’s global economic standing is improving. Our reform story is being taken seriously and indeed used as an example. Our resilience is better understood, and our investment case is strengthened, with confidence returning at a faster pace,” Edun said.

CBN Monetary Reset

At the centre of the adjustment has been the CBN’s return to orthodox monetary policy. The CBN under the leadership of Olayemi Cardoso inherited an economy in which foreign exchange shortages, multiple exchange rates, monetary financing and weak confidence had become mutually reinforcing.

The response was to allow the FX market to become more market-driven, tighten monetary conditions, improve transparency and rebuild the central bank’s credibility.

The process was expensive. Interest rates rose sharply and the naira initially weakened substantially. But the CBN’s argument was that restoring price and currency stability required breaking with the previous policy framework.

Cardoso has consistently linked the monetary reforms to investor confidence.

Speaking recently, he pointed to the change in Nigeria’s external position as evidence of the progress made.

“Anybody that wants to argue about what the impact of these reforms have been, go and look at the results,” he said, pointing to the dramatic improvement in reserves and the strengthening of the external buffer.

He added that reserves had reached around 10 months of import cover, noting that these were precisely the indicators international investors examined before taking positions in a currency.

“Doing this consistently is what is giving confidence to not just internal stakeholders, but those who also operate internationally,” Cardoso said.

The governor’s point is increasingly visible in the FX market.

The reforms have not eliminated volatility, but they have substantially reduced the distortion between official and parallel markets. The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of Economy, Dr Taiwo Oyedele recently noted that the premium, which had once exceeded 60 per cent, was now below five per cent.

Return of the Dollar

Perhaps the most practical evidence of the reform dividend is that foreign exchange is becoming less difficult to obtain.

For years, the problem was not merely that the naira was weak. It was that dollars were frequently unavailable through official channels.

That affected businesses, airlines, foreign investors and ordinary Nigerians travelling or paying for services overseas.

The improvement in liquidity is now being felt by consumers.

Nigerian banks have expanded international transactions on naira cards, while some have raised spending limits. Cardoso recently offered a remarkably simple description of the change.

Cardoso while speaking at the BusinessDay CEO Forum recently said: “When you travel today, you go with your naira card. It works. It has brought back the way the outside world looks at us. In the past, you go there, the card doesn’t work. Can’t pay for your goods. They look at your naira card. They throw it back at you. Not any longer.”

For the ordinary Nigerian, that may appear like a banking convenience. For investors, it is evidence that the country’s foreign exchange and payment infrastructure is functioning more normally.

Reserves, Remittances and External Buffer

The stronger FX market has coincided with a dramatic improvement in reserves.

Nigeria’s gross external reserves reached $54.48 billion on the 11th of September, up more than $12 billion from a year earlier.

Cardoso has also pointed to the changing structure of FX inflows, particularly diaspora remittances.

The CBN governor has repeatedly said Nigeria was targeting monthly remittance inflows of $1 billion, noting that the country had already made significant progress towards that goal with July recording $947 million inflow. The significance is larger than the dollars themselves.

Nigeria is gradually replacing an environment where foreign currency was scarce and heavily rationed with one where inflows are increasingly being captured through formal channels. That again is precisely the kind of market infrastructure investors want to see.

Most Underrated Reform

Meanwhile, market watchers stressed that if FTSE Russell and J.P. Morgan represent recognition from the capital markets, Nigeria’s exit from the FATF grey list represents recognition from the global financial system.

Nigeria was removed from the FATF list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring in October 2025 after demonstrating progress on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing reforms. FATF specifically cited improvements in risk assessment, financial-sector supervision, beneficial ownership information, financial intelligence, investigations and prosecutions.

The significance is considerable. Cardoso said Nigeria’s grey-listing had potentially cost the economy more than $30 billion in capital inflows, based on the historical impact of grey-listing on capital flows.

“Exiting the list therefore signals a major restoration of confidence and eases compliance frictions for correspondent banks,” he said.

The subsequent removal from the EU’s high-risk AML/CFT list reinforced that message.

For banks and international investors, analysts believe lower compliance friction means lower transaction costs and fewer obstacles to cross-border financial activity. It is therefore another piece of the investor-confidence puzzle.

Reopening the Door

The changing view of Nigeria is perhaps most obvious in the capital market. Nigeria’s return to the FTSE Russell Frontier Market Index, effective September 21, reverses its 2023 exit, which was largely linked to challenges around FX liquidity and investors’ ability to move their money out of the country.

Commenting on the development, Oyedele said the return was about more than just being back on the index. J.P. Morgan’s latest decision strengthens the case.

Nigeria has been assigned a 7.40 per cent weighting in the new GBI-EM Edge index, translating to roughly $17.47 billion of eligible Nigerian government debt.

Oyedele described the inclusion as “a clear, independent endorsement” of the reform agenda and said it reflected the confidence international capital markets now place in Nigeria’s economic management.

The $17.5 billion is not guaranteed new investment. Rather, it represents the eligible Nigerian debt corresponding to the country’s index weighting, with benchmark-tracking funds expected to adjust their portfolios over time.

But even that potential matters. It means Nigeria is once again positioning itself to benefit from institutional capital that was previously constrained by market-access concerns.

Oyedele, was also quoted to have said the inclusion was an independent validation of Nigeria’s ongoing economic reforms.

Oyedele stated, “This inclusion is a clear, independent endorsement of the discipline behind President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s reform agenda. It reflects the confidence international capital markets now place in Nigeria’s economic management, and it lowers the cost of financing our development priorities. We remain focused on the work still required to earn full reinstatement in JP Morgan’s flagship index.”

Rebuilding Banking System

The reform story is not confined to FX and capital markets.

The banking sector recapitalisation programme has also delivered a significant result. 33 of Nigeria’s 37 banks had met the new capital requirements, raising approximately N4.65 trillion in fresh capital.

For Cardoso, whose monetary-policy agenda depends heavily on a stable financial system, stronger bank balance sheets are essential. Analysts agree that a better-capitalised banking system is more capable of absorbing shocks, supporting credit growth and financing the investment cycle that policymakers ultimately want to create.

Ratings Agencies Take Note

The changing perception is also reflected in Nigeria’s sovereign ratings. S&P upgraded Nigeria to B from B- in May, while Fitch retained its B rating with a stable outlook and Moody’s revised its outlook to positive from stable, citing stronger reserves and improved economic resilience.

While the challenges remain, the direction is clear: Nigeria’s credit story is improving. Even S&P Global’s decision to acquire a majority stake in Agusto & Co. adds to the growing international interest in Nigeria’s financial markets.

Hard Part Begins

There is, however, an important caveat. Investor confidence is not the same thing as household prosperity.

Nigeria still faces high living costs, inflationary pressures, elevated interest rates, weak purchasing power and deep structural challenges. The administration itself acknowledges that macroeconomic stability is only the first stage.

Oyedele recently said the government’s next challenge was to translate the gains from stabilisation into shared prosperity.

That is the test that will determine whether the reform programme becomes a lasting economic transformation rather than simply a successful stabilisation exercise.

For now, though, the evidence is increasingly compelling.

The FATF grey-list exit shows that Nigeria’s financial system is becoming more trusted. The EU delisting shows that the improvement is recognised beyond the African financial system.

FTSE’s return shows that international equity investors can once again access the Nigerian market under its Frontier Market classification. J.P. Morgan’s inclusion shows that Nigerian government securities are becoming relevant again to global benchmark investors.

The rating upgrades show that sovereign risk is being reassessed.

The stronger reserves and rising remittances show that the external position has improved.

And the return of international functionality to naira cards provides perhaps the simplest everyday illustration of all.

Three years ago, the reform debate was largely about whether Nigeria could endure the pain.

Today, the question is increasingly about how Nigeria converts the resulting stability into investment, production, jobs and prosperity. What is clear is that the reforms are beginning to yield the international recognition and investor confidence the government sought.

World.title: Insurance Commissioner Urges Insurers to See Trust as Valuable Asset
World.content:
Ebere Nwoji

The Commissioner for Insurance, Mr Ayo Omosehin, has urged insurance professionals to see trust as insurance industry’s most valuable asset.

Omosehin who stated this at the 2026 Insurance Professional’s forum organised by the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria( CIIN), in Abeokuta, Ogun State, said no amount of capital, technology, or regulation could compensate for a deficit of trust.

He said this reality has placed an enormous responsibility on insurers, intermediaries, regulators, and professional bodies alike.

According to him, strong governance, ethical leadership, transparency, accountability, fair market conduct, and prompt claims settlement are not merely regulatory requirements but foundations upon which public confidence is built.

He said the establishment of the insurance Policyholders’ Protection Fund under NIIRA 2025 has further strengthened this confidence by providing an additional safety net in situations involving insurer distress.

He however said the regulator’s ultimate objective remained preventive rather than reactive. “Effective supervision, prudent risk management, and sound corporate governance must always serve as the first line of defence against institutional failure”, Omosehin stated.

He described insurance as a strategic instrument for economic stability and not just financial service.

He further described insurance as the institutional mechanism through which societies transform uncertainty into confidence and convert vulnerability into resilience. “The economics of risk and the social value of insurance at its essence, shows that risk represents uncertainty regarding future outcomes”, Omosehin stated.

World.title: Smart Stewards Targets SME Funding, Wealth Inequality at Summit
World.content:
Mary Nnah

Financial education organisation Smart Stewards will convene more than 3,000 entrepreneurs, investors and professionals in Maryland, Lagos on Saturday, 19 September 2026 for its 11th Annual Summit, ELEVATE 2026.

The gathering comes amid rising inflation, business closures and widening wealth inequality that continue to erode Nigeria’s middle class.

Organisers said economic uncertainty is forcing Nigerians to rethink how they earn, invest and preserve wealth. ELEVATE 2026 will shift the conversation from short-term income to building assets, businesses and financial systems capable of creating value over the long term.

The programme will provide practical insights on earning, saving, investing and building sustainable wealth in a volatile economy.

Speaking ahead of the event, Founder and Lead Coach of Smart Stewards, Sola Adesakin, said the summit is about access as much as information.

“We have never believed that information alone builds wealth. Wealth is built through capacity, through connection, and through access to the right rooms and the right capital. That is what ELEVATE is: a room where founders, investors and everyday builders stand shoulder to shoulder, and where a wealth dynasty stops being an idea and starts becoming a plan. This economy will shake many things. It should not be able to shake what we build together.”

World.title: Ingentia Energies’ Crude Oil Production Soars 150%, Unveils Growth Strategy
World.content:
Ejiofor Alike

The Board of Directors of Ingentia Energies Limited has lauded the outgone Interim Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Charles Odita, for his transformational leadership, which increased production by an impressive 150 per cent, reflecting the success of the company’s operational and growth strategies.

This commendation is coming as the new Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Victor Agbaroji unveiled a strategic agenda focused on strengthening and moving Ingentia Energies further into the top percentile of key players in the oil and gas sector.

In a letter signed by the Chairman of the Board, Chief Oseni Elamah, following a meeting in Lagos attended by both the incoming and outgoing chief executives, the Board described Odita’s tenure as a defining period in the Company’s evolution.

The board noted that under Odita’s stewardship, Ingentia Energies increased production by an impressive 150 per cent.

The board extended heartfelt congratulations and profound appreciation to Odita, describing his tenure as transformational, and characterised by strategic clarity, decisive execution and exceptional leadership.

Meanwhile, as he takes over the reins of leadership, Agbaroji has expressed appreciation for the achievements recorded under Odita and pledged to build upon the solid foundation already established.

He identified key priorities for the next phase of the company’s growth, including enhancing drilling operations, maximising the value of existing assets, improving cost competitiveness, expanding the company’s portfolio, and unlocking greater value from the asset’s gas resources.

“Our immediate focus is to strengthen the next phase of our drilling campaign by leveraging the seismic acquisition programme currently underway. This will enable us to execute a more robust and efficient drilling programme while improving exploration outcomes and operational performance,” Agbaroji said.

He also highlighted the importance of crude oil evacuation infrastructure in supporting future production growth, noting that the Company would further intensify efforts to advance its pipeline evacuation project.

World.title: ASIS Organisers Establish Africa Social Impact Network
World.content:
Nume Ekeghe

The organisers of the Africa Social Impact Summit (ASIS) have established the Africa Social Impact Network (ASIN), a pan-African platform designed to extend the impact of the annual summit by driving year-round partnerships, financing, knowledge exchange and development action across the continent.

The announcement followed the conclusion of the fifth Africa Social Impact Summit (ASIS 2026), held in Lagos in recently under the theme, “Financing for Development: Building Resilience and Transforming Emerging Economies.”

The summit brought together governments, development institutions, businesses, investors, philanthropies, academia and civil society to advance practical conversations and partnerships around Africa’s development priorities.

The establishment of ASIN marks a new phase in the evolution of ASIS, which over the past five years has grown into a major platform for multi-stakeholder engagement on sustainable development and economic transformation. According to the organisers, the network will serve as a permanent platform for policy dialogue, domestic and international capital mobilisation, strategic partnerships, innovation, research and the implementation of high-impact initiatives.

World.title: Ziba Unveils Development in Lagos, Introduces Loft-style Overwater Stays
World.content:
Sunday Ehigiator

Ziba, Nigeria’s first over-water resort, has unveiled Phase 3 of its development in Lagos, introducing larger Grand Overwater Rooms, loft-style overwater accommodation and a dedicated wellness centre.

The latest expansion, unveiled over the weekend, is aimed at further positioning the resort as a destination for luxury tourism and wellness while showcasing locally developed hospitality experiences.

Speaking at the unveiling, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Ziba, Tricia Olufemi, said the expansion marked a significant milestone for the resort and Nigeria’s hospitality industry.

He said, “Nigeria’s first over-water resort just got bigger. Today is a milestone. We’re taking the over-water experience we pioneered to a whole new level with larger Grand Overwater Rooms, the first-ever loft-style overwater stays in Nigeria, and a dedicated wellness centre. This is about proving that world-class luxury escapes don’t have to mean leaving Nigeria.

“When we started Ziba, people asked if an over-water resort could work in Lagos. We believed it could. Lagos deserves destinations that match its energy and ambition. We’re not importing a concept. We’re building a Nigerian luxury story.”

According to the resort, the new Grand Overwater Rooms provide larger spaces and expansive views, targeting couples, families and guests seeking accommodation directly over the water.

The loft-style accommodation features double-height ceilings and represents what Ziba described as the first of its kind among overwater stays in Nigeria. The expansion also includes a dedicated wellness centre offering spa, recovery and relaxation facilities.

Olufemi said the development demonstrated the potential of Nigerian creativity and hospitality to compete internationally.

World.title: Dangote Refinery IPO: i-invest Expands Digital Access for Retail Investors
World.content:
Nume Ekeghe

The opening of the Dangote Refinery public offer is giving retail investors another avenue to participate in the ownership of one of Africa’s largest industrial assets, with digital investment platform i-invest providing access to the offer through its app.

The public offer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE opened on September 14, 2026, with 4.1 billion ordinary shares being offered at N525 per share. If fully subscribed, the offer is expected to raise about N2.15 trillion.

For retail investors, the minimum subscription is 10 shares, requiring an investment of N5,250. Subsequent applications are to be made in multiples of 10 shares.

The structure of the offer, alongside the availability of digital subscription channels, could broaden participation in what is expected to be one of Nigeria’s most closely watched equity offerings.

i-invest, powered by Parthian, allows eligible investors to access the Dangote Refinery offer alongside other investment products available on the platform, including fixed-income investments, savings and equities.

Rather than relying solely on conventional subscription processes, investors using the platform can complete their application digitally after meeting the required account and regulatory conditions.

To participate, investors need to have their i-invest account and Know Your Customer details completed, including their BVN and other required information.

A Central Securities Clearing System account is also required for the electronic holding of shares. For eligible customers, i-invest provides a CSCS account through the platform, subject to approval.

Once the account is ready and funded, investors can access the Dangote Refinery offer, select the number of shares they wish to purchase, review the subscription details and submit their application.

At the offer price of N525, the 10-share minimum translates to N5,250, providing a relatively low entry point for individuals seeking exposure to the company.

The digital access comes as retail participation in Nigeria’s capital market continues to evolve, with investment platforms increasingly providing individuals with ways to access securities without depending entirely on traditional physical processes.

However, the ease of subscribing does not remove the investment risks associated with the offer.

The Dangote Refinery offer is an equity investment and the value of the shares may rise or fall after listing. Dividends are not guaranteed, while investors could lose part or all of their investment.

Investors are therefore expected to study the prospectus and other offer documents before making a decision. Those requiring additional guidance can also consult their stockbroker or financial adviser.

The offer is scheduled to close on October 13, 2026, subject to the applicable terms of the offer.

For retail investors considering the Dangote Refinery offer, i-invest’s digital channel provides an additional means of accessing the subscription, as the capital market seeks to widen participation beyond traditional investment channels.

World.title: FG Expands TETFund ICT Experience Centres to 15 More Institutions, Inaugurates KWASU Facility
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Federal Government has announced plans to expand its TETFund/Renewed Hope Initiative ICT Experience Centre programme to 15 additional tertiary institutions across the country as part of efforts to equip Nigerian youths with digital skills.

The disclosure was made on Tuesday by the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, during the inauguration of the ICT Experience Centre at Kwara State University, KWASU, Malete. She was represented by the wife of the Vice-President, Hajia Nana Shettima.

According to the First Lady, construction is already ongoing in Adamawa, Bayelsa, Borno, Delta, Edo, Enugu, Imo, Katsina, Nasarawa, Niger, Ondo, Osun, Rivers, Yobe and Zamfara States.

“The centre we are commissioning today represents opportunity, innovation, knowledge and hope for the future of young people in Kwara State and beyond,” she stated.

The KWASU facility, she explained, is a modern technology hub equipped with ICT laboratories, interactive digital displays, conference facilities and exhibition spaces to drive learning, creativity, research and technological advancement.

She noted that KWASU was one of six institutions selected for the pilot phase, with one centre in each geopolitical zone. Other centres have already been insugurated, while those at Kaduna State University and Taraba State University will be inaugurated soon.

Also speaking, TETFund Executive Secretary, Mr. Sonny Echono represented by Director of Monitoring and Evaluation, Olajide Babatunde, said the board approved N1 billion for each centre across the six zones.

Echono said the centres are designed to train students and lecturers in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics and software development, and to expose them to applications in security, agriculture, healthcare, media and mining.

He described the KWASU centre as one of the foremost ICT facilities in the country and the third to be inaugurated in 2026.

He called on the university management to ensure proper maintenance and regular upgrades.

World.title: Gayton slammed over ‘tone-deaf’ tweet amid GBV crisis
World.content:
Minister Gayton McKenzie has been criticised over his comments amid a GBV crisis. Images via X

Gayton McKenzie has been criticised over a “tone deaf” tweet in which he commended himself for bringing Chris Brown – who has a long history of sexual and physical violence allegations against women – to South Africa in 2024. This comes amid heightened gender-based violence concerns, particularly related to the murders of eight women near the Kempton Park area.

The Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture also engaged with a fiery back-and-forth with media personality Bonang Matheba on his X account.

GAYTON MCKENZIE LABELLED ‘TONE-DEAF’ OVER CHRIS BROWN TWEET

On Tuesday, 15 September, Gayton McKenzie trended on X over his back-and-forth tweets with media personality Bonang Matheba, who called the minister out over a lack of funding for South African artists.



Gaytona argued that through his cabinet, he had made a significant impact.

He tweeted: “The Chris Brown concert created the biggest job opportunities for young people in SA who were considered to be unemployable. It was the first time some received a salary. My job as Minister is always to make things easy for our promoters to bring big-name artists to SA”.

The Minister’s mention of the US artist, who has not only been convicted of felony assault in a domestic-violence case, but also linked to multiple other domestic and physical assault charges, sparked backlash online.

In the comments section, Gayton was inundated with complaints about his “tone-deaf” post.

Here’s what a few had to say…

@Maa_Mshengu: “Are you aware we are currently dealing with a GBV crisis at the moment? Read the room!”



@FaithPale: “You can’t be applauding an abuser, during a GBV crisis. Ooh, wow!”

@blackonees7: “Using Chris Brown at this stage where our beloved country cries over 8 women who had been brutally murdered is such a shame!. All your motivational talks and swindling won’t get you out of this one! Pathetic”

@Ol_etilwe: “Boasting about bringing a GBV perpetrator, mind you”.

I hate Gayton McKenzie, yerrr, he is so tone deaf. pic.twitter.com/3af4asDytI — MaBarçaUnited44⁷🇿🇦 (@ParkJimins_toof) September 15, 2026

‘LET’S HAVE FUN’

Chris Brown performed in South Africa in December 2024, just days after the 16 Days of Activism campaign ended. This came after the broadcast of an Investigation Discovery documentary titled Chris Brown: A History of Violence.

At the time, anti-GBV activists like Women For Change called on the Department of Home Affairs to revoke his visa ahead of the show. Chris seemingly taunted the bid with a jab at the organisation.

Despite the sensitive and serious nature, Minister Gayton McKenzie encouraged South Africans to support the controversial singer.

Addressing the public during his 100-day in-office update, Gayton claimed that he would prioritise hosting major music festivals in the country to attract high-profile artists.

The minister then nonchalantly mentioned Chris Brown, who had been trending at the time over a petition to cancel his shows.

Gayton said: “South Africans love dancing. Chris Brown’s concert was sold out in two hours. Our people are hungry for international acts”.

He added, “Don’t go any further, go to the Chris Brown concert.”

World.title: Cameron Waldeck-Cooks memorial service goes ahead
World.content:
Cameron Waldeck-Cooks's memorial service has taken place. Image via X/Canva

More than a month after her tragic death, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks has been fondly remembered in a memorial service. The St Stithians College student was found dead alongside her partner, Ethan Coetzee – an alumnus – at a game reserve in Mpumalanga.

Police have confirmed that a murder-suicide investigation is open.

Cameron allegedly died from strangulation/suffocation, while it has been reported that Ethan took his own life.



CAMERON WALDECK-COOKS MEMORIAL SERVICE

Over the weekend, the memorial service for Cameron Waldecks-Cooks took place.

The event was private, with no public details on its venue or guest list.

The Facebook and Instagram accounts of the St Stithians water polo team revealed that it had dedicated a game during a tournament over the weekend to Cameron, who also played the sport.



It shared: “This past Sunday, September 13, coincided with the memorial service for our beloved Saints Girls College Gr 11 student, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks. Unable to attend the service while competing on the final day of the St Alban’s Beach Polo tournament, our boys made sure Cameron was with them in spirit. Standing united by the pool, the team wore black armbands with ‘CAM’ written on their arms to honour her.

“Their heartfelt message to Cameron and her loved ones: ‘We wish we could have been there today. You will always be in our thoughts’”.

It’s unclear if the memorial service for Ethan Coetzee has taken place.



WHAT HAPPENED TO ETHAN COETZEE, CAMERON WALDECK-COOKS

In early August, news broke of an alleged murder-suicide involving two St Stithians learners: Grade 11 student Cameron Waldeck-Cooks and 2025 matriculant Ethan Coetzee.

Cameron, 17, and Ethan, 19, were found dead at a lodge in Mpumalanga on Monday, 3 August. Police initially investigated the deaths as an inquest and suspected that no foul play was involved.

However, preliminary findings as well as the opinion of an independent forensic pathologist have stated that Cameron died from strangulation/suffocation.



Ethan’s death is believed to be a suicide. A later report suggested that Ethan was a “jealous” and “controlling” partner to Cameron.

Police subsequently opened a murder case in connection with Cameron’s death. The investigation continues.

In a statement to TimesLive last month, St Stithians stated that it was “aware of difficult conversations this tragedy has prompted”



The Johannesburg private school, which dedicated a Women’s Day message to Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, had come under fire for its tribute to Ethan Coetzee just days earlier.

Many have accused the school of portraying Ethan as a “hero”.

The school declined to respond to rampant rumours about the alleged murder-suicide, including allegations of GBV and possibly drug use.



It shared: “We remain focused on supporting those most affected and caring for our community as it continues to navigate this profound loss”.

St Stithians also vowed to support students and staff affected by the double tragedy.

World.title: Ekurhuleni murders: Here are the eight cases police are investigating
World.content:
SAPS investigators work on the widening Ekurhuleni murder probe, which now includes eight women’s deaths across Kempton Park, Olifantsfontein and KwaThema. Image: SABC

Acting National Police Commissioner Lt-Gen Puleng Dimpane has detailed the eight women’s murder cases now under investigation across Ekurhuleni, as the South African Police Service widens its probe into the killings.

Police are examining five cases in Kempton Park, two in Olifantsfontein and one in KwaThema.

The cases span July to September, with investigators also reviewing earlier dockets to make sure no potentially linked deaths were missed.



SAPS has not confirmed that all eight murders are connected or that one perpetrator is responsible.

1. Kempton Park – 15 July

Police recorded the first case on 15 July.

A 37-year-old woman was found near the R21. Police arrested a suspect two days later and have positively linked him to that murder.

SAPS has not linked the suspect to the other cases.

2. Kempton Park – August

Dimpane said police recorded the second case in Kempton Park during August.

Investigators have included the case in the wider review as they compare evidence, locations and victim profiles.



3. Kempton Park – August

A third Kempton Park case followed during August, according to Dimpane’s breakdown on Tuesday night.

Police are examining that case alongside the others for possible similarities.

4. Kempton Park – September

The fourth case occurred in Kempton Park during September.

The growing cluster of deaths eventually prompted SAPS to bring together detectives, forensic specialists, crime intelligence and other specialised units.

5. Kempton Park – September

Police recorded another Kempton Park case in September, taking the number under investigation in the area to five.

Among the women identified during the broader investigation is Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo, 38, who disappeared after leaving her Rhodesfield home for a run.

Her family later formally identified her body at the Germiston mortuary.

6. Olifantsfontein – 14 September

Police found another woman dead in Olifantsfontein on Monday, 14 September.

The discovery widened the investigation beyond the Kempton Park cases and triggered further deployments across Ekurhuleni.

7. KwaThema – 15 September

Officers found another woman dead in KwaThema, Springs, on Tuesday morning, 15 September.

Her decomposed body was discovered on the side of the road.

KwaThema lies about 45km from Kempton Park, where the investigation initially centred. Police have been examining whether there are any forensic or investigative links between the cases.

8. Olifantsfontein – 7 September

Dimpane said police later added another Olifantsfontein case dating back to 7 September after reviewing cases that may be relevant to the investigation.

She acknowledged that police may have missed the case when initially compiling the running total.

The woman was found floating in a river near the Mall of Thembisa area.

Acting Gauteng Police Commissioner Maj-Gen Fred Kekana earlier said police had found no visible injuries on the woman but would not exclude the death until investigators completed further work. Public reporting has placed the river discovery in Clayville, near the Mall of Thembisa.

One suspect arrested, another sought

Dimpane also confirmed that police have one suspect in custody and are pursuing another person as investigators follow leads.

The arrested suspect relates to the first Kempton Park murder from July.

Police have not said the suspect is responsible for the other women’s deaths.

SAPS continues to examine whether investigators are dealing with one perpetrator, multiple perpetrators or separate crimes.

R400 000 reward on offer

Police have now offered a R400 000 reward for information that could help investigators make a breakthrough.

“There is R400 000 that we are putting on the table so that we are able to strengthen our investigations,” Dimpane said during Tuesday night’s high-level briefing.

EKURHULENI KILLINGS | Acting National Police Commissioner Lt-Gen Puleng Dimpane says a suspect has been arrested in connection with one of the murders committed in July, while police are pursuing another person of interest. A R400,000 reward has been offered for information that… pic.twitter.com/SQiqlNWHI6 — SABC News (@SABCNews) September 15, 2026

She also appealed to families with missing loved ones to contact police as forensic teams work with pathologists to identify women who remain unknown.

Lesufi: ‘We can’t normalise madness’

Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi has called for urgent action as concern grows across the province.

“We can’t normalise madness; this is madness,” Lesufi said after visiting the Kempton Park area earlier in the investigation.

He also urged residents to report anything they may have seen around the discovery sites, stressing that information that appears insignificant could prove crucial to investigators.

Lesufi said women could not continue living in fear of going about their daily lives and pledged provincial resources to support efforts to improve safety.

Police intensify Ekurhuleni operation

Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia confirmed on Tuesday night that the investigation now involves the murders of eight women.

SAPS has established a high-level multidisciplinary team and plans to significantly increase police visibility in Kempton Park and surrounding areas.

President Cyril Ramaphosa has also directed law-enforcement agencies to prioritise the investigation and ordered police to leave “no stone unturned” in bringing those responsible to justice.

For now, investigators continue to treat the evidence as decisive: eight murders are under scrutiny, but police have not yet proved that all eight form part of one pattern.

World.title: Police offer R400 000 reward in Ekurhuleni murder probe
World.content:
SAPS has offered a R400 000 reward for information that could help investigators make a breakthrough in the Ekurhuleni murders probe. Image: Pexels

Acting National Police Commissioner Lt-Gen Puleng Dimpane says police have arrested one suspect and are hunting another as investigators probe the murders of eight women across Ekurhuleni.

Dimpane made the announcement during a high-level briefing on Tuesday night, where police also confirmed a R400 000 reward for information that could help investigators make a breakthrough.

She said police had intensified the investigation, with specialised teams following leads, analysing evidence and working to establish possible links between the cases.



The South African Police Service has not confirmed that the arrested suspect is connected to all eight murders.

Families of missing women urged to come forward

Families who have missing relatives have been urged to contact police as investigators work to identify six of the women.

Police forensic teams are working alongside Gauteng Health pathologists as the identification process continues.

The appeal comes as SAPS examines a rapidly expanding number of cases across Ekurhuleni.

Police have not confirmed that one person or group killed all eight women.

Investigators are comparing forensic evidence, locations, victim profiles and the circumstances surrounding each death to establish whether any of the cases are connected.



Dimpane said police were following specific leads and working to consolidate information from the cases.

SAPS has deployed a high-level multidisciplinary team to drive the investigation.

Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia vowed that police would leave “no stone unturned” in bringing those responsible to justice.

Clayville river case added to investigation

Dimpane also confirmed that police are examining the death of a woman found in a river near the Mall of Thembisa in Clayville.

Police found the woman in the water and opened an inquest.

Acting Gauteng Police Commissioner Major-General Fred Kekana said earlier that investigators found no visible injuries on her body but included the case in the wider probe to ensure they did not overlook a possible connection.

The woman remains unidentified.

Eight women now form part of wider probe

The investigation initially centred on women found dead in and around Kempton Park before police widened their focus to other parts of Ekurhuleni.

Cachalia confirmed on Tuesday night that authorities were now investigating the murders of eight women.

Police have not released full details about the eighth woman or established that all eight deaths are linked.

SAPS has also announced plans to significantly increase police visibility in Kempton Park and surrounding areas as detectives pursue leads.

World.title: RG Snyman and wife welcome baby girl – See photos + her name!
World.content:
Springbok RG Snyman and his wife, Saskia, have welcomed their first child, a baby girl.

The rugby player, who is based in Ireland, has been out of action in recent months due to an ACL injury sustained in March.

RG SNYMAN IS A DAD!

On her Instagram account, RG Snyman’s wife, Saskia, shared news that the couple had welcomed their first child – a daughter.



The Snymans shared pictures of their newborn as well as her name.

Saskia shared: “Rooks Rose 🤍She’s here, and she’s perfect”.



RG – nicknamed the “Viking” – joins fellow Bok girl dads like Eben Etzebeth, Bongi Mbonambi and others. He is also a first-time father like Vincent Tshituka, Edwill van der Merwe and Kwagga Smith.

The towering lock has been out of action for the Springboks for the duration of 2026, after injuring his ACL in March. He is expected to return to play in 2027 after a lengthy rehabilitation.

ARE THEY IRISH CITIZENS?

RG Snyman – nicknamed the “Viking” – and Saskia moved to Ireland in 2020 when he signed with Munster. In 2024, the tallest Springbok signed with the rival Irish club of Leinster.



The Snymans have been living abroad for more than 5 years, making them eligible for residency.

Although their first child was born in Ireland, it does not automatically make her an Irish citizen.

Based on her eligibility, baby Rooks Rose could qualify for citizenship, as she is the child of legal residents of Ireland who have been living in the country for at least three of the four years preceding her birth.

WHEN WILL HE RETURN TO THE PITCH?

RG Snyman suffered a ruptured ACL in his right knee while playing for Leinster against Glasgow Warriors back in March.

With a lengthy rehabilitation, Leinster confirmed that RG had been ruled out for the remainder of the 2025/26 season.

Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus also confirmed that RG and Kwagga Smith, whose wife is also expecting, were two long-term injured Springboks expected to return in 2027

World.title: Three unfortunate problems Da Cruz has faced at Kaizer Chiefs
World.content:
Fernando Da Cruz arrived at Kaizer Chiefs with the pressure of restoring the club to the top of South African football. However, injuries, costly individual mistakes and the late arrival of new signings have made that task even more challenging.

For Da Cruz to get Amakhosi competing consistently, he will need to find solutions to all three issues.

1. INJURIES HAVE LIMITED DA CRUZ’S OPTIONS

The biggest early problem has been a growing injury list that has robbed Da Cruz of important players.



The likes of Flavio Da Silva, Rushwin Dortley, Bradley Cross, Khanyisa Mayo, Reeve Frosler and Langelihle Phiri have all been affected, leaving the technical team without several players who were expected to play important roles.

The absences of Frosler and Dortley have particularly affected the defensive structure. Mayo’s unavailability has reduced the coach’s attacking options.

As a result, Da Cruz has had to make tactical adjustments earlier than expected and experiment with different combinations instead of building consistency with his preferred team.



2. COSTLY MISTAKES KEEP COSTING CHIEFS

Another major concern has been the individual errors that have cost Kaizer Chiefs valuable points. Amakhosi have shown periods of impressive football under Da Cruz, but mistakes at the back have repeatedly undone their work.

Goalkeeper Brandon Petersen has come under scrutiny following costly errors, while defensive lapses have allowed opponents to punish Chiefs when the team appeared to be in control.

The 1-1 draw against Mamelodi Sundowns was another example of points slipping away in a match where Chiefs showed they could compete with one of the strongest teams in the Betway Premiership.



The draw against Polokwane City also highlighted the problem, with Da Cruz needing his players to become more clinical and more disciplined in decisive moments.

3. LATE SIGNINGS STILL NEED TIME

The final problem has been the integration of players who arrived towards the end of the transfer window.

Langelihle Phili, Adolf Mtasingwa and Faiz Abrahams missed important parts of pre-season after joining Chiefs late.



That has meant they did not have the same amount of time as their teammates to understand Da Cruz’s tactical demands and adapt to his playing philosophy.

The coach has therefore had to manage their minutes carefully, particularly Mtasingwa, while trying to avoid placing too much pressure on players who are still learning the system.

It has also prevented Da Cruz from consistently selecting what could be his strongest starting XI.



The upcoming international break could therefore be important for Chiefs. It gives the technical team an opportunity to work on defensive mistakes, allow injured players to recover and give the late arrivals more time to understand the coach’s demands.

Da Cruz’s start has certainly not been straightforward, but solving these three problems could be key to determining whether Chiefs can turn their promising performances into consistent results.

World.title: BREAKING: Ekurhuleni probe widens to EIGHT murdered women
World.content:
Police at the KwaThema scene where one of the women was found dead on Tuesday morning. Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia later confirmed that authorities are now investigating the murders of eight women across Ekurhuleni. Image: SABC

Police are now investigating the murders of eight women across Ekurhuleni, Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia confirmed on Tuesday night.

The widening probe began after police found a cluster of women dead in and around Kempton Park before investigators expanded their focus to other parts of the metro.

“The discovery of the bodies of eight young women who have been murdered is deeply distressing for all of us,” Cachalia said.



Authorities have not yet released details about the eighth woman, including where police found her or whether investigators have identified her.

High-level team takes charge

Cachalia said SAPS had established a high-level multidisciplinary team, led by the deputy provincial commissioner, to drive the investigation.

He vowed that police would pursue every lead.

“We will leave no stone unturned to bring the culprits to book,” he said.



Cachalia said SAPS had the experience and specialist expertise needed to investigate the killings and promised the political leadership would ensure investigators received the necessary support.

Police have not confirmed that one person or group killed all eight women. Investigators continue analysing each case to determine whether links exist.

Probe grew from four women to eight

The investigation has expanded rapidly since police initially began examining the deaths of four women found in Kempton Park between July and September.



As The South African previously reported, police released details of those four cases and confirmed an arrest in connection with the first woman’s murder. SAPS did not link that suspect to the other deaths.

A fifth woman was then found dead in Olifantsfontein on Monday, prompting police to widen the investigation.

On Tuesday morning, officers found another woman dead in KwaThema, Springs, roughly 45km from Kempton Park. Police did not immediately link that discovery to the earlier cases.



Later on Tuesday, Acting Gauteng Police Commissioner Major-General Fred Kekana confirmed that investigators had also added the case of an unidentified woman found floating in a river in Clayville, near the Mall of Thembisa, to the wider probe.

Cachalia’s evening announcement has now taken the number of murdered women under investigation to eight.

Four women sexually assaulted

The investigation has also produced disturbing forensic findings.



Police earlier confirmed that four of the first five women were sexually assaulted, while investigators continued examining possible links between the cases.

SAPS has repeatedly cautioned against drawing conclusions about whether one perpetrator, several perpetrators or separate crimes are involved before forensic evidence establishes a connection.

National police spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe said investigators were analysing evidence and victim profiles while specialist personnel joined the multidisciplinary team.



Elizabeth Moselakgomo among identified women

One of the women formally identified was 38-year-old Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo, who disappeared after leaving her Rhodesfield home for a run.

Her family later identified her body at the Germiston mortuary.

Her death prompted Athletics South Africa to call for women to be able to run, walk and exercise without fearing for their safety.



Gauteng Health also appealed to families of missing women to come forward as forensic teams worked to identify several of the bodies.

‘Women are unsafe’

Cachalia said the murders exposed the scale of violence facing women in South Africa.

He described the thought of a woman leaving home for something as ordinary as a run and never returning as “too unbearable to think about”.



“The deaths of eight young women, in these circumstances, is a reminder to us all that we live in a society in which … our mothers, our sisters, our daughters, our children are unsafe,” Cachalia said.

He called on South Africans to reflect on the country’s levels of murder, rape, domestic violence and gender-based violence.
