World.title: El Trompas, principal objetivo de las autoridades mexicanas por el asesinato de Claudia Tacoronte
World.content:
Las autoridades mexicanas ya tienen el apodo del presunto asesino de Claudia Tacoronte en Morelos. Al principal sospechoso del crimen lo conocen como El Trompas, según han confirmado a EL PAÍS fuentes cercanas a la investigación. El sujeto ya había sido grabado cometiendo varios robos en distintos comercios de Cuautla, uno de ellos fue incluso el mismo sábado que se produjo el ataque a la estudiante española. La ropa de los videos de los hurtos coincide con la que llevaba, según los testigos de la agresión, el hombre que apuñaló a Claudia cerca de la Casa de la Cultura y también con la que aparece en las cámaras de seguridad privadas de los vecinos: playera blanca, bermudas claras y mochila negra. Ese hombre es ahora el principal objetivo de las autoridades mexicanas.

Un poco antes de las 20.50 de la noche del sábado, Claudia Tacoronte fue asaltada en el centro de Cuautla, un municipio del Estado de Morelos que lleva años sufriendo los estragos de la delincuencia. La ciudad, de 183.000 habitantes, ha visto en los últimos meses la detención de su alcalde, el tesorero, el oficial mayor y el secretario municipal, acusados de colaborar con el crimen organizado, un grupo local vinculado al Cartel de Sinaloa. Hace años que los vecinos avisan de que las mafias controlan Cuautla y cómo eso ha incrementado los asesinatos y las extorsiones en el municipio.

La estudiante española viajó a la ciudad para asistir a una popular feria de plantas medicinales. Tacoronte llevaba apenas un mes en México y vivía en Cuernavaca, la capital de Morelos. Había llegado para estudiar unos meses en la universidad pública del Estado, la UAEM. Su estancia era parte de un intercambio con la Universidad de Granada, en la que se estaba formando en Educación Infantil.

Homenaje a Claudia Tacoronte en el en el Instituto de Ciencias de la Educación de la Universidad Autónoma del Estado de Morelos. Rodrigo Oropeza Patio del Instituto de Ciencias de la Educación en la Universidad Autónoma del Estado de Morelos. Rodrigo Oropeza Homenaje a Claudia Tacoronte en el en el Instituto de Ciencias de la Educación de la Universidad Autónoma del Estado de Morelos, en Cuernavaca, Morelos. Rodrigo Oropeza Compañeros de Claudia Tacoronte prenden veladoras en su memoria. Rodrigo Oropeza Elementos de seguridad resguardan la Casa de la Cultura de Cuautla,Morelos, este lunes. Rodrigo Oropeza

Ximena Becerril, una amiga de Claudia, contó a este periódico que ella estaba muy emocionada porque los organizadores de la feria de de Cuautla le habían ofrecido hospedaje en la Casa de la Cultura. “Le encantaba todo el asunto de los pueblos originarios”, apunta la joven, que recuerda a su amiga con la vitalidad, el entusiasmo y las ganas de conocer un país nuevo: “¡Siempre estaba emocionada! Decía que estaba en su mejor momento, yo la veía como libre”.

El sábado en la noche, en una calle que llevaba hacia su hospedaje, Claudia fue asaltada. Un sujeto la apuñaló y ella falleció a causa de las heridas. Le dio tiempo a correr, pedir auxilio y resguardarse. Un puñado de vecinos acudieron a su ayuda al oír los gritos, algunos incluso trataron de perseguir al agresor. Varios identificaron su ropa: parte blanca de arriba y una mochila negra.

En varias cámaras privadas de vecinos de la zona se observa a un hombre vestido así que sale corriendo. La principal hipótesis de la Fiscalía de Morelos sobre el asesinato de la estudiante es que se tratara de un robo, aunque siguen valorando otros “indicios”.

Unas horas antes del crimen, una cámara de seguridad de un comercio de Cuautla captó al mismo hombre —coincide todo, también la marca de la camiseta— presuntamente tratando de robar. En las imágenes, grabadas a las 13.15 de ese sábado, se observa como el sujeto sale a la carrera al ver pasar a una patrulla de policía. Estos días se ha difundido también en Facebook otra imagen de la misma persona en una tienda bicicletas, donde se le acusa de robo. Una fuente vinculada a la investigación ha confirmado que se trata del mismo sujeto, El Trompas, al que ahora se busca por el feminicidio de Claudia.

El crimen de la estudiante ha puesto a México de nuevo frente a uno de sus grandes lastres: la violencia contra las mujeres. En lo que va de año, otras tres estudiantes de la misma universidad que Claudia —la Universidad Autónoma del Estado de Morelos— han sido asesinadas; otras 69 mujeres en el Estado y 1.250 en total en el país. La impunidad por estos crímenes alcanza el 95%. El Gobierno español, a través de su canciller y del consulado, han afirmado que van a llegar hasta el final para que el asesinato se resuelva.

De momento, el Ministerio de Exteriores ya ha incluido Morelos en la lista de lugares donde recomienda a los españoles no viajar porque “se asiste a un incremento de la violencia ligada al narcotráfico así como de secuestros”. “Se debe actuar con prudencia, informarse antes de visitar ciudades y comarcas aisladas y procurar no efectuar desplazamientos nocturnos salvo en zonas pobladas. Permanecer siempre alerta ante incidentes imprevistos y concentrar las actividades propias en el propósito de la visita sin aventurarse solo por lugares desconocidos”, se lee en la página de la Cancillería. Así mismo, la Universidad de Granada también ha cancelado el intercambio a Morelos de otros tres estudiantes que estaba previsto para el próximo semestre.

World.title: La denuncia de la hermana de Claudia, la estudiante asesinada en México: “¿Tenemos que normalizar que se asesine a tres mujeres en un mes en la misma universidad?"
World.content:
La hermana de Claudia, la estudiante asesinada en México: "Vivimos en una sociedad enferma"

La denuncia de la hermana de Claudia, la estudiante asesinada en México: “¿Tenemos que normalizar que se asesine a tres mujeres en un mes en la misma universidad?"

Lara Tacoronte publica un vídeo en redes sociales condenando el feminicidio de su hermana: “Vivimos en una sociedad enferma”

World.title: La vida feliz de Claudia Tacoronte: “Siempre estaba emocionada… ¡La veía como una persona libre!”
World.content:
Un día, sin motivo alguno, Claudia le llevó una galleta. Un detalle. Otro día, cuando le contó que se le había caído el café, Claudia le trajo uno nuevo. La primera vez que almorzaron juntas, Claudia le dijo, ‘tu pide y yo como’. Ordenaron enchiladas verdes y a Claudia le encantaron. “Y la jamaica, ¡el agua de jamaica! Eso también le encantó”, dice su amiga. Por aquí caminaron juntas, aquí se conocieron y se hicieron amigas, su lugar seguro, el campus de la universidad, en Cuernavaca, México, rodeado de montañas. Aquí la recuerda ahora Ximena, invocando un recuerdo que parece, también, un barrera contra las lágrimas. Recordar ayuda, es una especie de embrujo, como si el pasado no acabara de ser cierto. Porque la certeza abruma: su amiga, Claudia Tacoronte, ya no está. La mataron.

Claudia Tacoronte era la nueva, venida de Granada, en España. Ximena Becerril, su primera compañera de pupitre. El 17 de agosto, la vida las juntó en una clase de filosofía de la educación. “Ella al principio como que no entendía mucho, pero yo le dije: ‘No te preocupes, yo te explico’. Y le explicaba”. La amiga sonríe, como si aquello en realidad hubiera sido solo un teatro, el tanteo nervioso de futuras cómplices. “¡Le gustaba moverse, el senderismo, estaba muy emocionada porque este martes iba a participar en una representación por el día de la independencia, ¡Siempre estaba emocionada!… Decía que estaba en su mejor momento, yo la veía como libre”, dice ella, que habla y habla, porque si calla y mira las coronas de flores y las velas…

Homenaje a Claudia Tacoronte en el Instituto de Ciencias de la Educación de la Universidad Autónoma del Estado de Morelos (UAEM), este lunes. Rodrigo Oropeza

Una vez, Becerril le dio un consejo a su amiga. Uno muy serio, ajeno a la energía juvenil, al optimismo. Le dijo: “Si estás en una situación de peligro, ¡nada más corre!”. Eso le dijo. Su amiga quiere pensar que Claudia corrió, que quiso escapar de su asesino, un hombre alto, de pelo corto, que la noche que atacó a la joven, el sábado, vestía una camiseta blanca y unas bermudas claras, a la espalda una mochila negra, pequeña. Pero no se sabe, porque Claudia estaba con su celular, separada del grupo, y no había una sola cámara de seguridad que enfocara ese espacio, la entrada de la Casa de la Cultura de Cuautla, una población mediana a dos horas de Ciudad de México, a una de Cuernavaca. Ni una cámara, ni un vigilante en la puerta, nada.

Los vecinos de la Casa de la Cultura están que trinan desde el sábado, porque un simple vigilante, dicen, podría haber evitado el ataque. Es posible. Pero los vecinos también dicen que Cuautla, una de las ciudades más importantes del Estado de Morelos, que gobierna Morena, es un absoluto desastre y que hay asesinatos todo el tiempo, y que la extorsión es la ley, y que a cada rato cierran negocios por ello, y que la corrupción y connivencia de la clase política con el crimen es el paisaje de sus días… No les falta razón. En mayo, el Gobierno federal, también en manos de Morena, detuvo al alcalde, al tesorero, al oficial mayor y al secretario municipal. ¿La acusación? Colaborar en las actividades de la aventura local del Cartel de Sinaloa.

Casa de la Cultura de Cuautla, Morelos, este lunes. Rodrigo Oropeza

Por eso, por la violencia, por esa podredumbre, Ximena Becerril le dio aquel consejo a su amiga, que si pasaba algo, corriera. Porque ella, a los 24 años, sabe que en Morelos —en México, en general— la violencia es un problema importante, que hay asesinatos todos los días, decenas, todos los días. El Gobierno federal, que dirige Claudia Sheinbaum, asegura que han bajado más del 50% desde su llegada al poder, en octubre de 2024. Parece cierto, los datos lo avalan. Antes llegaron a ser 100 diarios; ahora, 40, 30. Una cantidad lo suficientemente alta, sin embargo, como para que la Universidad Estatal Autónoma de Morelos (UAEM), la gran casa de estudios regional, a la que acudía Claudia Tacoronte, cuente otros tres asesinatos de alumnas en los últimos siete meses.

Pero el crimen no ocurrió allí, en la UAEM, sino en Cuautla. La víctima fue al municipio a pasar el fin de semana, a participar en la “XLII Fiesta Nacional de la Planta Medicinal”, que organizaban entidades privadas. Ximena Becerril dice que no sabe si fue sola, o con alguien. Dice, eso sí, que vivía sola en un departamento cerca de la universidad. Dice también que la última vez que hablaron fue el jueves. Dice que Claudia estaba muy emocionada porque los organizadores de la fiesta le habían ofrecido hospedaje en la Casa de la Cultura, lugar donde se celebraban las jornadas. “Le encantaba todo el asunto de los pueblos originarios. El fin de semana anterior, había ido al Museo Nacional de Antropología”, en Ciudad de México, con dos amigos.

Cuautla, un lugar que hace 10 años alcanzó la hora estelar de los noticieros, porque la Fiscalía enterró cuerpos sin etiquetar en una fosa común, cuerpos, en algunos casos, de personas desaparecidas, personas que sus familias buscaban. Ahí fue Claudia Tacoronte y ahí pasó el viernes y el sábado, como atestigua un video de la fiesta. Allí estuvo la joven, una ciudad que hace tres días era pueblo y que en su adolescencia demográfica sufre una tremenda desnutrición en las periferias, con bolsas de pobreza y desesperanza a cada costado. “El problema ya no es la cocaína o la marihuana, es el cristal”, dice una veterana política local. El cristal, la metanfetamina. No se sabe si Claudia Tacoronte era consciente del contexto. Por ejemplo: que hace 11 meses, México desbarató aquí cerca un laboratorio que producía 300 millones de pesos al mes en esa droga, 15 millones de euros.

Anuncio del Plan Cuautla, una estrategia del Gobierno federal para combatir la delincuencia en el municipio de Cuautla, Morelos. Rodrigo Oropeza

Los vecinos están molestos porque no había policía en la fiesta de la planta medicinal, porque luego del ataque tardaron en llegar, porque nada garantiza que lo ocurrido suponga un cambio, algo que ilumine un poco el futuro. Mientras, evocan la noche del sábado. Una mujer que vive justo enfrente dice que lo primero que escuchó fueron tres gritos: ¡ayuda, ayuda, ayuda!. “Primero pensé que igual eran de una obra de teatro, como es casa de cultura… Pero luego dije: ‘No, es otra cosa”. Ella y algunas más salieron. Otra de las vecinas entró en el recinto y se acercó a la víctima. Una mujer estaba con ella. Era, le dijo después, la que había gritado. “Otros vecinos se fueron corriendo detrás del asesino”, dice. Las dos se quedaron con Claudia. Ella le tomó la mano. Aún estaba viva. “Le decía ‘baja tu respiración, que si no sale más rápido la sangre”. Le rogaba que lo hiciera. Eran las 20.52 del sábado. La ambulancia tardó unos 15 minutos en llegar.

¿Por qué? ¿Por qué ese hombre atacó a una mujer que, salvo sorpresa mayúscula, no conocía? No se sabe. La Fiscalía de Morelos, encargada de las pesquisas, apunta a un robo. El Gabinete de Seguridad federal, que desembarcó masivamente en Cuautla tras la detención del equipo de gobierno municipal este verano, dice que va a detener a los responsables. Cuautla luce tapizada estos días con lonas anunciando su presente, el operativo de las autoridades contra el crimen, la extorsión, el asesinato, la violencia, el “plan Cuautla”. Es una invitación del Gobierno de Sheinbaum a confiar en las autoridades, a denunciar a los criminales, a tratar de rehacer el tejido social. La veterana política local, zanja: “Hay una tremenda descomposición social aquí”.

World.title: El Gobierno prevé reubicar a los menores irregulares en Ceuta en un plazo mínimo de dos meses si continúa el bloqueo del PP
World.content:
El Gobierno empieza a perder la paciencia conforme aumenta el desgaste político por Ceuta. Ministros que están muy encima de la gestión de la crisis causada por la permanencia en la ciudad de unos 10.000 de los entre 70.000 y 80.000 inmigrantes irregulares que participaron en el salto fronterizo del 30 y 31 de julio adelantan que La Moncloa prevé reubicar en la península a los menores irregulares en Ceuta en un plazo mínimo de dos meses aplicando la ley vigente —el real decreto ley aprobado en abril de 2025 que establece los cupos para cada territorio en situaciones de colapso como el que sufre la ciudad norteafricana— si el PP continúa con su “bloqueo”. El ministro de Política Territorial y coordinador del mano único de la crisis, Ángel Víctor Torres, explicó en la comparecencia posterior al Consejo de Ministros que este lunes, en la séptima semana desde el estallido de la crisis, se habían empezado a tramitar los primeros 10 expedientes de reagrupación familiar de menores migrantes. Si esta no fuera posible, los menores serían trasladados a la Península. El ministro estimó además que entre 700 y 1.000 menores continuaban en las calles sin filiar.

Otro de los motivos para trasladar a los menores fuera de Ceuta sería la falta de garantías por parte de Marruecos para permitir las reunificaciones familiares. Según fuentes gubernamentales, antes de la entrada masiva de finales de julio se habían planteado 600 expedientes desde 2021, y Rabat no había dado respuesta a ninguno. Pedro Sánchez defendió anoche en La Sexta la actuación “inteligente” del régimen de Mohamed VI en una entrevista en la que dio de margen hasta “final del año para arreglar la situación en Ceuta”. Sin embargo, esos precedentes hacen que el Gobierno ya contemple como el escenario probable obligar a los barones del PP a cumplir con el real decreto que establece los cupos para cada territorio. El PP preside 11 comunidades autónomas además de Ceuta y Melilla y cogobierna en Melilla.

Los ministros consultados responsabilizan al partido de Alberto Núñez Feijóo de la falta de colaboración de las autonomías presididas por los populares para albergar en la península a parte de los menores que entraron en la avalancha. “Hemos trabajado con el horizonte de trasladarles y se les trasladará. La reticencia es del PP”, transmiten fuentes gubernamentales, que atribuyen la tardanza en los trámites de filiación al “boicot” del PP, como ha expresado en público Óscar Puente.

Uno de los miembros del Consejo de Ministros achaca buena parte de la lentitud en la respuesta a la cris política y social en Ceuta a “la falta de colaboración” de Juan Jesús Vivas. El dirigente popular, que lleva 25 años al frente de la ciudad, se encuentra sometido según las fuentes citadas a una enorme presión por los “intereses partidistas” de Génova. El resultado, de acuerdo con los ministros consultados, es que Vivas no se quiere enfrentar a su partido. Feijóo visitará el lunes Ceuta junto al presidente del Partido Popular Europeo, Manfred Weber. “En privado dicen que los saquemos a las bravas, que no quieren enfrentarse al PP”, afirma un ministro involucrado en la resolución de la crisis. El Gobierno detalla que las fórmulas posibles sobre la mesa son los acuerdos bilaterales con otras comunidades, como ha ocurrido con el caso de Navarra, que ha recibido a cinco menores. Esta es la opción más rápida. “Estamos trabajando con otras comunidades, no solo del PSOE. Hay otros mecanismos como a través de entidades o ya mediante el real decreto ley”, abundan.

El Ministerio de Juventud e Infancia tiene previsto convocar una nueva sectorial con las comunidades autónomas. El objetivo del ministerio, que dirige Sira Rego, de Sumar, es que las comunidades participen en el plan de acogida de forma voluntaria. Si no es así, el Gobierno obligaría al cumplimiento del real decreto ley.

El Pacto Europeo de Migración y Asilo (PEMA), que entró en vigor en junio para unificar y reformar las normas de control fronterizo, acogida y asilo en la Unión Europea, también estaría demorando el proceso, según las fuentes consultadas. El motivo sería el endurecimiento del plan migratorio de Bruselas, donde además el Gobierno progresista de Pedro Sánchez ha perdido a buena parte de sus aliados y se ha quedado en una situación de minoría.

World.title: El PP europeo insinúa la suspensión del acuerdo UE-Marruecos por la crisis de Ceuta
World.content:
El curso político en la UE también se inaugura con la crisis de Ceuta presente. El Parlamento Europeo debate este mismo martes sobre “los recientes ataques híbridos y la instrumentalización de los migrantes en Ceuta”, a la que sucederá, ya el próximo jueves, la votación de una resolución sobre este asunto. En el texto presentado por el Partido Popular Europeo, se exige a Marruecos “cumplir sus responsabilidades como socio clave de la UE y honrar sus compromisos en la gestión de fronteras, retorno y cooperación en migración”. Añade, además, que “cualquier declaración que ponga en duda la soberanía española es inaceptable e incompatible con las obligaciones de un socio clave”.

Apunta el eurodiputado popular Javier Zarzalejos que es “difícil aspirar a una relación política y comercial con Marruecos” por todo lo que ha pasado. “Ni los cadáveres de los 150 ahogados han sido autorizados a ser retornados”, insiste. Otras fuentes del mismo grupo parlamentario también explican que, si bien no se habla expresamente de suspender ese acuerdo, sí que está implícito.

Zarzalejos, de la mano de Vox, insiste en devolver a todos los que entraron. Más contundente es, todavía, el eurodiputado de Vox Jorge Buxadé: “El argumento de los procedimientos es una broma. Ceuta es un escenario de guerra. El Gobierno nos ha mentido: fue una avalancha de 100.000 personas. Marruecos ha hecho una sola cosa buena: decir que los quiere a todos”. Por su parte, el socialista Juan Fernando López-Aguilar insiste en que todo eso es ilegal en lo relativo a menores y solicitantes de asilo.

El texto presentado por el PPE, el grupo más grande de la Eurocámara, está abierto ahora a la negociación. Fuentes del grupo parlamentario explican que su intención es pactarlo con los grupos proeuropeos, es decir, socialistas y demócratas, los liberales de Renew y Los Verdes, por lo que es probable que haya cambios sustanciales y, opinan incluso, que no es un texto duro con el Gobierno español para facilitar ese pacto.

La eurodiputada del PP, Dolors Montserrat, en el pleno del Europarlamento este martes en Estrasburgo. Christian CREUTZ

No obstante, antes incluso de que se conocieran las diferentes propuestas de resolución sobre la crisis ceutí −la del PPE es solo una, hay otras presentadas por otros grupos, aunque lo normal es que solo salga una adelante enmendada por aquellos que la respaldan−, Marruecos ha preferido actuar y el lunes por la tarde envió un correo electrónico a eurodiputados en el que cuestiona ser responsable de la crisis. “¿Qué interés tendría Marruecos en provocar una crisis grave con España y la Unión Europea, sobre todo en un momento en el que la UE es el principal socio de Marruecos y en el que las relaciones entre Marruecos y la UE se están fortaleciendo y consolidando aún más?“, puede leerse en el texto recibido, al menos, por eurodiputados socialistas y del PNV, no así los del PP español, según fuentes de este partido. El correo, firmado por la embajada marroquí ante la UE y la OTAN, destaca que el Gobierno español ha eximido de responsabilidad a Rabat.

El registro de las propuestas de moción ha precedido al debate sobre la crisis migratoria de este verano. Y ahí se ha palpado que Ceuta también sube la temperatura en el Parlamento Europeo. El debate que se ha celebrado este martes en Estrasburgo se ha llenado de reproches cruzados entre todas las fuerzas políticas presentes. La mayor de ellas, el PP europeo, ha empezado por reprochar al Gobierno “la tardanza de semanas” en reclamar ayuda a la Comisión Europea. Lo ha hecho su vicepresidente, el belga Jeroen Lenaers, quien ha empezado su intervención subrayando que “Ceuta es Europa”.

Aunque, desde luego, la intervención más dura de los conservadores ha sido la de la española Dolors Montserrat. La eurodiputada del PP ha cargado contra Sánchez diciendo que “lo sabía y se fue de vacaciones”. “Esto le convierte en cómplice”, ha apuntado, para señalar a continuación a Marruecos como “responsable por acción o por omisión”. Montserrat también ha pronunciado la frase de Leaners acerca de la europeidad de Ceuta.

Esta última frase ha sido casi el único punto en el que, con diferentes tonos, han coincidido casi todos los participantes en el debate. “Ceuta es España, es Europa”, ha repetido la presidenta del grupo socialista, Iratxe García Pérez. La española ha reprochado al PP y a las familias políticas a su derecha que reclamen la expansión de menores por ser “un ataque al Estado de derecho”, después de destacar la solidaridad europea con Italia, Polonia o Lituania en situaciones similares a las que ha sufrido la ciudad del norte de África.

Para el PP español, la situación en Ceuta se ha convertido en una herramienta con la que atacar al Ejecutivo de Pedro Sánchez, que no está dispuesto a soltar. De hecho, el mismo lunes quedó claro que su prioridad es llevar la crisis al escenario europeo. Y eso se ha visto en el debate con claridad en el debate.

El próximo lunes, por ejemplo, el líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, viajará de nuevo a la ciudad autónoma acompañado del líder del PP europeo, Manfred Weber, en la que será su cuarta visita desde el salto masivo hace un mes y medio. Antes, este jueves, el jefe de los populares se reúne en Madrid con el comisario de Inmigración, Magnus Brunner.

World.title: Allianz se retira como patrocinador del Festival de las Ideas tras la amenaza de boicot de más de una treintena de participantes
World.content:
La aseguradora rechaza “firmemente las acusaciones” sobre sus vínculos con Israel y los organizadores asumen el coste de la decisión y siguen “adelante con la convocatoria”, que arranca este jueves

Faltaban apenas 48 horas para el arranque de la tercera edición del Festival de las Ideas en Madrid, que se celebra entre el 17 y el 20 de septiembre, cuando este martes por la mañana se hizo público un comunicado en el que más de dos decenas de participantes ponían en suspenso su contribución a esta gran cita cultural. El cineasta Rodrigo Sorogoyen, la escritora Alana S. Portero, el artista El Niño de Elche, el filósofo Paul B. Preciado, entre otros, firmaban un escrito —al que fueron sumándose más nombres hasta superar la treintena de un total de los cerca de 100 invitados al certamen—, en el que anunciaban que no asistirían a los actos en los que estaba prevista su presencia hasta que el festival no se comprometiera “públicamente a desvincularse de Allianz y a no aceptar apoyos económicos, ni en esta ni en futuras ediciones, de entidades que colaboran con el Estado de Israel en la destrucción del pueblo palestino”.

Horas después, Allianz se retiraba como patrocinador de esta cita. “Es imposible ya quitar el nombre de los programas de mano, pero Allianz se desvincula del festival. Asumimos el coste para poder seguir adelante con la convocatoria”, explicaban los organizadores, la empresa cultural La Fábrica y el Círculo de Bellas Artes.

Ambas entidades lanzaron una respuesta oficial pasadas las tres de la tarde, donde señalaban que la suspensión del patrocinio de Allianz era consensuado. El festival, por tanto, “continúa con su programación completa, reafirmando su compromiso con el mantenimiento de un espacio de reflexión que considera fundamental para el fomento del pensamiento crítico”, indicaba el escrito. “Ambas partes coinciden en que el festival debe seguir siendo un espacio dedicado al intercambio libre de ideas, al debate abierto y a la diversidad de perspectivas, sin que ninguna controversia externa desvíe la atención de su programación, sus participantes o su público”.

A esta nota se sumó poco después la respuesta de Allianz: “Rechazamos firmemente las acusaciones vertidas contra nuestra compañía y respaldamos nuestras prácticas empresariales responsables. No queremos que este debate desvíe la atención del Festival de las Ideas, de sus organizadores, participantes o público. Por ello, hemos decidido retirarnos del patrocinio para que el evento pueda celebrarse según lo previsto”.

En la nota de los participantes que amenazaban con ausentarse del festival si la empresa alemana mantenía el patrocinio se apuntaba: “El gigante alemán de seguros, Allianz, es hoy en día el mayor comprador mundial de bonos del Estado israelí y, por tanto, financiador fundamental del genocidio en curso”. Y añadía: “Allianz no puede alegar desconocimiento porque su nombre figura en el informe de 2025 de la relatora de Naciones Unidas Francesca Albanese, titulado De la economía de la ocupación a la economía del genocidio, por la compra de esos bonos, cuya inversión ha multiplicado por tres desde entonces”.

La aseguradora alemana era hasta el martes el patrocinador oficial del evento, que también cuenta con la colaboración de Redeia, CaixaBank y The Cocktail. El festival recibe además apoyo institucional del Ministerio de Cultura, la Dirección General del Libro, la Comunidad de Madrid, el Ayuntamiento de Madrid, el Ministerio de Sanidad, el Ministerio de Juventud e Infancia, el Consejo de Juventud de España, las embajadas de Francia y Alemania, el Foro Cultural de Austria, la Casa de Asia y la Fundación Casa de México de España. Cuenta también con nueve medios asociados, entre los que está EL PAÍS.

Además de las conversaciones entre los invitados, el programa cuenta con actividades escénicas, paseos filosóficos, visitas a exposiciones, talleres y varios speaker’s corner en plena calle. El punto central de las actividades era, como en las dos anteriores ediciones, el Escenario Allianz, en la plaza de España, pero este año cambiará su nombre para dejar fuera a Allianz. El festival incluye actividades en las fundaciones Ramón Areces y Ortega Marañón, en Casa de México, CaixaForum, el Ateneo, la Casa del Libro en Gran Vía y en pequeños escenarios en las calles Bailén, Alcalá y Montera, así como en el Círculo de Bellas Artes.

Antes de que se anunciara la retirada de Allianz del festival los organizadores explicaron que harían todo lo posible por sacar adelante la convocatoria. “No queremos que la ciudadanía pierda este espacio de reflexión y debate que lleva ya dos años en marcha y en el que ha habido posturas propalestinas”, explicaron. Entre otros actos en esta línea citaron la conferencia inaugural del año pasado a cargo de Pankaj Mishra, en el que el intelectual se refirió en el escenario Allianz Plaza de España a la situación en Gaza y afirmó que el colonialismo no había desaparecido.

El ministro de Cultura, Ernest Urtasun, también afirmó antes de que se hiciera pública la retirada del patrocinador, que no le gustaba la presencia de empresas vinculadas a Israel en actividades culturales, pero señaló que debía ser la organización del festival la que tomara “sus propias decisiones”.

Entre los firmantes que habían denunciado la participación de Allianz hay personalidades de distintos ámbitos de la cultura como Inés Hernand, Marta Sanz, Remedios Zafra o Rocío Molina. “Tomamos esta decisión desde la diversidad de voces y de perspectivas, pero unides en una posición común de solidaridad con el pueblo palestino y de rechazo a cualquier forma de complicidad cultural o empresarial con la vulneración de los derechos humanos”, planteaban en el comunicado. “La cultura no es un espacio neutro: es un campo atravesado por relaciones de poder, intereses económicos y conflictos políticos. Un Festival de las Ideas que hace del cuerpo su tema central de reflexión no puede, al mismo tiempo, contribuir a blanquear a los actores económicos que permiten que tenga lugar un exterminio, una ocupación y un apartheid”.

Los firmantes no pretendían, aseguraron, señalar a la organización del festival. “Al contrario, esperamos que este gesto sirva para abrir una reflexión colectiva, para que el festival revise sus vínculos y, ojalá, para que dé una respuesta pública, positiva e implicada, que nos permita sumarnos a los debates y hacer de ellcasi cos un lugar de pensamiento y de ampliación del espacio democrático. Creemos en una cultura comprometida con la justicia, los derechos humanos y la dignidad de todos los pueblos”.

World.title: Heinen warns “hard choices” are needed to secure future growth
World.content:
Finance minister Eelco Heinen has said the Netherlands needs to build a “coalition for growth” to secure the future prosperity and security of the country.

Heinen said no one party had a monopoly on the answers and his own ideas on the role of markets and European co-operation had been forced to change in response to the challenges to the international order in recent years.

But he warned that the Netherlands also needed to cut its spending and reform social security and healthcare if it wanted to become “the best place to invest and grow”.

“International competition is becoming fiercer, our productivity is hardly growing and investment is lagging behind,” he said.

“Economic growth must become a national challenge, because a country that moves forwards is in everyone’s interest.”

Heinen, who represents the right-wing, fiscally conservative VVD party in the centre-right coalition, said the budget package had made space for the demands of opposition parties on both left and right.

Capital gains

Many of the original plans in the coalition agreement have been watered down or postponed as Heinen seeks support for a “common goal” that goes “beyond the next budget.”

The cabinet will bring forward plans to introduce capital gains tax system to replace the Box 3 asset tax, which the Supreme Court has said violates European human rights laws.

Heinen said the extended discount on fuel duty, cutting airport tax and making air travel more sustainable showed he was prepared to accommodate the wishes of opposition parties.

Social security

But his reference to “hard choices” were a clear signal that he is determined to press ahead with significant cuts to the social security and healthcare budgets, which the largest left-wing party Pro and the trade unions insist must be scrapped.

“Without reforms to social security and healthcare the money we spend today will hold back the growth of the future,” Heinen said.

The minister said the “handbrake” needed to be taken off investment, with the government increasing investment in helping startup businesses “get off the ground and stay here”.

Heinen said his ideas on international co-operation had changed in recent years as he saw the trend in the global economy turning from free trade to the agressive use of economic power.

European co-operation

“You know I believe strongly in the power of the market, but if the market comes up short and promising businesses can’t grow as a result, you have to be prepared to adapt your beliefs to reality,” he said.

International rules were no longer a guarantee of global security and the Netherlands needed to work on strengthening the European Union’s internal economic ties. “Yesterday’s world is not coming back,” he said.

“I will still be critical when Europa claims more influence than it needs or builds up more debts. But co-operation sometimes gives us more influence.

That’s why we must deepen European co-operation and make our internal market work better and improve our ties with countries outside Europe.”

World.title: Opposition parties dismiss king’s speech as road to stagnation
World.content:
Opposition parties have accused the Dutch government of failing to make choices and leading the country into a “stagnation” following a king’s speech packed with appeals to the Dutch traditions of compromise and co-operation.

In a long and wide-ranging speech, King Willem-Alexander said “communality” could be an “antidote to polarisation” and said solutions needed to be found on issues such as nitrogen pollution, the housing crisis and social unrest around asylum.

But opposition parties said the cabinet had failed to set out a clear vision or take the initiative in coming forward with ideas to fix the problems.

“Politics is about making choices,” said Joost Eerdmans, leader of the right-wing conservative JA21. “The king can say democracy isn’t 50% plus one, but that’s how it works in practice. They’ve forgotten to turn left or right, or else they can’t.”

Jesse Klaver, leader of the largest left-wing opposition party Pro, said the king’s “fine words” could not disguise the fact “that the cabinet is rudderless.”

“We are in a permanent process of forming the government because the minority government can’t agree on which way to take the country in.”

Lack of direction

In the weeks before the opening day of parliament the three coalition parties D66, CDA and VVD were unable to agree what concessions to make to opposition parties in the budget deal that finance minister Eelco Heinen will deliver on Tuesday.

Instead the minority government will have to keep negotiating with opposition leaders to find the 10 seats it needs in the lower house and the 16 seats in the Senate to pass its laws.

Mirjam Bikker, leader of the ChristenUnie, said the king’s speech showed a lack of direction from the coalition parties.

“If you want to make progress, you have to decide which way to go,” she said. “We’ve seen a few concessions on minor things like cuts to healthcare, but my concern is that without a sense of direction it’ll just be a few trinkets.”

Geert Wilders of the far-right PVV criticised the speech for failing to address people’s concerns about fundamental issues such as the rising cost of living.

”Lots of money is being spent on Europe, development aid, nitrogen and the climate, while we see the country is changing and we can’t pay the bills,” he said. ”The sooner this cabinet falls, the better.”

World.title: Protecting democracy takes centre stage in king’s speech
World.content:
Democracy was the central theme of king Willem-Alexander’s speech to both houses of parliament on Tuesday afternoon, an event in which the monarch traditionally outlines the main themes of government policy for the coming year.

“Democracy requires constant protection and maintenance,” the king said.

“Everyone who does something for another person – as a volunteer, an unpaid carer or in some other capacity – serves the public interest and makes the Netherlands stronger. Fortunately, this Dutch tradition of community spirit endures, as an antidote to polarisation.”

“That is why it’s so important that we don’t reduce the concept of democracy to the will of half the people plus one. Democracy should unite people, not play them off against each other.

An important element in this, the king said, is ensuring the public have confidence that government will solve their problems. “It is a joint contract with parliament and the government to make sure that their questions can more often be answered by ‘yes’.”

“Parliamentary democracy belongs to everyone, is for everyone and should serve everyone.”

Read the official translation of the speech

The king went on to outline various policy initiatives drawn up by the minority government for the coming years. Some problems, such as the housing shortage, nitrogen-based pollution, public safety and climate change have, he said, been “asking for solutions for far too long.”

The king said the cabinet will continue to listen to the concerns of farmers who are worried about their livelihoods, particularly those working close to areas where nature is under threat. But it would be “irresponsible” to delay measures to reduce nitrogen pollution, he said.

He called for a pragmatic approach to solving the housing crisis, including more reliance on prefabricated buildings. Reducing refugee numbers will take time and he described the wave of protests about the location of refugee centres as “worrying”.

“It must be clear that threats and violence are unacceptable,” he said.

Railway sabotage

The king’s speech took place as the police and railway officials sought to end at least 30 acts of sabotage on the railways, plus numerous hay bale fires close to motorways, thought to have been carried out by militant farmers.

He did not refer to the trouble expressly, but he closed his speech by saying that one definition of democracy includes the need to give way occasionally to the meaning of others.

“The spirit of reasonableness and compromise implied in that remark will solve more problems for people than the constant controversies that sometimes seem to be gaining the upper hand,” he said.

World.title: One in four questions in Dutch parliament “written using AI”
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Around a quarter of questions from MPs in the Dutch parliament were written with the help of AI tools such as ChatGPT or Claude, according to research by broadcaster NOS.

NOS analysed 28,000 questions using the AI detection tool Pangram and found that 26% of them showed stylistic features of AI.

Usage peaked at more than 30% just before the summer recess, but dropped to around 17% in July, roughly the same level as a year go.

Some MPs included a sentence or two of AI, while others used to generate whole strings of questions.

Last week prime minister Rob Jetten was criticised after it emerged that around 30% of his social media posts included AI-generated content.

Some of the messages were apparently personal reflections on sensitive subjects such as the mistreatment of Moluccan war veterans in the 1950s, which Jetten recently apologised for on behalf of the government.

Jetten defended the practice, saying that “like three-quarters of Dutch people I sometimes use AI to make things better”.

The use of AI to formulate questions is not necessarily a problem, according to some experts. “If MPs weren’t using it at all I would see that as a bad thing,” AI developer Maarten Sukel told NOS.

But he said it should not be used as a short-cut for in-depth research. “If you’re working on a dossier that you don’t know so much about and you let AI help you come up with questions to ask in parliament, that’s a problem.”

“Faster and smarter”

MP Daniël van den Berg, of the right-wing opposition party JA21, said: “I think it would be a shame for me to spend hours trawling through minutes and documents looking for media items. AI helps me do it faster and smarter.”

But Marleen Stikker, founder of De Digitale Stad, one of the Netherlands’ first online networks, said using AI in parliament undermined Dutch democracy.

“We are outsourcing our democratic system to the American AI companies’ algorithms, which aren’t even neutral, they’re skewed. That’s absurd, surely?”

World.title: Children in Dutch care system exploited on placements abroad
World.content:
Children in the Dutch care system may be being exploited while on youth placements abroad, an investigation by current affairs programme Nieuwsuur has found.

Councils and child protection agencies can sometimes send children with behavioural problems to other countries, such as Spain, when there is no suitable place for them in the Netherlands. This is supposed to be a temporary solution but some end up staying for up to three years.

The investigation found that the health and youth care inspectorate (IGJ) has been flagging risks in the system since 2009, but parliament was never informed. The inspectorate now says it is receiving reports of children being forced into unpaid work, locked up and not going to school, and admits that nothing has changed.

Because the IGJ has no jurisdiction in foreign countries it cannot investigate reports itself. Some children are also being sent outside the EU, the investigation found, some to Morocco.

Those placed in Morocco have no background in the country, which the organisation running the site, Multi Plus Zorg, said is an advantage because it makes the children more dependent on staff and lets them focus on their own development. Youth law professor Mariëlle Bruning told the programme it “smells of abuse”.

The IGJ said “peer pressure” was being used in some places to keep children under control, and that some were subjected to “outdated” methods focused on punishment.

It also said it has reports of children being physically restrained and barred from leaving the grounds, neither of which is permitted in this type of care, and of some having to do heavy work instead of going to school.

The inspectorate last counted how many Dutch children were in care abroad in 2007, when there were 330.

Youth care minister Mirjam Sterk said she found the situation “worrying”. Parliament passed a motion earlier this year to limit placements abroad as far as possible.

World.title: Croatian couple on run from Slovenia arrested near Dutch border
World.content:
A Croatian couple who went into hiding in the Netherlands after being sought in connection with a murder in Slovenia have been arrested across the border in Germany.

The 31-year-old man and 29-year-old woman were stopped in a car park Isterberg, near the border town of Nordhorn, on Friday evening. They were driving a car with Slovakian numberplates that turned out to have been stolen from another vehicle.

The Telegraaf reported that the couple had been living in the Netherlands prior to their arrest. Police believe they had just crossed the border from the Netherlands because strict checks are in place on the German side.

A check on the couple revealed that prosecutors in Slovenia had issued a European arrest warrant for the couple, who are suspected of beating, strangling and murdering their victim.

They spent Friday night in a police cell in Nordhorn before appearing in court the next morning, where a district judge ordered them to be transferred to prison in Oldenburg prison, where they are expected to face an extradition hearing.

World.title: Three Dutch die in small airplane crash in Germany
World.content:
A small aircraft carrying three Dutch people crashed in Erkelenz, not far from the German border near Roermand. Local police confirmed all three were dead at the scene on Monday morning.

The victims were a 57-year-old man from the Súdwest-Fryslân area of Friesland, and a 58-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman, both from Amsterdam, the foreign affairs ministry told broadcaster NOS. Their names have not been released but next of kin have been notified, the ministry said.

The plane, a four-seat Cessna 172, belonged to Vliegschool Hilversum, a flight school based at the airfield outside Hilversum. Flight tracking data show it took off at 10.25am and disappeared from radar at 11.18am near Erkelenz.

The school released a statement: “With great concern we announce that an accident has occurred in Germany involving one of our aircraft, a Cessna 172. The circumstances of the incident are still unclear.”

The school has halted all its flights while the investigation into the crash is ongoing. The purpose of the flight, and what caused it to crash, has not been made clear.

Dutch aviation safety investigators are joining German authorities to establish what happened, broadcaster NOS reported.

German media reports indicate that the plane may have been on route to Freiburg, and that the pilot had contacted air traffic control due to bad weather before the plane began losing altitude and crashed.

World.title: Polish PM condemns “disgrace” of failed Venezuela oil deal under former government following FT report
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. Prime Minister Donald Tusk says that Poland has been “disgraced in front of the entire world” by a new Financial Times report on how Polish state energy firm Orlen lost $230 million (856 million zloty) trying to buy Venezuelan oil through intermediaries, unsecured payments and cryptocurrency transfers. Tusk called the case a further example of “dirty deals” conducted under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which was in power at the time. Orlen was then led by Daniel Obajtek, who is now a member of the European Parliament representing PiS. Obajtek himself today said that he wants the issue to be clarified in court and suggested that the current authorities are using the case to distract from current soaring fuel prices. How Poland lost $230mn trying to buy Venezuelan oil with crypto https://t.co/Xo07JkYy1t — Financial Times (@FT) September 15, 2026 In a report today, the FT provided new details on a case that has already drawn public attention in Poland. In April 2024, Orlen revealed that its Swiss oil trading subsidiary had lost around $400 million in prepayments for Venezuelan oil and petroleum products that were never delivered. Orlen, which was under new management after Obajtek had been fired earlier that year following the arrival of Tusk’s government, said that the losses included around $240 million paid to a Dubai-based intermediary run by a 25-year-old from Hong Kong. A week later, Polish prosecutors announced that they had launched an investigation into the case, focusing on Orlen Trading Switzerland (OTS), the subsidiary that oversaw the Venezuela deal. Polish prosecutors have launched an investigation into OTS, @GrupaORLEN's Swiss subsidiary which had lost $400 million on prepayments for oil that was never delivered. It also announced that the homes of Orlen's former senior management had been searchedhttps://t.co/QQ5QJMsHg4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 1, 2024 The FT detailed how the then head of OTS, a Lebanese-born Polish citizen of Palestinian descent, who can be named only as Samer A. under Polish privacy law, had sought in 2023 to commission the import of Venezuelan oil through intermediaries, who were given a $230 million advance without any security or guarantees. Although the United States, under then-President Joe Biden, had temporarily suspended sanctions on Venezuelan oil, allowing companies such as Orlen to buy it, Venezuela’s state oil company, PDVSA, remained largely cut off from the global financial system. The FT detailed how the intermediaries therefore sought to use cryptocurrency to facilitate the deal. However, although oil tankers leased by Orlen to collect the oil sat waiting (accruing further large costs), the promised oil was not delivered, and Orlen’s advance payments were lost. The issue is now the subject of a criminal investigation in Poland and an ongoing arbitration case with the intermediary in Dubai, Hannon International. Speaking ahead of a meeting of his cabinet on Tuesday, Tusk said that the FT story is a “disgrace in front of the entire world”. He called the Venezuelan oil incident “the biggest scandal, or one of the biggest scandals, in our country’s history”. Turning his aim on the opposition, he said that the case includes “everything that has recently been associated with PiS”, including “dirty deals” and cryptocurrencies. That was a reference to an ongoing investigation into alleged links between a collapsed crypto firm, Zondacrypto, and figures associated with the opposition. Tusk also noted that opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has recently blocked government bills intended to better regulate crypto markets and to levy a windfall tax on fuel firms. “We may be dealing with a network of dirty and highly dangerous dealings,” said the prime minister. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk: Cała Polska dzisiaj to komentuje. The prosecutors also reported today that, last month, they issued indictments against three former senior Orlen and OTS executives for failing to fulfil their duties to oversee the companies’ assets, resulting in losses of $378 million. In a further post, he suggested that Orlen and the authorities are “trying to cover up current issues again, such as the most expensive fuel in history”. In response, Orlen’s press office wrote under one of Obajtek’s posts that they would “help [him] with English”. “The article is about how your team transferred hundreds of millions of dollars to a company owned by a 25-year-old from Dubai. He converted them into cryptocurrencies, which he copied onto USB drives. And then he handed them out in restaurants to people posing as oil traders…In this story, only Orlen’s money, which they lost, was real.” Panie Pośle, pomożemy z angielskim. He went from being the mayor of Pcim, a rural commune of 11,000 people in southern Poland, to the CEO of Orlen, Poland’s biggest company, in the space of three years. Under Obajtek’s leadership, Orlen expanded rapidly, swallowing up other state energy firms and expanding into new areas of activity. By 2023, it was ranked among Europe’s 50 biggest companies. However, Obajtek was also accused of using the company’s considerable resources to support PiS politically, including through Orlen’s purchases of hundreds of local media outlets – many of whose editors were replaced with PiS-friendly figures – and lowering fuel prices ahead of the 2023 elections. World.title: “Don’t be a creep”: Polish ice cream company launches campaign against sexual harassment of staff
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Polish ice cream chain has launched a campaign to stamp out sexual harassment of staff by customers, including empowering employees to refuse to serve such clients. The campaign is based around the fact that the Polish word for ice cream, “lody”, also has an informal vulgar meaning, referring to oral sex. The company, Good Lood, which runs 37 outlets, says that its female staff regularly suffer lewd comments from male customers incorporating this double entendre. In response, in late August it launched a campaign titled “Nie bądź oblechem”, meaning “Don’t be a creep”, with information displayed prominently at its ice cream stands and on its social media platforms. The firm said it condemned “crude remarks, inappropriate jokes and verbal harassment directed at service workers” and promised to support its staff in dealing with them. “Everyone deserves respect, without exception!” Good Lood advised employees to respond to inappropriate comments with a short, firm retort such as “Great, that’s the 20th time I’ve heard that” or “Perhaps you could repeat that more loudly, so the rest of the queue can hear?” It also called on other customers to react if they witnessed such behaviour. In a follow-up social media post last week, the company confirmed that staff had its backing if they decided not to serve a customer. “If someone is a creep and makes inappropriate comments and verbally harasses them, our team have the right to refuse them service.” That post alone has so far garnered more than 50,000 likes or other positive responses on Facebook. Good Lood says that its messages posted as part of the campaign have already received over 10 million organic views on social media. Comments on the company’s posts show overwhelming support, with many commenters sharing their own experiences. “At last someone has spoken out about this!” wrote one, who said she worked in an ice cream parlour as a teenager. “I remember how outraged I felt when I heard comments like that from men who could have been my fathers, or even my grandfathers. I wonder what would happen if someone spoke to their daughters or granddaughters like that.” Good Lood says it want to start a broader conversation on the “global issue” of harassment and disrespect towards front-line staff in retail and hospitality. “Working in service or hospitality does not mean consenting to disrespect. The safety and wellbeing of our team will always come before profit. We are not afraid to lose a customer who cannot show basic human respect,” the company said in a press release. Founded 10 years ago in Kraków, Good Lood now has 37 outlets there as well as in the Warsaw area. It also sells its products throughout Poland at Biedronka, the country’s largest supermarket chain. The ministry says the content is based on its official security handbook, which it sent to all 17 million Polish households earlier this year, and is intended to help people prepare for emergencies before they occur. “We only find out whether we’re prepared for difficult situations when they actually arise,” said Mateusz Jarecki, who is presenting the segments. “That’s why, in collaboration with specialists, we’ve produced a series of short, easy-to-follow videos that will help you prepare for various life scenarios.” The government is sending copies of a booklet advising how to prepare for and act in emergencies to all 17 million households in Poland. A moose wandered onto the tracks at Warsaw Central Station on Sunday evening, disrupting rail services in the Polish capital for more than 80 minutes before it was safely removed. The animal first appeared on a platform before moving onto the tracks, forcing Polish Railway Lines (PLK), the company responsible for Poland’s rail infrastructure, to suspend, cancel and divert several train services. View this post on Instagram A post shared by TVP3 Warszawa (@tvp3warszawa) Videos and photographs shared online showed the moose lying on the tracks and running along the railway line at Warsaw Central, the capital’s busiest station, which is mainly underground and therefore not easy for such a large animal to access. Police do not know how the moose ended up at the station, reports broadcaster TVN24. Officers were first alerted at 7:10 pm on Sunday and cordoned off the platform where the animal was located. When emergency services arrived, the moose was tranquilised. It was then placed on a large sheet and carried out of the station by police officers and emergency workers before being loaded onto a specialist vehicle to be returned to a forested area. PLK, which named the moose Emil, later confirmed that the animal had been safely removed and that normal train services were being restored. The company added that the disruptions lasted just over 80 minutes, using a pun combining the Polish words for moose (łoś) and 80 (osiemdziesiąt) to produce the word “łosiemdziesiąt”. ❗Aktualizacja❗Zwierze zostało bezpiecznie zabrane z torów. Przywracana jest rozkładowa organizacja ruchu pociągów. Utrudnienia trwały przeszło łosiemdziesiąt minut. https://t.co/Xui2B6SxyU — PLK SA (@PKP_PLK_SA) September 13, 2026 The Eurasian moose (also known as the Eurasian elk) has long been native to Poland, but by the mid-20th century hunting and habitat loss had brought the species close to extinction in the country. Its population subsequently recovered, reaching an estimated 6,000 animals by the 1980s and around 30,000 by 2019, helped by a moratorium on moose hunting introduced in 2001. Several hundred live in the Kampinos national park on the northwestern outskirts of Warsaw. They are therefore relatively frequent visitors to the capital, according to the Interia news website, although venturing onto train lines in the centre is unusual. The growth in the moose population, combined with urban expansion and changes to its habitat, has led to other high-profile encounters in areas inhabited by humans. In 2022, a moose was spotted on the roof of a shopping centre in the northern Polish city of Elbląg. A moose was this morning spotted on the roof of a shopping centre in Poland. World.title: Poland issued EU’s third most residence permits to immigrants in 2025
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland issued first residence permits to almost half a million immigrants in 2025, which was the third-highest figure in the European Union, behind Spain and Germany but ahead of Italy and France. However, the number of permits issued by Poland fell for the fourth year running, as the country continued to tighten its migration rules. Previously, between 2017 and 2022, Poland had led the EU figures for six years running, reaching a peak of almost one million permits in 2021. The new data, released on Friday by Eurostat, the EU’s statistical agency, show that Poland issued 467,314 first residence permits to immigrants from outside the EU in 2025. As was the case last year, Spain (635,438) issued the most, followed by Germany (605,292). Poland was then followed by Italy (433,099) and France (377,462). However, whereas in those four other countries the number of permits rose in 2025 (by 13.1% in Spain, 11.1% in Germany, 25.0% in Italy and 9.2% in France), in Poland the figure fell by 4.4%. That decline has come amid a tougher new migration strategy by the current government, a coalition that ranges from left to centre right, led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Ahead of elections in 2023, Tusk, then in opposition, accused the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which had ruled Poland since 2015, of allowing “uncontrolled” migration, including through widespread abuses of the visa system. Shortly after coming to power in those elections, Tusk, a former president of the European Council, declared that the “survival of Western civilisation” depends upon preventing mass migration. His government has since introduced tougher entry requirements for foreign workers and students, suspended asylum rights for migrants who irregularly cross the border from Belarus, and stepped up deportations of immigrants who have committed crimes or entered the country unlawfully. Poland has introduced tougher new rules regulating the entry of foreign students and immigrant workers. “This is another step towards regaining control over migration and increasing the safety of Poles," says the government https://t.co/gYdikpc6pL — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 2, 2025 The new 2025 data show that, in relative terms (the number of permits issued in relation to countries’ populations), Poland was only ninth in the EU (12.8 permits per 1,000 people), behind Malta (56.9), Cyprus (46.7), Portugal (27.3), Lithuania (18.5), Ireland (13.4), Croatia (13.2), Luxembourg (13.1) and Spain (12.9). That marks a significant decline since 2021, when Poland issued 967,345 permits, which was the highest in the EU in absolute terms but also second-highest in relation to population. In 2025, as in previous years, Poland issued the most first residence permits to Ukrainians (241,126, 51.6% of the total), who are by far the country’s largest immigrant group. They were followed by Belarusians (128,468, 27.5%), Georgians (10,249, 2.2%), Indians (9,230, 2%) and Turks (7,533, 1.6%) – the same top five nationalities as in 2024. Indians are now the third-largest group of foreign workers in Poland, followed by Colombians, according to new data from the country’s Social Insurance Institute (ZUS). Ukrainians remain by far the largest immigrant group, followed by Belarusians https://t.co/hNiOqmeUfX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 11, 2026 Following a decade of unprecedented mass migration, the number of foreigners with residence permits in Poland this year passed two million for the first time, making up just over 5% of the country’s population. Around 1.5 million of those are Ukrainians. In June, the number of foreigners working in Poland reached 1.14 million, making up almost 7% of the workforce. While Ukrainians constitute two thirds of the total, the fastest-growing nationalities are Colombians and Indians, who are now the third- and fourth-largest groups of foreign workers. The rise in migration has come as Poland’s economy has boomed but the country has also faced a demographic crisis, with a shrinking, ageing population and one of the lowest birth rates in the world. In 2023, the state Social Insurance Institution (ZUS) calculated that, in order to maintain its ratio of working-age population to retirees, Poland would need to attract almost two million immigrant workers over the following decade. However, it admitted that that target was “unrealistic”. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has warned that the Central European Visegrád Group (V4) would seek to block any European Union climate policies that push up energy prices. Speaking after a meeting with the leaders of the other V4 countries, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic, Tusk said that they could not accept policies that further weakened competitiveness at a time when they were already facing high electricity costs. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Bratysława ⤵️ Polska i grupa #V4 nie pozwoli na żadne zmiany i na żadne propozycje instytucji europejskich, czy innych państw, które mogłyby wpłynąć na pogorszenie sytuacji energetycznej w naszych państwach. Ceny energii w tym regionie muszą spaść. pic.twitter.com/BFnRx8Clse — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) September 10, 2026 In recent months, Poland and some other member states have been pushing for a softening of the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS), a cap-and-trade scheme launched in 2005 that makes polluters pay for carbon emissions in sectors such as power generation and heavy industry. They have also secured a postponement of the introduction of ETS2, which will cover emissions from road transport and buildings. “Whether we are talking about ETS1, ETS2, or other proposals, anything that brings a risk of more expensive energy for us will be blocked by us,” said Tusk on Thursday at a press conference alongside the other V4 prime ministers, as well as Ireland’s Micheál Martin. “Poland and the V4 will not allow any changes or any proposals from European institutions or other countries that could worsen the energy situation in our countries,” he added. “Energy prices in this region, including in Poland, must fall.” Poland has recorded the EU's third-fastest rise in household electricity prices this year. The country now also has the bloc’s second-most-expensive electricity, when taking cost of living into account https://t.co/WNLdCfOP16 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 30, 2025 Tusk argued that high energy prices pose a threat not only to Central European economies but also to the competitiveness of the EU as a whole. “We can forget about any dreams of competing with China or the United States if our energy prices remain as they are right now,” warned Tusk. Slovakian Prime Minister Robert Fico likewise said the V4 countries were united in their approach to the emissions trading system. “We will be very active, and we will also engage in discussions outside the meetings of the European Council and the Council of Europe to discuss what steps to take to bring down these energy prices,” he said. Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš also expressed frustration with rising energy costs. “All of us in our industrial region pay a lot of money for emissions allowances. And what did the commission tell us in 2020? That the price of this allowance in 2030 will be €26.50. Right now, it’s €80,” he said. According to the Eurostat data, households in Poland paid €27.09 per 100 kilowatt-hours (kWh), including taxes and levies, for electricity in the second half of 2025. That was the 11th highest figure in the EU and below the figure of €28.96 across the bloc as a whole. However, when adjusted for purchasing power standards (PPS), which account for differences in costs of living, Polish households faced the second-highest electricity prices in the EU, at 37.15 PPS per 100 kWh, behind only Romania (49.52 PPS) and the Czech Republic (39.16 PPS). The effects of ETS on electricity bills has moved to the centre of political debate this year after the main opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), called for Poland to unilaterally withdraw from the system, saying it makes “Poles a cash machine for the EU’s absurd leftist climate policy”. The opposition-aligned conservative president, Karol Nawrocki, has also twice sought to call national referendums on rejecting EU climate policies, including ETS, arguing they are too expensive. Both his efforts were rejected by the government’s majority in parliament. While the government has rejected the idea of withdrawing from ETS – which it says would result in large, ongoing fines being levied against Poland – it has pushed for reforms to the system. In July, the European Commission outlined proposals to soften ETS in response to pressure from countries such as Poland, allowing industries to continue emitting CO2 for longer while providing more financial support for investment in clean technologies. Yet there are also a number of other EU member states that argue against weakening ETS, saying it would penalise those who moved early to cut emissions. Poland's right-wing opposition wants to withdraw from the EU Emissions Trading System, saying it makes Poles "a cash machine for absurd leftist climate policies"@PStrzalkowski explains what costs ETS really brings, and what prospects there are for reform https://t.co/UxpMWpG1pE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 4, 2026 Just before the European Commission unveiled its proposal in July, Poland’s climate minister, Paulina Hennig-Kloska, said she had assembled a coalition of 10 countries calling for ETS reform and a more realistic emissions-reduction path. They also want ETS funding mechanisms to account for national differences, including energy mixes and GDP per capita, to ensure a fairer transition for lower-income countries starting from a more challenging position. Poland, for example, has a historical reliance on coal, which it still uses to produce around half of its electricity, helping make it one of the EU’s biggest emitters. Renewables generated 29.4% of Poland's electricity in 2025, almost exactly the same figure as in 2024, ending a period of strong growth since 2021. Coal (52.2%) remained the dominant source, though its share declined. For more, read our full report: https://t.co/XjD9hfhabo pic.twitter.com/WklP7dYL78 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 2, 2026 However, the country has made significant progress in expanding renewables in recent years, particularly solar and onshore wind. In 2025, renewables accounted for just over 29% of Poland’s electricity generation, almost three times the share recorded a decade earlier. Further progress is expected this year, after Poland began to generate electricity from offshore wind farms for the first time. Under a national energy and climate plan approved by the current government in June, it plans by 2040 for Poland to generate 18-21% of power from offshore wind and 22-27% from onshore wind. A further 15-16% will come from nuclear, 14-18% from solar, 7-8% from gas and 0-5% from coal. Poland’s first offshore wind farm has begun to deliver electricity, with Prime Minister @donaldtusk celebrating the development as a "key element of our energy security and sovereignty". The government wants 20% of power to come from offshore wind by 2040 https://t.co/EodvInFmrn — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 10, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish far-right leader Braun vandalises Ukrainian monument with hammer
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun has published a video of himself using a hammer to attack a monument in Poland dedicated to soldiers from the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), a World War Two partisan formation that fought against the Soviet Union but was also responsible for massacring Poles. Braun declared that the monument, which was also recently vandalised by other unknown perpetrators, should be removed as it “insults the memory of victims of the Ukrainian genocide against Poles” and “glorifies Nazism”. The incident comes amid recent tensions between Warsaw and Kyiv over World War Two history, and in particular the fact that the UPA continues to be honoured in Ukraine. Pomnik UPA w gminie Dołhobyczów w powiecie hrubieszowskim do likwidacji❗️ Obelisk obrażający pamięć ofiar ukraińskiego Ludobójstwa na Polakach powinien zostać usunięty profesjonalnymi narzędziami natychmiast po udokumentowaniu przestępstwa banderyzmu!#StopBanderyzacjiPolski… pic.twitter.com/8Q4QZ2z5vJ — Grzegorz Braun (@GrzegorzBraun_) September 10, 2026 The monument in question is located in the village of Liski, a few kilometres from the border with Ukraine, and marks the burial site of 41 UPA soldiers killed while fighting against the NKVD, the Soviet secret police, in 1946, in the aftermath of World War Two. The area previously had a large ethnic-Ukrainian population. The memorial was vandalised last month, when it was sprayed with black paint and its arch was damaged. On Monday this week, further damage was discovered to the inscription on the monument. Police announced that they had launched an investigation into vandalism, property damage and ethnic hatred, but had not yet identified the perpetrators, reported the Polish Press Agency (PAP). On Wednesday evening, Braun published a video showing himself and another man using a hammer to repeatedly strike the front of the monument, causing visible damage to the stone, which contains the names of the killed UPA soldiers. They also appear to attempt to remove a separate plaque. During the video, Braun, who is a member of the European Parliament and finished fourth in last year’s Polish presidential election, claimed that local residents are “afraid they would be set on fire” if they attempted to remove the memorial themselves. It is not clear when the video was recorded. Shortly after Braun published it, local police in Hrubieszów county, where the monument is located, issued a statement saying that officers were investigating damage to the monument. Interior ministry spokeswoman Karolina Gałecka shared their statement and declared that “the perpetrators will not go unpunished”. Sprawcy zniszczenia pomnika w Białymstoku nie pozostaną bezkarni. Policjanci zabezpieczają dowody i przesłuchują świadków. https://t.co/7HCApuhPZ1 — Karolina Gałecka (@K_Galecka) September 10, 2026 Braun, who regularly carries out stunts intended to demonstrate his anti-Ukrainian, antisemitic and anti-LGBT views, and is already facing multiple legal cases over such incidents. He is currently on trial for attacking a celebration of the Jewish festival of Hanukkah in parliament using a fire extinguisher. Last month, he was charged with the crime of denying Nazi crimes for claiming that the gas chambers at Auschwitz are “fake”. He was also charged with theft over incidents in which he tore down Ukrainian and European Union flags, and with vandalism of an LGBT+ exhibition. If convicted, some of the crimes Braun is charged with carry potential years-long prison sentences. Braun’s Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) party, which recently called for a “normalisation of relations with Russia”, enjoys support of around 8-9%, according to polling averages. That could make it a key player in deciding who can form a government after next year’s parliamentary elections. Figures from Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun's party celebrated Russia Day at the Russian embassy and presented a letter hailing Russia's development, blaming "globalists" for the Ukraine war and calling for normalisation of Polish-Russian relations https://t.co/SU3gEdVod0 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 13, 2026 At the time of writing, there had been no response from Ukrainian authorities to Braun’s latest stunt. However, when the same monument was vandalised last month, the Ukrainian embassy in Warsaw issued a statement expressing its “deep indignation”. “Regardless of the difficult and tragic chapters of our shared history, burial and memorial sites should remain outside the realm of political disputes and be treated with respect,” they wrote. The embassy also expressed “particular concern that this incident occurs against the backdrop of a rising number of hostile acts toward Ukrainians in Poland, including reports of aggression and attacks on Ukrainian citizens” “Any attempts to shift historical disputes into the realm of vandalism, intimidation or hostility toward modern Ukraine and Ukrainians are dangerous and must be met with an appropriate legal response,” they added. Poland and Ukraine have been embroiled in a diplomatic dispute since May, when President Volodymyr Zelensky named a military unit after the “heroes of the UPA”. His Polish counterpart, Karol Nawrocki, responded by stripping Zelensky of Poland’s highest honour. Tensions have since cooled, and Ukraine has made moves to defuse the crisis. However, significant differences remain, in particular over memory of the so-called Volhynia massacres, in which the UPA led the killing of around 100,000 Polish civilians. Poland regards the episode as a genocide. Ukraine strongly rejects that label, and also continues to honour the UPA for its role in fighting against Moscow-imposed Soviet rule. Recent months have also seen a rise in anti-Ukrainian sentiment in Poland, including a series of cases of verbal or physical attacks against Ukrainians, who are by far Poland’s largest immigrant group. Reported anti-Ukrainian hate crimes were up 30% in the first half of this year. Demonstrations took place in 25 Polish cities on Sunday against the “growing wave of hate and violence” against Ukrainians, who are Poland’s largest immigrant group. Reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland are up 30% this year https://t.co/gGAEc6QZWT — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 10, 2026 In 2017, Ukraine responded to the dismantling of a UPA monument in Poland by introducing a ban on exhumations of Polish victims of the Volhynia massacres on its territory. It is believed that tens of thousands still remain buried in unmarked mass graves. However, last year, in a diplomatic breakthrough, Kyiv allowed such exhumations to resume, and since then the remains of dozens of victims have been found, researched and reburied. Earlier this month, Poland also granted Ukraine permission to conduct a search for the remains of Ukrainian civilians killed by Polish resistance fighters during World War Two.
