World.title: adidas and HNS Unveil New Croatia National Team Kits
World.content:
adidas has unveiled the long-awaited new official kits for the Croatia national football team, the first set produced under a long-term partnership with the Croatian Football Federation (HNS).

Combining cutting-edge performance innovation with elements founded in Croatian culture and identity, the new kits celebrate the heritage, pride and passion that define Croatian football.

The unveiling marks the start of a new chapter for one of international football’s most recognizable national teams. Having cemented its place among the world’s leading footballing nations, Croatia will step out in an adidas kit for the first time as part of the partnership announced earlier this year.

HNS / adidas

The new home shirt offers a modern take on Croatia’s iconic red-and-white checkerboard pattern, one of the most striking visual symbols in international football. For the first time, letters from the Glagolitic alphabet — the oldest known Slavic script and an important symbol of Croatian cultural heritage — have been woven into the checkerboard design, running throughout the pattern to give one of Croatian football’s most recognizable emblems a fresh, contemporary twist. The back of the collar also features the word “HRVATSKA” written in Glagolitic script, further tying the shirt to Croatia’s cultural history.

The away shirt, meanwhile, draws inspiration from Croatia’s long tradition of lace-making, a craft passed down through generations and another significant part of the country’s cultural heritage. An intricate lace-inspired motif runs across the shirt’s navy base, offering a modern interpretation of that tradition. The design is completed by a collar detail bearing the word “HRVATSKA” in typography inspired by cross-stitch embroidery, linking the traditional craft to contemporary football design.

HNS / adidas

“These shirts are much more than innovative football kits and striking design. Working with adidas, we chose a design that perfectly combines local pride with a global perspective. Those are exactly the values Croatia has always stood for, and now a new generation of fans and players will carry them forward,” said Marijan Kustić, president of the Croatian Football Federation.

Both shirts were developed to meet the demands of football at the highest level and feature the latest adidas CLIMACOOL+ technology. Specially developed stretch fabrics and 3D body-mapping technology improve ventilation and breathability, helping players stay dry through high-intensity matches and in hot conditions. Perforated three-stripe panels and strategically placed mesh zones further boost airflow and comfort.

Croatia’s men’s national team will wear the new kits for the first time during the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures.

Alongside the new shirts, adidas is also launching a wider Croatia national team collection that includes shorts, socks, training wear and leisurewear, designed for fans who want to show their connection to the national team both on and off the pitch.

A video unveiling the new kits has been posted on the Instagram profiles of @adidasfootball and the Croatian Football Federation.

The new Croatia national team kits, along with the full HNS x adidas collection, are available to buy from today at the official HNS online store. Pick out your kit, step into a new era of Croatian football, and wear it with pride.

World.title: CRANE Forum 2026: Productivity as a European Priority, Judiciary as the Greatest Obstacle to Investment
World.content:
September the 15th, 2026 – The CRANE Forum 2026 was recently held, which welcomed around 200 guests from the fields of investment to politics, and from economics to financial institution representatives.

As stated, around 200 guests involved with the Croatian economy, entrepreneurs and investors, members of the Government, ambassadors and representatives of international financial institutions, as well as county prefects and mayors, gathered at the Tihočaj estate in the Žumberak – Samobor Hills Nature Park to discuss investment prospects and the frameworks in which they will be implemented.

In Jastrebarsko on the 12th of September 2026, the fourth CRANE Forum, organised by CRANE, the Croatian Association of Investors and Business Angels, was held. The location was the Tihočaj estate in the Žumberak – Samobor Hills Nature Park. Once again this year, the Forum brought together all levels of decision-making on a single investment in one place: 200 guests from the top of the Croatian economy, entrepreneurs and investors, members of the Government, ambassadors and representatives of international financial institutions, as well as county prefects and mayors.

“Since 2008, CRANE has been connecting entrepreneurs and investors and bringing together capital, knowledge and experience with those who make the decisions. For development and new investments, finding an investor is not enough. What is also needed is a state that cooperates and understands the vision, and a local environment that knows how to create the conditions for its implementation. That is why we do not build the Forum as a conference, but as a working meeting at which everyone who decides on a single investment is present,” said Davorin Štetner, President of CRANE.

The key topics of this year’s Forum were the new multiannual financial framework of the European Union after 2027, the tax system as a competitive advantage, the role of local self-government in attracting strategic investments, and investments in healthcare.

Speaking about what Croatia can expect from the EU’s multiannual financial framework after 2027, Nataša Mikuš Žigman, Minister of Regional Development and EU Funds, stressed that the priorities coming from Brussels are focused on security, defence and climate efficiency, but equally on investments in productivity and competitiveness. Croatia, she announced, has already begun preparing a future competitiveness investment programme that will combine public and private funds, with the aim of raising the productivity of the economy. Among the novelties are milder requirements for technical documentation at the application and contracting stage, the possibility for applicants with smaller tax debts not to be excluded from the procedure but to settle them before the decision on the award of support is made, and raising the threshold for the implementation of procurement procedures with simple procurement via the eKohezija platform. In the negotiations on the new multiannual financial framework, Croatia insists that administrative burden relief actually reaches end-users and does not remain only on the Brussels–Member State axis.

On the panel dedicated to the tax system, in which Tomislav Ćorić, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, Davor Baković, President of the Croatian Exporters Association and Chairman of the Management Board of Končar MT d.d., Davor Tremac, Executive Director of Fono, and Domagoj Kamenski, Executive Director of Kamgrad, participated, it was emphasised that the Croatian tax framework in itself is not an obstacle to growth, but in certain segments even represents a competitive advantage, with a corporate income tax rate lower than the average of developed countries and excellent incentives for investment and research and development.

That the tax rate is not decisive is also shown by comparison with the surrounding region: ahead of Croatia on investment attractiveness rankings are the Czech Republic and Slovenia, which have significantly higher corporate income tax rates. The key problem, as Tremac stressed, is distrust in the judiciary, because what is contracted on paper is difficult and slow to enforce before Croatian courts, and this has been pointed out for thirty years without progress. The price of this distrust is measured in capital that does not arrive: when the enforceability of contractual protections is not certain, investors do not abandon the investment, but the jurisdiction, so Croatian companies register their holding companies in Ireland, the Netherlands or Luxembourg, and the tax base moves with them. The conclusion of the panel is therefore that lowering tax rates would not solve a problem that the rates did not create; the greatest contribution to the investment climate would come from judicial reform, i.e. the speed and predictability of resolving commercial disputes.

Speaking about investments in healthcare from the Government’s perspective, Minister of Health Irena Hrstić emphasised that the Government of the Republic of Croatia has invested around €3.4 billion in the healthcare system over the past ten years or so, and that investments continue in line with the policy of balanced regional development – from the new University Hospital Centre Osijek and the project for a new University Hospital Centre for Dalmatia, which the Ministry and the Government have already given the green light, to the hospital in Blato, whose foundation stone will soon be laid and which will be the first “Carbon Zero” hospital in Europe, heated by geothermal energy and financed by European funds. The leading principle is smart investment, with the emphasis that the goal is functional healthcare equally accessible to all parts of Croatia.

A strong diplomatic dimension was given to the Forum by the presentation of new interlocutors of the Croatian business community at the international level: Ronke Amoni Ogunsulire, World Bank Director for Croatia and Slovenia, Her Excellency Anne Toft Sørensen, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Denmark to the Republic of Croatia, and His Excellency Glenn Morrison, Ambassador of Australia to the Republic of Croatia. Their presentation opens new channels of cooperation and a direct link between the domestic business and investment community and partners outside Croatia, which is crucial for attracting investment and strengthening export opportunities. In addition to them, the Forum also gathered other esteemed ambassadors and representatives of international financial institutions, thereby confirming its role as a meeting place of the Croatian economy with international partners.

what is crane?

CRANE – the Croatian Association of Investors and Business Angels is otherwise the oldest Croatian association of investors and business angels, founded in 2008. It connects ambitious entrepreneurs with investors who invest money, knowledge, skills and business contacts in their projects, with the aim that as many innovative companies in the early stage of development as possible grow into successful business stories. CRANE is the national representative of Croatia in the European Business Angels Network (EBAN) and a member of the Global Business Angels Network (GBAN), and in addition to its investment activity systematically advocates a better regulatory and tax framework for entrepreneurs and investors in Croatia and at the level of the European Union. More at www.crane.hr.

World.title: Hybrid Electro-Diesel Train Between Split and Zagreb Now Operational
World.content:
September the 15th, 2026 – The very first hybrid electro-diesel train between Split and Zagreb is now fully operational. Here are all the details.

As of today (September the 15th, 2026) the very first electro-diesel train will enter service on the Split – Zagreb Main Station route. The train departs (as it has today) from Split station at 07:54. Poslovni reports that the new train is adapted to the specific characteristics of the Zagreb–Split line, which is partly electrified and partly non-electrified. It has 150 seats, and passengers have access to free Wi-Fi, power sockets next to the seats, a modern information system, visual and audio announcements, ramps for people with disabilities, and space for bicycles. The train also features self-service machines for buying coffee and other hot drinks, water, soft drinks, sweets and snacks.

The introduction of the new electro-diesel trains for long-distance transport continues the modernisation of the HŽ Passenger Transport fleet, while at the same time reducing energy consumption, noise and greenhouse gas emissions. Experts from the KONČAR Group, in cooperation with numerous Croatian companies, were involved in the development and production of the trains.

As part of this massive project, six electro-diesel trains are being procured, financed by a loan from the European Investment Bank amounting to 57.3 million euros. All six trains will be put into service by the end of this year. As of December 2026, with the start of the new timetable, Zagreb and Split will be connected by four daily trains, further improving the connectivity of Croatia’s two largest cities and the quality of travel.

Ahead of the first regular journey of the new train, statements for the media will be given by State Secretary for Railways Žarko Tušek from the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure, President of the Management Board of HŽ Passenger Transport Željko Ukić, President of the Management Board of KONČAR Gordan Kolak, Split-Dalmatia County Prefect Blaženko Boban, and Deputy Mayor of Split Matea Dorčić. Also present on the journey will be Zadar County Prefect Josip Bilaver and Šibenik-Knin County Prefect Paško Rakić.

World.title: Brač Fire: Residents Without Electricity Told to Follow TV and Radio
World.content:
September the 15th, 2026 – Brač residents worried for their properties and indeed their lives in the recent Milna fire were very clumsily advised to follow the TV and radio – despite having no electricity.

The Early Warning and Crisis Management System (SRUUK) was activated on Saturday evening because of a large fire in the wider Milna area on Brač. Lukrecija Zderic reports for Index that residents in that area received a message on their mobile phones with a link to instructions on how to act, along with advice to follow further announcements on television and radio. At the same time, part of Brač had no electricity, which raised the question of how exactly people without power were supposed to obtain new information about the fire.

On Saturday evening, the fire, driven by strong wind, spread rapidly towards Milna as well as the bays of Duboka and Osibova, where Resort Gava with a large number of tourists is located. More than 200 firefighters were on the ground trying to stop the fire from spreading towards the populated area.

false evacuation and sruuk activation

The red sky above Brač and Milna was visible even from Split, while Index readers filmed the firestorm approaching the settlement. As the situation became increasingly serious, various pieces of information about a possible evacuation began to arrive. Shortly before 23:00, a notice about the evacuation of the population was published on the Facebook page of the Milna Volunteer Fire Department. It stated that the situation was critical and called on citizens to make their private boats available for evacuation needs. The post was deleted about half an hour later, and services on the ground reported that there was no official evacuation.

At 23:28 the SRUUK was activated. Citizens in the endangered area received a warning via SMS or Cell Broadcast about the danger, together with a link to additional information. Clicking the link opens a page of the Ministry of the Interior (MUP), i.e. the Civil Protection Directorate, containing “Instructions for Citizens.” These are general instructions on how to behave during a fire, and below them citizens are directed to follow further announcements via television, radio and links of the Civil Protection Directorate. At that moment Milna was already without electricity. The earlier post about evacuation further confused residents. Some did not know whether they should leave the place, so they prepared for evacuation and went out onto the street by the sea.

The SRUUK activated once again that evening at 00:22, when citizens once more received a link with instructions on how to act in the event of a fire. Why residents in the endangered area without electricity were recommended to follow information via TV and radio remains unknown for now. Because of the approaching fire a partial evacuation of the most endangered parts of Milna and the surrounding area was carried out, while the entire settlement was never evacuated at any point.

a fire warning for a fire on an island was received in split… on the mainland

The Civil Protection Directorate was therefore asked for an explanation as to exactly why citizens in an area affected by a power outage were directed to television and radio, who in such a situation is responsible for delivering key information, and how many times the SRUUK was activated during the fire on Brač. We will publish the answer when we receive it. However, the problem was not only in the content of the messages. Residents we spoke to said that some received the warning around 23:00 and then again after midnight, while others received only the first message. According to their accounts, some residents of Supetar received no warning at all.

At the same time, a warning about a significant fire danger was also received by some citizens who were at that moment in Split and on the island of Hvar, even though they were not on the territory of Brač. We have also requested an answer from the Civil Protection Directorate on this issue.

a heavily criticised system

The SRUUK has previously been criticised for not being activated during crisis situations. The last time this happened was during the large fire near Omiš, in which three people died and five more are still fighting for their lives. The fire left enormous consequences — people were left without homes and jobs, thousands of hectares of forest burned, and the safety of the population remains threatened due to possible landslides.

The non-activation of the system at that time was justified by Split-Dalmatia County Prefect Blaženko Boban with the assessment that sending a warning could cause panic. On Brač the opposite question has arisen: did the unclear communication from the services further contribute to confusion and panic among residents? In the fire that has been burning on Brač for several days, around 4,000 hectares of forest, low vegetation and maquis have totally burned, as have private buildings, cars and one resort. Around 700 people were evacuated and two people were injured. There is still some smouldering on the ground, the fire has not been completely extinguished, and firefighters remain on alert.

Over 200 firefighters on the ground have for days been making superhuman efforts to defend houses and protect residents. For the locals they are heroes who risk their own lives to protect people and property. Yet the question remains how much help they receive in crisis situations from a system that the state paid 8.4 million euros for. The SRUUK was conceived as a tool for timely warning of citizens. On Brač, however, it has been shown that simply sending a message is not the end of its job, the key question is whether citizens can, after that message, actually receive clear, timely and useful information when they need it most.

World.title: Iraq signs Energy Cooperation Agreement’s fourth phase with Siemens
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz oversaw on Tuesday the signing ceremony for the fourth phase of the Energy Cooperation Agreement between the Iraqi Ministry of Electricity and Siemens.

The agreement that marks the progression into phase four of the ongoing long-term energy strategic partnership was signed as part of al-Zaidi’s trip to Europe.

The ongoing partnership aims to modernize Iraq’s power sector, build highly efficient generation capacities, and expand transmission and distribution networks throughout the country.

In August 2025, the Iraqi cabinet adopted the fundamentals of an energy cooperation strategy with Germany-based Siemens Energy.

Siemens has previously been engaged in electricity projects in Iraq, including long-term service contracts for three power plants in 2023 as part of larger energy cooperation efforts. Siemens also signed an agreement to improve Iraq’s electricity infrastructure in the same year.

Iraq relies heavily on natural gas supplies from Iran to generate electrical power and frequently experiences electricity outages. These outages worsen during the summer months when temperatures exceed 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) in different parts of the country.

To address the country’s increasing energy demand, the Iraqi government is collaborating with Siemens to develop new power plants with a total capacity of 14,000 megawatts.

The new power plants are expected to use local fuel and combined cycle technology, increasing production efficiency and lessening reliance on imported fuel.

Iraq’s electricity grid is experiencing a daily shortage of over 35,000 megawatts due to restricted fuel availability for power plants and a reduction in some external supply sources. In early August, output was barely 24,600 megawatts.

Demand in the summer fluctuates between 55,000 and 60,000 megawatts, exacerbating the supply imbalance and causing continued operational issues for the system. Production levels rely on gas supplies from Iran, which stand at around 20 million cubic meters per day.

World.title: Iraq may import LNG from French company
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is exploring new avenues to secure fuel for its power plants, with the Ministry of Electricity seeking to diversify its gas sources.

The endeavor includes a preliminary agreement with a French company to discuss the supply of liquefied natural gas (LNG) and its regasification within the country in the coming phase.

The Electricity Ministry said on Monday that Electricity Minister Ali Saadi Wahib signed a preliminary agreement in Paris with TotalEnergies to supply LNG to power plants in Iraq.

The step comes as Iraq seeks to reduce its reliance on limited gas sources and secure a more stable fuel supply for its power plants, thereby increasing electricity supply hours and providing the Ministry of Electricity with additional options during upcoming negotiations with suppliers.

The agreement establishes a framework for discussions and negotiations regarding the potential delivery of LNG via a floating platform that would dock at Iraqi ports in Basra. The LNG would then be regasified and injected into the Iraqi national grid.

The agreement includes exploring the deployment of a floating platform to receive LNG shipments in Iraq and conduct regasification operations before transporting the fuel via the national gas pipeline network to power plants, according to the operational needs of the Iraqi grid.

The proposed approach seeks to enhance the flexibility of the fuel system, as LNG can serve as an additional source when necessary. This strategy also enables Iraqi authorities to evaluate the quantities, timing, and both commercial and technical terms prior to finalizing a binding agreement.

Under the initial memorandum of understanding, Iraq is continuing negotiations with the French company to finalize details regarding supplies, infrastructure, and regasification mechanisms.

This new endeavor aligns with another initiative focused on supplying LNG to the Khor Al-Zubair port in Basra. Baghdad has entered into an agreement with US-based Excelerate Energy to establish a regasification terminal that will operate independently.

World.title: ITEX IRAQ 2026 signs strategic media partnership with Al Shabab TV
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – ITEX IRAQ 2026 has concluded a strategic media partnership with Al-Shabab TV, establishing an integrated broadcasting and digital coverage framework ahead of the country’s flagship information and communications technology summit.

The bilateral agreement aims to amplify the exhibition’s media reach and deliver comprehensive programming across both local and regional audiences, showcasing Iraq’s accelerating pivot toward modern digital infrastructure and public-sector technological transformation.

Scheduled to convene from September 30 to October 3, 2026, at the Baghdad International Fairgrounds, ITEX IRAQ serves as the nation’s premier convergence point for telecommunications, enterprise IT, FinTech, cybersecurity, and digital governance.

Under the newly inked arrangement, the partnership pairs the multimedia broadcast network of Al-Shabab TV with the executive convening power of ITEX IRAQ 2026, creating an expanded promotional runway for participating multinational tech vendors, domestic startups, technical forums, and public-private initiatives shaping the country’s digital economy.

The expanded media coverage framework will track core milestone events across the four-day expo, including specialized panel sessions on emerging technologies, enterprise cloud modernization, artificial intelligence integration, and high-level regulatory forums.

By broadening multi-platform coverage, both entities seek to spotlight actionable investment opportunities and homegrown technological innovations, connecting institutional decision-makers with a wider demographic of young professionals, tech entrepreneurs, and regional commercial stakeholders.

World.title: Economist warns of demographic time bomb over Iraq youth unemployment
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Prominent Iraqi economic expert Manar Al-Obeidi has warned of an impending demographic crisis facing the nation’s leadership, cautioning that a looming human time bomb could soon see millions of unemployed youth taking to the streets in widespread protests demanding jobs.

In a televised interview with journalist Muna Sami, Al-Obeidi grounded his warning in demographic findings from the Ministry of Planning’s recent nationwide census, which registered Iraq’s population at 47 million people and revealed that nearly half of the country is under the age of 25, while active participants in the workforce account for just 30 percent.

Al-Obeidi emphasized that over the next five to ten years, this massive youth cohort will reach prime working age, creating an unprecedented wave of job seekers that the public sector cannot absorb.

With state payrolls already saturated, federal institutions will have zero fiscal or administrative capacity to offer additional civil service appointments unless the government enacts radical economic restructuring to build productive industrial lines and real production capacities.

Consequently, Al-Obeidi argued, an inability to accommodate these incoming labor cohorts will inevitably trigger widespread social unrest as youth exercise their legitimate right to demand viable livelihoods.

Compounding this looming crisis is a structural paradox within the domestic economy: despite high unemployment figures, private-sector enterprises face chronic talent deficits.

Al-Obeidi observed that nearly every private firm, including his own organization, struggles to recruit qualified local personnel because the traditional public education system fails to equip graduates with modern, market-relevant competencies.

This systemic failure places accountability squarely on the Ministries of Education and Higher Education, whose outputs remain disconnected from private industry demands.

Under standard economic models, every one-percent expansion in a specific sector’s gross domestic product typically generates a two-percent rise in corresponding job opportunities.

However, Al-Obeidi pointed out that in Iraq, economic expansion frequently bypasses domestic labor entirely due to this widening skill deficit. In the booming residential real estate and construction sectors, developers have repeatedly turned to Egyptian, Turkish, and Iranian firms and laborers to fill operational needs, underscoring an acute domestic shortage of skilled technical talent capable of matching the execution standards required by modern infrastructure projects.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets German president in Berlin
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in Berlin on Tuesday to discuss prospects for political, economic, and investment cooperation between the two countries.

Al-Zaidi is expected to hold discussions with representatives of 30 German companies to discuss investment opportunities and economic cooperation between Iraq and Germany, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The corporations participating in the discussion, which will address cooperation and investment partnerships between the two sides, expressed a strong desire to invest in Iraq.

The Iraqi prime minister’s discussions in Berlin will include finalizing several memoranda of understanding in the economic and investment sectors, strengthening the partnership between the two countries.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Germany comes a day after he concluded a trip to the French capital, Paris, where he and President Emmanuel Macron oversaw the signing of six memoranda of understanding covering air defense, military supply, energy supplies, civil aviation, development finance, and youth and innovation support.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Germany is a significant step in the Iraqi government’s efforts to strengthen commercial ties with other nations and multinational enterprises.

The visit aims to attract foreign investment and utilize German expertise and technology to support Iraq’s economic development.

World.title: Iraq PM donates 47 billion dinars to renovate five Baghdad hospitals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Specialized engineering teams have initiated extensive rehabilitation and modernization works across five major public hospitals in Baghdad, financed through personal donations provided by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi, Minister of Health Abdul Hussein Al-Mousawi announced on Tuesday, September 15, 2026.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Al-Mousawi disclosed that the Prime Minister contributed 47 billion Iraqi dinars out of his personal funds to underwrite the long-overdue infrastructure upgrades after engineering assessments confirmed an absolute absence of allocated state budget lines for the capital projects.

The structural renovation campaign spans anchor healthcare institutions across the capital, comprising Baghdad Hospital within the Medical City complex, Al-Kadhimiya Teaching Hospital, Al-Kindi Hospital, Al-Yarmouk Hospital, and Al-Zafraniya Hospital.

In addition to covering the full 47-billion-dinar reconstruction bill, Al-Mousawi revealed that Al-Zaidi personally donated $2 million directly to the Ministry of Health to procure an essential, life-saving pharmaceutical supply that faced severe procurement delays due to funding shortfalls, allowing specialized medical crews to begin immediate rehabilitation works across the designated hospital wards.

Al-Mousawi explained that publicly spotlighting these targeted private contributions serves to cultivate broader philanthropic and civic engagement, urging corporate institutions and private-sector actors to step forward and assist in rebuilding the country’s burdened healthcare architecture.

The health minister highlighted that this collaborative model has already yielded tangible support from the Association of Private Hospitals, which responded by significantly expanding its corporate social responsibility commitments, pledging to conduct 10 specialized surgical procedures free of charge each month, well exceeding the initial civic target of four surgeries.

World.title: Iraqi PM to sign crucial economic deals during trip to Germany
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi will hold important discussions with German officials during his visit to Berlin.

The discussions will include finalizing several agreements and memoranda of understanding in the economic and investment sectors, strengthening the partnership between Iraq and Germany, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Al-Zaidi’s trip to Germany represents a crucial step in the Iraqi government’s efforts to enhance economic relationships with other countries and international businesses.

The visit aims to attract foreign investment and leverage German expertise and technology to foster Iraq’s development.

The talks will focus on collaboration in the energy, industry, infrastructure, transportation, water, and service sectors, as well as strategies to boost the capabilities of the private sector and increase Germany’s engagement in Iraq’s major initiatives.

The expected agreements will create new opportunities for German investments and facilitate the execution of economically viable development projects.

The step aligns with the government’s efforts to diversify its economic resources and lessen reliance on revenue from oil exports.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Germany comes a day after he concluded a trip to the French capital, Paris, where he and President Emmanuel Macron oversaw the signing of six memoranda of understanding covering air defense, military supply, energy supplies, civil aviation, development finance, and youth and innovation support.

World.title: Iraq postpones start of 2026–2027 academic year to October 11
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Education announced on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, the postponement of the official start of the 2026–2027 academic year to Sunday, October 11, pushing back the previously scheduled launch date of September 20.

According to an official statement issued by the Media Office of the Minister of Education and carried by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Minister Abdul Karim Abtan Al-Jubouri issued the directive to grant administrative and teaching cadres the operational bandwidth needed to conclude second-round examination cycles for non-terminating grades and finalize campus preparations nationwide.

The ministerial directive also incorporated seasonal climate considerations, citing prevailing high temperatures across the country as a primary factor behind the delay to ensure student health and classroom safety.

Ministry officials underscored that the additional three-week window will be utilized to wrap up logistical, technical, and administrative arrangements, enabling local directorates across all governorates to complete physical facility upgrades and coordinate school readiness before millions of pupils and students officially resume classes across Iraq.

World.title: Multiple attempts at high-stakes entrance tests, better centres top reform wish list
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A single bad day should not decide a student's future - and a poorly equipped examination centre should not ruin it. These concerns feature in thousands of suggestions received by the high-powered task force set up to overhaul India's examination system.

The panel, led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, has been consulting stakeholders ahead of its next meeting, scheduled after the Brics summit. It will begin examining reform proposals, sources said.

Constituted amid paper leaks, cancelled tests and infrastructure failures, the task force is examining examination security, technology, infrastructure, accessibility, student well-being and testing-agency reforms.

Suggestions invited from citizens until Sept 13 will be compiled into a detailed report. A prominent demand is to give candidates multiple attempts at high-stakes entrance tests.

Manojranjan Nayak, founder-president of Siksha 'O' Anusandhan, a deemed-to-be university, said: "Examination reform must move beyond making a flawed system more efficient. Multiple attempts can reduce the disproportionate cost of one bad day, but they should be combined with secure, accessible and uniformly equipped centres, transparent evaluation and greater weight for sustained learning.

World.title: Bangladesh PM was invited for Brics meet and bilateral visit: Govt
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Govt reiterated Tuesday that it had invited Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman for both Brics and a bilateral visit. In a letter dated July 14, accessed by TOI, PM Narendra Modi had invited Rahman for the

in his capacity as Bimstec chair and said his participation would "greatly enrich the deliberations".

After Rahman's swearing-in as PM, Modi had invited him for a bilateral visit. Dhaka, however, pulled out of talks for finalisation of the visit dates, apparently because of the lack of any firm commitment from India on ex-PM Sheikh Hasina's extradition.

World.title: CBI officer in RG Kar, Hathras cases assigned Disha probe
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Decorated CBI officer Seema Pahuja will supervise the investigation into the Disha Salian case, bringing her expertise in handling sensitive criminal inquiries to this high-profile probe, sources said.

The team is set to record statements of all individuals who attended a gathering earlier that night at the Mumbai home of Rohan Roy, Disha's fiance, prior to her death on June 8, 2020.

A veteran investigator, Pahuja is currently posted as an SP with the special crimes unit at the agency's headquarters in Delhi. She will be assisted by a team comprising investigating officer deputy SP Puran Kumar and others.

Known for her meticulous approach and sharp forensic acumen, she has earned a formidable reputation within the investigative agency.

Her stellar track record in breaking down dense evidence trails earned her the gold medal for 'best investigating officer' in 2021.

Officials who have worked with her said Pahuja has been trusted with complex, sensitive, and emotionally charged cases that capture national attention through her career. Her portfolio features pivotal roles in major investigations, including the 2024 Kolkata RG Kar rape and murder case and the 2020 Hathras case.

World.title: Balakrishnan panel unlikely to propose inclusion of converts in SC list
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A special panel may recommend to the govt that status quo should be maintained on the definition of Scheduled Castes, as laid down by the Presidential (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, and not expanded to bring in Dalit converts to Islam and Christianity.The commission of inquiry, headed by former Chief Justice of India KG Balakrishnan, has been mandated to investigate if status of Scheduled Castes can be extended to persons who have converted to religions other than those eligible for it - popularly known as "Dalit converts to Christianity and Islam".The 1950 Presidential Order states that only persons belonging to Hinduism, Sikhism and Buddhism can be members of Scheduled Castes.The vexed issue has been pending before Supreme Court for over 20 years in which "Dalit converts" have demanded that they be included in the Scheduled Castes' list.Reports of the past commissions - Kaka Kalelkar, Sachar and Rangnath Misra - on the tricky issue, and the stand taken by National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) over the years have provided the background material for research. A 1911 book by a Christian missionary has also been relied upon.While Sachar did not recommend the Scheduled Castes status for religious converts, Misra panel did ask for the Scheduled Castes' list to be made religion-neutral. Its recommendation was apparently not accepted by govt because the panel did not conduct a study to reach its conclusion. Kalelkar commission, sources said, recommended only OBC status, and not Scheduled Castes recognition to Dalit converts.NCSC took a contradictory stand during the UPA govt, even mentioning that 50% cap on reservations should not be disturbed.According to sources, the 1911 book states that Dalits gain social status after conversion - something which seems to lighten the burden of disability which is cited for giving affirmative action benefits to Scheduled Castes. Given the inputs, the commission may recommend that the present arrangement on eligibility for inclusion in Scheduled Castes' list should stay. Besides, there is also a lack of clarity on which of the religious converts were formerly members of Scheduled Castes, sources said.Pending for over two decades, the demand of religious converts to be included in Scheduled Castes' list has become controversial because of its political dimensions. Existing Dalit communities are often found to oppose fresh inclusions in Scheduled Castes' list, arguing that such a move will increase the number of claimants for job and educational reservations.BJP argues that making Scheduled Castes status religion-neutral will encourage religious conversions.

World.title: Why no safety warnings for B787 fleet, US aviation group asks AAIB
World.content:
MUMBAI: The Foundation for Aviation Safety (FAS), a US aviation safety group, has written to Indiaâs Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), questioning why it has not issued interim safety recommendations for the Boeing 787 fleet, despite holding evidence of chronic system failures on the aircraft involved in last yearâs Ahmedabad crash, which killed 260 people.

Over the past year, FAS said it had received more than 100 non-public documents specific to the crashed Air India 171 aircraft (VT-ANB). FAS sent these documents to AAIB via a UK AAIB expert.

âThe documents are vital to reconstructing the operational history of the doomed airplane. These documents explicitly detail chronic, systemic aircraft failures involving the airplaneâs electrical, electronic, and/or flight computer systems,â said Ed Pierson, FAS executive director, in an email to AAIB director general on Aug 29.

âBy actively withholding this information from public announcements, the AAIB is failing its primary objective, the prevention of future accidents through timely, transparent safety manager at Boeingâs Renton 737 factory, raised internal warnings about overworked, error-prone production teams that he says went unheeded.

He later founded FAS, which came into prominence for its work scrutinising Boeingâs manufacturing and safety practices in the aftermath of the 737 MAX crashes, and disclosures.





Most critically, despite being in possession of evidence pointing to chronic and dangerous system failures, AAIB has issued zero interim safety recommendations or warnings to the global aviation community,â it added.

Pierson, a former senior manager at Boeingâs Renton 737 factory, raised internal warnings about overworked, error-prone production teams that he says went unheeded. He later founded FAS, which came into prominence for its work scrutinising Boeingâs manufacturing and safety practices in the aftermath of the 737 MAX crashes, and has since been pressing AAIB on the AI171 investigation.

In an Aug 21 letter, FAS had asked to be formally recognised as a stakeholder in the investigation and for its technical findings to be included in the investigation record. AAIBâs Aug 26 reply confirmed it received the documents via a UK AAIB expert on June 10 and that its investigation team had examined them, adding that the probe followed fair and impartial practices under the relevant regulations. AAIB did not respond to FASâs Aug 28 letter, which alleged the agency was suppressing vital B787 safety information.

AAIB told TOI, âA common update/report will be published by the AAIB.â

A

FAS first outlined the documentsâ contents in a Jan presentation to the US Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. Pierson told TOI the crashed aircraftâs records showed recurring failures in its Electrical Wiring Interconnection System (EWIS).

Itâs the network of all wires, cables and connectors distributing electricity, data and signals through the aircraft.

The 787âs EWIS spans over 150 km of wiring, more than 3,500 connectors and 40,000 cable segments. Aircraft wiring was once treated as a minor component, but after the 1996 TWA B747 and 1998 SwissAir MD-11 crashes killed a combined 529 people, EWIS emerged as a distinct, critical aircraft system on a par with engines or fuel systems.

The FAA formally codified EWIS regulations in 2007.

âWhat I do know is that VT-ANB had plenty of EWIS failures,â Pierson said, citing the non-public documents.

âIt also had primary power distribution failures, not just EWIS, but actual power generation, stable, high-quality electrical power. It had lots of problems with that. It had all those other issues: open circuits, short circuits, burning, arcing, fire, etc.â He said problems could arise from wiring routed too close together, chafing against sharp edges, or improper bonding and grounding, leading to electricity going places itâs not supposed to go.

âYou can have a lot of issues with EWIS. EWIS has been identified as a causal factor in many accidents,â Pierson said.

Among the documents sent to AAIB is one detailing a 2022 incident when VT-ANB, flying into Frankfurt, suffered multi-system failures on both sides of the aircraft. On landing, the P100 primary power panel was found burning, producing â12 pages of aircraft system faultsâ.

World.title: SC junks ex-Delhi mayor's plea for FIR on UP cops
World.content:
NEW DELHI: SC Tuesday refused to entertain former Delhi mayor Farhad Suri's plea for an FIR against UP police for conducting a midnight raid at his city home in search of journalist and Ram temple donation pilferage whistleblower Abhishek Upadhyay.

Suri's counsel, Anoop Awasthi, told SC that a Ghaziabad police team had raided Suri's Nizamuddin East residence on the night of Aug 22 without disclosing warrants and corresponding entries at Nizamuddin police station. He urged the CJI Surya Kant-led bench to lay down guidelines for the police department of a state conducting midnight raids in another state.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

UP additional advocate general Sharan Dev Singh Thakur said Suri's petition was an abuse of the process of law and "unnecessary sensationalisation" as police merely rang the bell to find out whether Upadhyay, who was wanted in a road rage case in Ghaziabad, was available at his place.

They left after Suri denied Upadhyay's presence, Thakur said, adding that Suri could approach senior police officers for registration of an FIR and, if dissatisfied, he could move a trial court with a private complaint against police.

As Suri wanted the FIR to be lodged in Delhi, the bench disposed of his petition by giving him liberty to approach the Nizamuddin police station for filing a complaint against the officers who raided his home unauthorisedly. SC had on Aug 25 protected Upadhyay against arrest by Ghaziabad police. tnn

World.title: Pak raising Azhar bounty a gimmick, says India
World.content:

World.title: U.S. announces visa curbs targeting South Africa foreign nationals for ‘race-based discrimination’
World.content:
Secretary of State Marco ​Rubio said on Tuesday (September 15, 2026) ⁠the U.S. government was announcing a new visa restriction ‌policy targeting some foreign nationals ‌in South Africa.

The policy ‌targets “foreign ⁠nationals who are ⁠responsible for, or complicit in, the enactment or implementation of ​laws or policies ‌that enable uncompensated land seizures, race-based discrimination, and/or the incitement of ‌imminent violence against members ​of minority ethnic or racial groups ⁠in South Africa,” Mr. Rubio said in a statement.

“The ‌South African government has not adequately addressed the previously laid out concerns,” Mr. Rubio said.

Relations between Washington and ‌Pretoria have soured since the ​start of Donald Trump’s second term, ⁠with the U.S. president criticizing ⁠the country for its policies aimed ‌at addressing racial inequality.

World.title: U.S. acknowledgement of orbital arms ignores space conflict consequences: Russia
World.content:
Russia’s Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday (September 16, 2026) the U.S. acknowledgement that Washington had ​deployed orbital weapons ignored the possible consequences of ‌a conflict and threatened long-term stability in ​space-based activity.

“In pursuit of its ⁠narrow self-interests, Washington is ready to completely ignore the catastrophic consequences for humanity of any armed conflict in ‌orbit,” Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said in a commentary on the Ministry ‌website.

Ms. Zakharova said the presence of U.S. ‌weapons ⁠in space risks the prospects for ⁠space exploration.

“Colossal risks are created for numerous socio-economic processes on Earth and people’s well-being directly depends on them,” she ​said.

U.S. Air Force ‌Secretary Troy Meink told a conference near Washington, D.C., on Monday (September 14, 2026) that the United States possessed “on-orbit space control weapons capable ‌of defending the Joint Force against hostile ​adversary action.”

The statement was the strongest admission by a U.S. official of American ⁠weapons in space amid rising space tensions with Russia and China.

Ms. Zakharova described the acknowledgement ‌as part of attempts to “distract world attention from the U.S.’ own aggressive strivings in terms of space,” including “absurd” accusations that Moscow was developing anti-satellite weapons.

“The moratorium on testing ... anti-satellite missiles promoted by the so-called ‘collective West’ is laden ‌with hypocrisy, as in reality it does not affect ​the use of weapons that the U.S. already has and does not ⁠apply to other types of anti-satellite systems that Washington ⁠is seeking to develop,” she said.

Ms. Zakharova said resolutions co-authored by Russia on ‌barring deployment of space-based weapons and transparency in using space would be presented to the ​U.N. General Assembly next month.

World.title: Key allies TDP, Shiv Sena back Amit Shah's statement on UCC in all NDA-ruled States
World.content:
After Home Minister Amit Shah's assertion that a Uniform Civil Code will be implemented in all NDA-ruled States before 2029, key NDA partners TDP and Shiv Sena on Tuesday (September 15, 2026) backed the BJP on the issue.

Another BJP ally JD(U) gave a guarded response, saying it will study the Uniform Civil Code Bill and will "not oppose it for no reason".

The support of the TDP with 16 Lok Sabha MPs, the Shiv Sena with 13 and the JD(U) with 12 is crucial for the Narendra Modi government. While the TDP is in power in Andhra Pradesh along with Jana Sena and BJP, the BJP shares power with the JD(U) in Bihar and the Shiv Sena in Maharashtra.

TDP's Andhra Pradesh president P. Srinivasa Rao said in Amaravati that it is bound by the Union Home Minister's statement on UCC as an NDA partner.

"Yes, I have seen our Union Home Minister's statement on UCC and as NDA partners we are bound to go by his statement," Mr. Rao, who represents Gajuwaka assembly constituency, said.

Though there is criticism over UCC, he noted that it "strengthens the unity of the country and doesn't show much gender bias".

"And critics, of course, some say that it (UCC) infringes on religious freedom. Our country is culturally diverse. But we always think that this UCC will strengthen and unify the country," he said.

"So, we will be going by our home minister's statement being NDA partners," he added.

CPI(M) state secretary V. Srinivas Rao, however, claimed that the BJP is resorting to UCC politics to divert the country's attention as it is "facing heat from the new generation (Gen Z) due to unemployment" and other reasons, especially in the backdrop of the recent Jantar Mantar student protest movement.

Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Chaudhary also said the JD(U) will study the Uniform Civil Code Bill and will "not oppose it for no reason" if provisions are unexceptionable.

The former state JD(U) president made the statement while addressing a press conference at the party office. He was replying to queries about the political turbulence that has ensued after Shah's assertion that UCC will be implemented "across 22 NDA-ruled states by 2029".

On Monday (September 14, 2026), senior JD(U) leader and Phulwari Sharif MLA Shyam Rajak had spoken out strongly against the UCC, claiming that he was expressing a view in line with the stand taken earlier by party supremo Nitish Kumar, who had told the Narendra Modi government at the Centre, "we will support the Bill in Parliament but are opposed to its implementation in Bihar".

Mr. Chaudhary, however, maintained that "there is no reason to make haste in the matter" and pointed out that "our national working president Sanjay Kumar Jha has said that he will hold talks on the issue with none other than the Union home minister".

"As of now, we are not aware of the details of the legislation on UCC. Let it be placed before us. If we find there is nothing objectionable, why shall we oppose it without any reason? And if there are points of concern, these will be conveyed to the Union Home Minister," he said.

Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister and Shiv Sena president Eknath Shinde backed Shah on the UCC issue, saying Sena founder late Bal Thackeray had envisioned the common law for all.

"Hinduhridaysamrat Balasaheb Thackeray's vision was 'one country, one law' with equal justice for all. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has also stated the same position on UCC," Mr. Shinde said.

He added that the Mahayuti government in Maharashtra remains positive about the Uniform Civil Code and will make a definitive decision at an appropriate time.

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Monday (September 14, 2026) said the State government would implement the UCC once the committee preparing the draft bill submitted its report.

Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah said the BJP should introduce the UCC Bill in Parliament if it has the numbers to pass it, instead of pushing it through individual states, and claimed the BJP's allies also have reservations.

"If you have the numbers, bring it to Parliament. Why are you doing it through different states? Anyway, within their own NDA, not everyone agrees with this. According to the news, Janata Dal (United) raised their hands and said this won’t be implemented in Bihar,” Mr. Abdullah told reporters here.

The National Conference leader said the BJP should not bring the UCC “through the backdoor”. "The way their own allies are not in favour of it, I don’t think they will be able to get it passed in Parliament. That is perhaps why they are taking this route,” he added.

All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) president Asaduddin Owaisi said in Bhopal that if the NDA constituent parties such as the JD(U) and TDP have "the slightest disagreement" with the BJP's ideology, they should oppose the Uniform Civil Code.

The UCC was being introduced in various states with the aim of "targeting" India's 18 crore Muslims, and the real objective of the BJP and RSS was to "dismantle" the protections guaranteed (to religious minorities) under Articles 25, 26, and 29 of the Constitution, he alleged.

Owaisi said it would be a different matter if the NDA allies had aligned themselves completely with BJP's ideology. "But if they still have even the slightest difference with the BJP, they should oppose it (UCC)," he said.

World.title: FBI chief Kash Patel defends hiring policy changes on prostitution, bestiality at fiery hearing
World.content:
FBI Director Kash Patel defended on Tuesday (September 16, 2026) a recent policy change to allow some applicants who have engaged in prostitution and bestiality to be considered for employment, insisting that the move was made to enable victims of those acts to apply for a job without fear of automatic disqualification.

The subject arose during a fiery Senate Judiciary Committee hearing in which Mr. Patel clashed with Democrats over his firing of agents who participated in investigations of President Donald Trump and suggested that agents might be dispatched to the polls on Election Day amid Justice Department and White House concerns about voter fraud.

The hours-long hearing featured the name-calling and bitingly personal exchanges that have come to define Mr. Patel's appearances on Capitol Hill, with Democrats characterising the Trump appointee as unqualified, criticising him for politically charged investigations into Mr. Trump's enemies and highlighting travel that has included a trip to the Winter Olympics in Italy in which he partied with U.S. hockey players and a snorkeling excursion at the Pearl Harbor memorial in Hawaii.

“He's an incompetent lackey. He's like an 18-year old-kid who wants to join a fraternity that he could never be a member of, doing keg stands and chugging with friends. He's an embarrassment to the agency and wouldn't qualify even to be an FBI agent,” said an exasperated Sen. Cory Booker of New Jersey, his voice rising in anger.

“What a mockery you are,” he added.

Mr. Patel shot back, “You are the biggest mockery in the United States Senate, and you're sitting next to Schiff.” That was a reference to Sen. Adam Schiff, a California Democrat and outspoken Patel critic.

Patel pressed on the FBI's hiring standards

The FBI quietly issued guidance this past spring lifting a categorical hiring restriction on applicants who had previously participated in prostitution. The bureau made a similar change with regard to childhood experience in bestiality.

Under questioning, Mr. Patel denied that the changes reflected a lowering of employment standards and insisted they were designed to prevent victims who'd been forced to engage in that conduct from being automatically disqualified.

“We did not want to punish victims of bestiality, victims who were trafficked. We did not want to make it an automatic disqualification for the FBI to consider you if you were a victim of these awful, heinous acts,” Mr. Patel said. “We are not going to target victims and prevent them from serving in their capacity to serve this country.” The questioning spanned partisan lines, with Republican Sen. John Kennedy of Louisiana grilling Patel about the rationale for a change that the FBI director said was proposed to him by subordinates.

“When you saw bestiality, I say this with respect: The person who recommended it, why didn't you just say what planet did you parachute in from?” Sen. Kennedy asked.

Mr. Patel conceded that was his initial response, but “they then explained to me and showed me cases in which people were forced into it and applied to the FBI and so I thought they should be considered. It's not an automatic disqualification.”

The Associated Press reported last month that the FBI still intends to bar some applicants who are revealed to have previously engaged in prostitution, including if they've done so within the last 10 years.

Patel did not rule out sending agents to polling places on Election Day

The hearing took place two months before the midterm elections in November and at a time when the FBI has opened investigations related to the 2020 contest, including by seizing voter data in Fulton County, Georgia.

Mr. Trump regularly makes false claims that elections are rigged and riddled with fraud, especially in the months before an election. But there is no widespread fraud in American elections. Local election officials have detailed processes for auditing the accuracy of the vote after ballots are tallied.

Even as he disputed his loss in 2020, audits, reviews and recounts in the battleground states where he challenged the outcome all affirmed Democrat Joe Biden's win.

Those voter fraud claims, and the FBI's efforts to investigate the 2020 race, have spurred Democratic concerns that Patel could plunge the bureau into the upcoming election.

Asked whether the FBI has the general authority to monitor elections, Mr. Patel replied that responsibility rests with the Department of Homeland Security. He said the FBI's presence on Election Day will be “housed” with election crimes coordinators at each of the bureau's 56 field offices, but under questioning, he declined to rule out that agents would be dispatched to the polls in the event of problems or reports of interference.

“Do you pledge that you will not in any way interfere in the will of the American people when they go to the polls in November?” asked Democratic Sen. Peter Welch of Vermont in one of the hearing's more combative exchanges.

“I pledge unequivocally that I will not participate in your charade of lies,” Patel said, later calling Welch a “total fraud.” FBI firings were also a featured topic of the hearing Patel repeatedly touted what he asserted was his record-breaking success at the FBI, proclaiming the “most prolific reduction in crime in U.S. history” even though violent crime rates in American cities had begun dropping well before Mr. Trump took office last year for reasons that are difficult to pinpoint.

Kash Patel: The die-hard loyalist

Democrats seize on the tumult inside the FBI

Even as the Republican-led panel tried through its questioning to keep the focus on Mr. Patel's crime-fighting efforts from his perch at the nation's premier federal law enforcement agency, Democrats seized on the tumult inside the FBI over the last year — including sweeping firings of agents who participated in investigations of Mr. Trump, the bureau's aggressive efforts to investigate media leaks by serving subpoenas at reporters' homes and Patel's travel schedule that has blended private leisure with professional responsibilities.

Democrat Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut pressed Mr. Patel on the firing of national security agents with expertise in Iran shortly before the U.S. launched attacks on the country last February. He noted that the agents had participated in an FBI investigation into Trump over his retention of classified documents at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida.

“Do you think firing the president's political opponents is more important than retaining the decades of experience and expertise monitoring intelligence threats from Iran?” Mr. Blumenthal asked.

“I think what's most important is to not have a weaponized FBI, and I will endeavor every single day to make sure we have no one there that is doing that,” Mr. Patel responded. He did not say why their participation in the Mar-a-Lago investigation represented “weaponized” law enforcement.

Mr. Patel later suggested that the scope of firings had been overblown, saying many agents had retired on their own. And he defended his personal travels by pointing to numbers that he said showed that two recent predecessors, Chris Wray and James Comey, had traveled more.

World.title: Bihar Cabinet approves ₹3,516 crore for Vishnupad Temple area development, Son-Falgu river link
World.content:
The Bihar Cabinet on Tuesday (September 15, 2026) gave its administrative approval for two development projects worth just over ₹3516, including the comprehensive development of the Vishnupad Temple area in Gaya Ji and the construction of the Son-Phalgu river linking scheme.

The Vishnupad Temple area in Gaya Ji will be developed on the lines of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor in Varanasi at an estimated cost of ₹2,520 crore, while the construction of the Son-Phalgu river linking scheme will be completed at an estimated cost of ₹996 crore, Secretariat Department’s Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) Arvind Kumar Chaudhary told reporters.

A total of 17 decisions were taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary.

Talking to reporters in after the Cabinet briefing, Mr. Chaudhary said that the completion of this project will provide new impetus and strength to Gaya’s religious, spiritual, and cultural traditions, which have continued for thousands of years, particularly important religious rituals such as Pind Daan, Tarpan, and Pitru Paksha.

MoU for air connectivity

In another important decision, the Cabinet also approved an MoU between Civil Aviation Ministry, Airports Authority of India (AAI), New Delhi and the State government for expanding air connectivity in the State under regional connectivity scheme, modified UDAN scheme.

As a result of MoU, the roles and responsibilities of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Airports Authority of India, and the state government will be clearly defined. This will facilitate the provision of necessary financial assistance under the UDAN Scheme for new air routes proposed by the state and will also help in continuing operations on routes with low passenger demand during the initial period.

It also gave its nod for the constitution of “Bihar State Civil Aviation Cadre Recruitment Rules 2026” to regulate the recruitment and promotion of technical and non technical posts under Civil Aviation Department, Bihar.

Contractual appointment in govt medical colleges

The Cabinet also gave its nod for recruitment to the post of Assistant Professors on contractual basis in five government medical colleges of the State untill regular appointments are made to these posts, the ACS said, adding that it would make the teaching faculty available in these colleges in line with standards set by National Medical Commission, New Delhi.

The five government medical colleges where contractual teaching appointments will be made includes government medical colleges at Bettiah, Purnea, Chapra (Saran), Jan Nayak Karpoori Thakur Medical College, Madhepura, and Shri Ram Janki Medical College, Samastipur.

Similar contractual appointments of teaching faculty —Professor, Associate Professor and Assistant Professor— will be made in government dental colleges of the State till regular appointments to these colleges are made.

It also dismissed Dr. Ravi Shankar Prasad, General Medical Officer, posted at APHC, Bahadur in Khagaria district, from the service for remaining unauthorisedly absent from the service since November 17, 2021.

₹1,000 crore from BCF for flood protection and other works

The Cabinet also gave its nod for obtaining ₹1,000 crore as an advance from the Bihar Contingency Fund under the Water Resources Department, Mr. Chaudhary said, adding that the amount received will be utilised under the State plan for flood protection works, Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali Abhiyan, and other important works in the irrigation sector.

The State cabinet also approved the ‘Bihar Water Resources Restoration and Silt Management Policy, 2026’, which proposes to facilitate the removal of accumulated silt from water sources, restore the capacity of water structures, and utilise silt from rivers, barrages, reservoirs, etc. for necessary earth filling and construction works in various projects.

World.title: Teen stabbed to death during Ganesh idol procession in Indore
World.content:
A 16-year-old boy was stabbed to death and another minor injured following an altercation during a Ganesh idol procession in Madhya Pradesh’s Indore, police said on Tuesday (September 15, 2026).

According to the police, the incident took place around 9.30 p.m. on Monday (September 14, 2026) in Musakhedi area under Azad Nagar police station limits following an argument between some boys in a Ganesh Chaturthi procession.

Additional DCP (Crime) Rajesh Dandotiya told The Hindu that the deceased has been identified as Krishna Panwar, 16, and his friend Sahil Rathore, 15, has sustained knife injuries.

Mr. Dandotiya said that Mr. Rathore is out of danger now and teams have been formed to nab the accused, all a 16-year-old.

He said that an FIR has been lodged in the matter under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) Sections 103(1), 109(1), 118(2), and 296(b).

As per the FIR, the argument took place when the accused pushed the victims during dancing in the procession which led to an altercation after which he stabbed the two boys with a knife.

Mr. Panwar suffered knife injuries in his chest and taken to MY Hospital where he was declared dead, the FIR said.

World.title: Ex-ABVP convenor, PM-EAC members in NCERT’s new English and Economics textbook committees
World.content:
The National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) has constituted two committees to develop Economics and English textbooks for Classes 11 and 12, whose members include a former national media convenor of the RSS-affiliated Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), as well as members of the Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council.

Earlier, the NCERT had announced a committee to develop Political Science textbooks for the senior secondary classes, with at least four members having direct or indirect links to the RSS.

Right-wing student activist

A notification issued by NCERT on September 8 for the English Language and Literature Textbooks Committee named Saket Bahuguna, Assistant Professor (Linguistics) at the Central Institute of Hindi, Delhi, as one of the panel’s 17 members. Mr. Bahuguna is a right-wing student activist who rose to prominence through university politics in New Delhi.

Originally from Uttarakhand, he completed his graduation and post-graduation at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) and later pursued research in Linguistics at Delhi University (DU). He became an active student leader, rising to become the Delhi State secretary and subsequently the national media convener of the ABVP.

He was one of the central figures and vocal faces of the ABVP during the February 2016 JNU protests. He clashed with left-wing student groups over the organisation of an event on campus regarding Parliament attack convict Afzal Guru, positioning himself as a voice against “anti-national” activities.

Ideological policing

Throughout his tenure as a chief spokesperson for the ABVP, he faced continuous friction and allegations from political opponents regarding high-handedness and ideological policing during student union elections and seminars across the DU and JNU campus networks.

The textbook committee also includes Trivikrama Kumari Jamwal, former Head of English at The Shri Ram School Aravali, Gurugram. She is also a member of the erstwhile Mewar royal family. In 2017, her brother wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on behalf of the family, urging the government to withhold the certification and release of Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s Padmavati, citing “misrepresentation of heritage”.

The 17-member team will be headed by N. Nagaraju, Vice-Chancellor of the English and Foreign Languages University, Hyderabad.

Incorporating Indian knowledge systems

NCERT also named Sanjeev Sanyal, a member of the Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council (PM-EAC), as the head of the 14-member committee for Economics textbooks. PM-EAC member Shamika Ravi is also part of the committee.

“The textbooks will subsequently undergo a review to ensure the integration of themes such as cultural rootedness, Indian knowledge systems, inclusion, educational technology and assessment,” said the NCERT notification.

The committees have been instructed to ensure the new textbooks incorporate cross-cutting themes prescribed by other NCERT Curriculum Area Groups, including equity and inclusion, age-appropriate pedagogy, value education, information and communications technology (ICT), Indian knowledge systems, and environmental education.

The English textbook committee is expected to finish its work for Class 11 by November 30, 2026 and for Class 12 by September 30, 2027, NCERT director Dinesh Saklani said in the notification. The draft manuscript will then be reviewed by NCERT. The Economics textbook committee is expected to complete its work by February 28, 2027 next year.

World.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy says Russian drones attacked Moldova twice while he was in transit
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said in an interview broadcast on Tuesday (September 15, 2026) that ​Russian drones attacked Moldovan airspace twice while he was ‌in the country aboard his aircraft in ​transit.

Mr. Zelenskyy told the U.S. television ⁠network CBS that he was in Moldova on Ukraine’s western border, at Chisinau airport, on his way to ‌and from a trip abroad when the incidents occurred.

“In Moldova, my ‌presidential jet was there and that’s ‌why they ⁠attacked Moldova, the airspace of Moldova. ⁠Maybe they didn’t want to attack me personally...,” Mr. Zelenskyy said. “When we came back home, again through Chisinau, again ​they did the same.”

On ‌September 9, a Moldovan government spokesperson said the departure of Mr. Zelenskyy’s aircraft for Norway was delayed as Moldovan authorities closed the country’s ‌airspace over a drone alert.

Two Russian drones ​entered Moldovan airspace on that day. One landed in a field north ⁠of the capital, triggering a fire, while the second carried on into Romanian airspace.

Mr. Zelenskyy had ‌not previously spoken of the second incident. It was not clear exactly when the President was again in transit in Moldova on his way back to Ukraine from Canada.

Moldovan authorities said two drones entered the ‌country’s airspace on Monday (September 14, 2026) for about 10 ​minutes each over the space of an hour before noon local time.

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs4.10 per litre, HSD by Rs6.41 per litre
World.content:
The government on Tuesday increased the price of petrol by Rs4.10 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs6.41 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs384.34 per litre while HSD will cost Rs415.83 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 16 (Wednesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

A statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said owners of two- and three-wheelers would receive relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles up to 800cc would receive the same relief on a monthly quota of 30 litres.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Pims fire: Inquiry committee finds 'systemic, institutional failure' behind tragedy
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An inquiry committee formed to probe the deadly fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) has found “systemic and institutional failure” and determined that an electrical failure was the most likely cause of the blaze, it emerged on Tuesday.

The August 26 fire at a nursery in Pims’ Mother and Child Hospital claimed the lives of 14 newborns. The incident raised concerns over fire safety measures and sparked calls for accountability, with criminal action being ordered against eight officials.

Headed by former interior secretary Shahid Khan, the committee was formed on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s directives on the day the fire occurred. It has presented its findings and recommendations in a 43-page report available with Dawn.

The committee concluded that “ systemic and institutional failure is established , while individual responsibility varies with the strength of the evidence”.

It added that Pims and its “senior management bear the principal institutional responsibility for failing to convert known risks, prior warnings and assigned duties into an effective safety system”.

“Administrative, disciplinary, contractual and criminal responsibility must attach only where the relevant duty, omission and causal consequence are proved,” the report said.

“The electrical spark explains how the fire began; the institutional system explains why it became a catastrophe.

“Fourteen newborns were lost not because one safeguard failed, but because too many safeguards were absent, weak, delayed or never verified to be working ,” the report declared.

It explained: “The causal chain is coherent. A localised electrical failure most probably started the fire; combustible and oxygen-supported conditions accelerated it; inadequate detection and protection failed to contain it; overcrowding, limited evacuation capacity and the absence of a rehearsed neonatal emergency system constrained rescue; delayed institutional activation weakened response; and longstanding governance, maintenance and regulatory failures allowed these vulnerabilities to coexist.”

The report pointed out a “history of known but incompletely closed risks”, citing prior warnings.

These included earlier correspondence by the Capital Development Authority (CDA), the Federal Ombudsman’s 2015 findings, Pims’ own 2025 acknowledgement of ageing fire safety infrastructure, and especially the July 6, 2026 Nursing Hostel fire, which had already highlighted deficiencies in detection, alarms, electrical inspection, evacuation, firefighting equipment, drills and emergency planning.

“Yet those warnings had not been converted into a comprehensive, time-bound and independently verified corrective programme before the Nursery fire,” the report regretted.

“The specific AC 2 defect may not have been foreseeable; the need for stronger fire preparedness plainly was,” it said, referring to the likely fault in the connected electric cable.

“The strongest technical evidence, from the National Forensics Agency, identifies the АС Unit No. 2 electrical supply cable near/over AC Unit No. 1 as the most probable point of ignition,” the report said about the cause of the fire.

It explained that abnormal localised electrical heating — possibly from excessive current, a high-resistance connection or another localised defect — most probably caused insulation failure and ignition of nearby combustible material.

The evidence does not establish arson, multiple ignition points, an external fault of the Islamabad Electric Supply Company (Iesco), a pre-fire oxygen leak, or an incubator or warmer as the source, the committee determined.
